narrative: Today 06/16/21 at 8:45 am, Licensing Program Analysts (LPAs) Belinda Gilmer conducted an unannounced required annual at this Short Term Therapeutic Residential Treatment (STRTP) facility. LPA met with Carlos Garces Administrator/Executive Director/Facility Manager. LPA toured the facility with Mr. Garces both inside and outside. This facility has five (5) bedrooms, three (3) bedrooms. There are no changes to the floor plan that was originally submitted to Community Care Licensing. The passageways and entries were unobstructed, at the time of this inspection. There was no swimming pool or body of water on the premises. The disinfectants, cleaning solutions, and other hazardous items were locked and inaccessible to the children. LPA observed a letter from the Joint Commission date 6/14/21, stating the accreditation survey has been postponed due to the COVID 19 pandemic and Bright Horizon will be considered accredited beyond their current certificate expiration date of 5/28/21. Mr. Garces stated there are no firearms/dangerous weapons at this group home. The facility has required non-perishable foods for one (1) week and perishable foods for two (2) days. The facility provides meals, nourishment, or snacks. Medications are locked in the staff office in a locked file cabinet and accessible only to employees. The temperature in the rooms that clients occupy is maintained at a comfortable temperature for the children. Hot water temperature in the three bathrooms was at 106.5 degrees Mr. Garces ensures that children are accorded dignity in personal relationships with staff and others. Children live in a safe, healthy, comfortable facility and are treated with respect. LPA observed the children's rights, children's group home Ombudsman flyer, visitation rules and policy, emergency disaster plan, and foster youth bill of rights were posted. The complaint and grievance procedures posted. There is a phone available for the children to use. The Administrator is required to be on-site at least 20 hours per week (Monday thru Friday at 7:00 am-noon. Mr. Garces ensures appropriate staff/client coverage/ratios for all required positions. The Personal Report (LIC500) dated 06/01/21, doesn't have staff hours. As per the Administrator due to the COVID 19 pandemic and staff being shifted around to cover staff out with COVID 19 he couldn't update the LIC 500. LPA discussed with Administrator the importance of reporting incidents appropriately to the licensing and placement agency. The following topics were discussed with the STRTP representative: The runaway plan and law enforcement contact policies. Emergency Intervention Protocols and proper documentation. As per the Administrator, there were no physical restraints in 2021 or as of the date of this inspection Mental Health Client transition planning and how Child and Family Team are being initiated and utilized Clients involvement in planned activities. Children Records: LPAs reviewed 4 children's files. The files contain a record of the client's Health and Education Passport, Individualize Education Program (IEP) admission agreement, medical assessment, consent forms, identification emergency information, appraisal and needs and services plan, immunization record, centrally stored medication record, safeguards for property/valuables, personal rights form and cash resource information. Staff Records: LPA reviewed 6 employee files. The files contain the following documentation: first-aid certificate, Child Abuse Index Checks/Department of Justice (DOJ)/Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) criminal record clearances, personnel record, health screening, criminal record statement, employee rights, and tuberculosis test. Staff number 1 on the review of staff/volunteer records did not obtain a criminal record clearance and was not associated with this group home. Based on the guardian system a letter was generated and appears to have been mailed to the employee and the facility on 5/14/21 informing them that fingerprints process was closed and the employee was not associated to this group home. The Administrator said he never received a letter from Care Provider Management Bureau. Administration/Accountability: LPA received and read the minutes from the board of directors meetings dated 4/7/21. The Emergency Evacuation plan and physical plant sketches are posted. The Emergency Disaster Plan, LIC 610C was posted. Personal rights were posted. The facility License was posted in a prominent place. As per Title 22, the following deficiency was observed during this inspection and will be cited. Copies of these LIC 809s LIC 858, LIC 859 and civil penalty assessment -caregivers background check were provided during this exit interview. LPAs also discussed the facility appeal rights during this exit.

On 05/25/2022, the Department received a complaint alleging that clients are smoking marijuana in the facility. Staff members who were interviewed denied the allegation that clients are allowed to smoke in the facility, including activities outside of the facility grounds. LPA was informed by staff members that they have caught client(s) smoking inside the facility, including while conducting routine checks and were able to confiscate the contraband and document the incident. Staff workers, including the Administrator, stated that staff are always present and are working professionally. Staff interviewed stated that they are not supplying marijuana to the clients and do not condone this type of activities. In confidential interviews, all clients interviewed denied the allegation that staff working at the facility allowed them to smoke marijuana or any other form of tobacco or device such as a vape. All clients denied that staff are supplying marijuana or other forms of contraband. Several clients disclosed that they obtain their smoke and other devices, such as a vape while at school. Clients interviewed stated that staff are quick to take away any contraband they discover while at the facility. The clients that admitted smoking inside the facility is done without staff having any knowledge. L.A. County representative that was identified in the referral as having direct information about the allegation could not be contacted, therefore no statement was obtained. The county emergency response worker (ER) who was assigned to the referral made the determination that the referral is to be evaluated out. It should be mentioned that LPA Vargas determined that there were some irregularities in the manner that the facility were under reporting special incident reports (SIR) with respect to discovering contraband. Statements obtained could not corroborate the allegation reported. Therefore, the above allegation of neglect/lack of supervision is determined unsubstantiated at this time. A finding that the complaint is unsubstantiated means that although the allegation may have happened or is valid, there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that the alleged abuse occurred. An exit interview was conducted and copy of this report was provided to the facility representative for review and signature. No deficiencies were cited at this time

On July 21, 2023 at 10: AM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Irene Yamamoto conducted an unannounced case management inspection at the facility. LPA met with the facility representative named above. The purpose of the inspection is to address the following: - The facility received information that a staff provided a vape pen to a client while in care. The staff was terminated but the facility did not report the incident to Community Care Licensing (CCL). - Records obtained and reviewed by the undersigned LPA show that staff did not have a criminal record clearance and was not associated to the facility during staff's employment period from July 6, 2022 to January 31, 2023. Based on the above information, a deficiency citation is issued under 80061(b)(1)(E) Reporting Requirements and 80019(e)(1) Criminal Record Clearance. These violations pose an immediate health, safety, and personal rights risk to clients in care. A violation of Section 80019(e) will result in an immediate assessment of civil penalty of one hundred dollars ($100) per violation for a maximum of 5 days by the Department therefore, a civil penalty assessment of $500.00 is issued. An exit interview was conducted, and the following reports were provided: LIC809, LIC 809-D, LIC421BG and LIC Confidential Names Form. Appeal rights forms were provided and explained.

It was alleged that staff provided a minor with a vape pen while in care. Confidential interviews reveal that former and current clients in care denied the allegation. They denied being provided with a vape pen by any staff. They denied witnessing any staff provide a vape pen to other clients. The identified client denied the allegation. Staff who were interviewed denied providing any minor with a vape pen. The identified staff denied the allegation and accused another staff of the allegation. However, records reviewed support the allegation that the identified staff provided the identified client with an vape pen on more than one occasion. The records reviewed include an admission to the allegation by the identified staff. The facility terminated the identified staff's employment on January 31, 2023, due to the allegation. Based on the above information, the preponderance of evidence standard has been met, therefore, the allegation is substantiated. A deficiency citation is issued under Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) 87072(c)(11) Personal Rights - To be free of physical, sexual, emotional, or other abuse, and from corporal or unusual punishment, exploitation, infliction of pain, humiliation, intimidation, ridicule, coercion, threat, mental abuse... This requirement was not met as evidenced by records reviewed which include the admission by the identified staff to providing a client with a vape pen while in care. This poses an immediate health, safety, and personal rights risk to clients in care. An exit interview was conducted, and copies of the following licensing reports were provided: LIC 9099, LIC 9099-C, LIC 9099-D and LIC Confidential Names Form. Appeal rights forms were provided and explained.

On August 09, 2024, Licensing Program Analysts (LPAs) Juliet Robles, Olena Maico and Brent Lockhart conducted an unannounced inspection at the facility at 8: AM. LPAs met with Carlos Garces, Administrator and Shaun Fernandez, Facility Manager. The purpose of the inspection was to conduct a Required - Year inspection at this Short Term Therapeutic Residential Treatment Program (STRTP) facility. The STRTPs Mental Health Program Application is valid until 02/02/2025. This STRTP is licensed to serve up to six (6) males ambulatory children ages 7-17 years of age. The facility also provides services to non-minor dependents. Currently, there are four (4) clients in placement. This is a one story home with five (5) bedrooms, three (3) bathrooms, one (1) office, a full kitchen, dining room and family room. PHYSICAL PLANT: A tour of the facility was conducted at 9: AM, along with facility manager. LPAs observed the following posted items that are accessible to clients like: Grievance Procedures, Personal Rights, Ombudsman Poster, license, facility sketch and menus. All hazardous items have been properly made inaccessible to areas where clients will have access. The medications were stored and locked in a cabinet near the entrance. Cleaners/chemicals are locked and stored in the garage. Sharp knives are inaccessible and stored in a locked cabinet near the entrance. There are two (2) First Aid Kits that are checked and are complete. Supplies of staples non-perishable foods for one week and perishable foods for two days are maintained in the facility. The facility has smoke detectors and carbon monoxide that are operable and located in bedrooms and hallways. The hot water in the client bathroom was measured to be 106 degrees (F). The facility outside grounds was also inspected and it was observed to be clean and well maintained. Emergency exits were free from obstruction. Operations Facility maintains a current, written plan of operation that meets licensing standards. Facility maintains a register of clients and the register is available upon request. The board of directors regularly conducts meeting to review and discuss the STRTPs operation. Disaster Preparedness Plan Facility maintains a current, written disaster and mass casualty plan of action. Facility conducts disaster drill at least every month or with new hire. The drills are documented, and the documentation is maintained in the facility for at least a year. Facility maintains an emergency and disaster plan, register of clients, Needs and Services Plan for each client, medication records, and contact information for each client's responsible party and physician. Core/Therapeutic Services Facility provides core services and supports to children as appropriate or necessary that are trauma informed, culturally relevant, age and developmentally appropriate and include the following: Medi-Cal specialty mental health services; transition port services; educational and physical, behavioral, and mental health supports; activities to support children with services to achieve permanency. Client Records LPAs 11: AM started to review six (6) client records. All client records are electronic and available to the licensing agency to inspect, audit and copy upon demand. Client records contain required information including, but not limited to, consent forms, court orders, appraisal/needs and services plan, medical assessment/consent; safeguards for cash resources, personal property and valuables; education records; personal rights forms; and medication administration records and psychotropic medication record. Emergency Intervention Plan: Facility utilizes technique of group and individual behavior management like crisis prevention and alternative methods of handling aggressive and assaultive behavior. Staff have trainings on manual restraint if needed to be utilized. STAFFING RECORDS: During the inspection review, LPAs reviewed five (5) staff files and verified that all facility staff was subject to criminal records review, fingerprinted and cleared DOJ, FBI and CACI. All staffs signed the Criminal Record Statement and acknowledgement to report Child Abuse. Personnel records are maintained on the administrator, facility manager and each employee. Documentation of the required education, experience and training requirements are maintained in the personnel file. On today's inspection, two (2) Type B deficiency citations are issued under 87070(b)(14)(F) Children's Records and 87065.1(d)(6)(A) Staff Record. An exit interview was conducted, and a signed copy of this report, LIC 809C, LIC809D, LIC811 and appeal rights were provided to the facility manager.

It was alleged Staff are not addressing minors' multiple AWOL's while in care, Staff are not adequately supervising minors in care and Staff are not preventing minors from smoking while in care. It was also alleged Staff are not preventing minors from using marijuana while in care, Staff are not reporting incidents involving minors in care and Staff are mismanaging minor(s) medication(s) while in care. The staff stated that clients are talked to and discouraged to leave the facility by given them other options to do. The staff stated that two to three staff supervise the clients, the staff are through out the home and the staff conducts room checks periodically. The staff stated clients are discouraged to smoke and are reminded of the facility's rules regarding smoking, the staff stated that contraband is confiscated when the staff is able to get from the clients. The staff state that incidents are reported to management and the management has not discouraged the staff from reporting incidents. The staff stated that all the staff has been trained on medication distribution and protocol is follow by the staff. The staff reported that the staff gives the proper medication to the client and stand there to make sure the clients take the medication. The confidential interviews revealed multiple staff are in the facility supervising the clients and that the staff check on the clients frequently through out. Information indicated that the staff tries to talk out the clients when leaving the facility without permission and redirect the clients when acting out. The confidential interviews indicated that the staff gives the medicine to clients and stand there to make sure the clients take the medicine. Information indicated that there has not been a physical altercation between staff and clients. The Social Worker stated that they had no concerns with the care and supervision in the facility and that the staff communicates issues with the social workers. Based on the interviews and records reviewed, the allegations are found to be unsubstantiated. Although the allegations may have happened or are valid, there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove the allegations. Copies of LIC9099, LIC9099C, LIC811 and Appeals rights were provided and discussed with the facility representative mentioned above. There were no deficiencies cited.

LPA met with Ayan Hill, Licensee (L) and Radiance Clinton, Facility Administrator (FA) who granted LPA entry into the facility. During the visit, LPA utilized the CARE Tool to conduct a Health and Safety Inspection of the facility. LPA observed the interior and exterior of the facility to be clean and safe. LPA observed that the facility is a two-story residence with five bedrooms and three bathrooms. One bedroom will be shared by two youths and the remaining four are all single rooms. All bedrooms and bathrooms have adequate furniture, linens, supplies, and equipment for the capacity of the facility. Sufficient storage space for client's personal belongings was observed in each room. All three bathrooms will be accessible to clients. Water temperature was tested and found not the exceed 120 degrees F.The facility is requesting to be licensed for six female youths ranging in age from 12 to 17 years old + 18 years old if youth is 17 years old upon placement. LPA observed the locked medication box and petty cash box in a locked cabinet in a locked garage, which is also utilized as a staff office. Staff will be the only ones to access this area and LPA observed where the spare keys are kept in an emergency. Two locked boxes with cleaning chemicals and spare feminine hygiene products are also kept in the garage. A small fridge will be purchased in the near for refrigerated medications. The kitchen area was equipped with an adequate amount of utensils, dining supplies, and cups for clients. No food was observed as there are no clients, and no pending placement at this time. Facility will verify required food on hand at time of client placement. (Cont. on LIC 809C) A fully equipped first aid kit was reviewed and is placed in the staff office and the pantry. LPA observed the spare pantry where there was extra food storage and emergency supplies. Licensee will purchase, in the near future, a generator for power backup incase of blackout. Brighter Day STRTP's physical plant is adequately prepared to accept clients. After completing and finalizing the Program Statement/Plan of Operations, LPA will print LIC 203A for the facility. An exit interview was conducted and a copy of this report was given to Licensee.

On this date, LPA (Licensing Program Analyst) Lisa Slusher conducted a case management inspection for the purpose of following up on issues discovered during a complaint investigation and a review of incident reports. The following are addressed on this date. 1. The facility submitted an incident report for an incident occurring on 6/4/23 for an incident involving C1. C1 was restrained during this incident. The staff person lacked Emergency Intervention Training by the licensee and performed a restraint which was not a part of their Emergency Intervention Plan. A citation for STRTP ILS Section 87095.65 2. The incident report regarding the restraint on 6/4/23 lacked required information for the reporting of manual restrains. The facility is cited for a violation of STRTP ILS section 87061(i)(6) 3. An incident occurred on 6/3/23 involving law enforcement. The incident report indicates that the youth (C1) was "sitting on the curb" within the sight of staff. The report also indicates that the youth destroyed a closet organizer. The facility contacted law enforcement for "property destruction and a runaway youth". Based on interviews and evidence reviewed, the agency failed to provide adequate care and supervision to the youth and instead contacted law enforcement. The facility is cited for section 80078(a) Responsibility for providing care and supervision. 4. This facility was licensed in December of 2022. Based on the number and severity of incidents, confidential interviews and other reviewed documentation, the board of directors has not established appropriate internal policies for staff nor appropriate oversight of incidents occurring at the facility. Additionally, the board has not ensured appropriate staffing levels to control for staff burnout when acceptiing additional youth for placement. This poses a potential threat to the health, safety or personal rights of clients in care. The facility is cited for section 87063, Accountability.

narrative: It was reported the facility stored expired medications from previous placements incase a current placement's medication prescription was not refilled timely. The facility staff denied the allegation. Statements obtained from interviews conducted with staff indicated expired medication is taken to a pharmacy to be disposed and if a client's placement is terminated, their respective County Social Worker will pick-up left-over medication. Statements obtained from confidential interviews conducted revealed two clients did not have a prescription filled on one occasion each. One of the reported incidents was due to the facility being unable to obtain documentation from the client's home county. It was reported the facility lost a client's medication. The facility staff denied the allegation. Statements obtained from interviews conducted with staff did not reveal knowledge of, or incidents related to a client having medication lost or stolen. Statements obtained from confidential interviews conducted indicated that current clients placed in the facility have not had medication lost or stolen. It was reported medication was accessible to clients in care. The facility staff denied the allegations. Statements obtained from staff indicate that medication is kept in a secured lock box and inaccessible to clients. Statements obtained from confidential interviews conducted provided conflicting statements. One client reported that medication is inaccessible to clients while another client reported that medication was accessible to clients. Statements obtained from confidential interviews conducted indicated previous facility staff would allow multiple clients to enter the staff office while administering medication and create the opportunity for clients to access another client's medication. However, this client further reported that current staff implemented a new system and allow only one client in the office at a time during medication administration. It was reported the facility billed a county for providing 1:1 staff to client ratio and did not provide the client the 1:1 supervision. This allegation was disproved by statements obtained from an interview conducted with the clients SCSW, who reported the facility did not bill the respective county for 1:1 supervision while the client was in placement. Based on information obtained through interviews conducted and records reviewed the allegations were found unsubstantiated. Although the allegations may have happened or are valid, the standard of the preponderance of evidence was not met. Exit interview conducted and a copy of this report was provided to the facility representative. No deficiencies were cited during this inspection.

On 09/23/21 at 09: AM, Licensing Program Analysts (LPA) Zeyda Loera conducted an unannounced Post Licensing Inspection at the facility. LPA met with Princess Wesley, Administrator. The facility currently has a provisional Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) license. The STRTP's Mental Health Program Application is pending approval. The STRTP has a pending application for National Accreditation. This STRTP is licensed to serve up to six (6) ambulatory children ages 12-17 years of age. There are three (5) ambulatory minors, currently in placement. The LPA requested the following: Personnel Report LIC500, Client Roster, Board of Meeting Minutes, Clients and Staff Files. This facility is a one-story home with four (3) bedrooms, three (2) bathrooms, a staff office, kitchen, dining, a living room, and a laundry room. There are no bodies of water on the premises. There are no firearms or ammunitions in the facility. At 09: AM, LPAs conducted a walkthrough of the entire facility. Physical Plant The license, facility sketch, personal rights, emergency disaster form, complaints poster, emergency phone numbers and food menu are posted in a prominent, publicly accessible location in the facility. Disinfectants, cleaning solutions and sharps are kept inaccessible in a locked closet. Facility has non-perishable food for at least one week and perishable food for at least two days. Medications are centrally stored in a locked storage room. Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors were tested and in proper working order . Fire extinguishers were fully charged. First Aid Kits were checked and found to be complete. Room temperatures are maintained at 76 degrees F. The hot water temperature was tested and measured at 110 degrees F. All sinks, showers and toilets were in working order. No more than 2 children share a bedroom. All beds are in good repair; equipped with good springs, clean mattresses and pillows. Adequate supply of beddings and linens were observed. Facility provides age-appropriate clothing items and hygiene products. Overall, facility is clean, safe, sanitary and in good repair. Operations Facility maintains a register of clients and the register is available upon request. The board of directors regularly conducts meeting to review and discuss the STRTP's operation. The facility administrator and manager are the responsible and capable staff for communicating with emergency personnel in the facility. The facility has developed, maintained and implemented written complaint procedures. Client Records LPAs reviewed four (4) client records. All client records are available to the licensing agency to inspect, audit and copy upon demand. Client records contain required information including, but not limited to, consent forms, court orders, needs and services plan, removal/discipline/complaint procedures; medical assessment; safeguards for cash resources, personal property and valuables; education records; personal rights forms; and medication administration records. LPAs found that Needs and Services Plan (NSP) were not signed by authorized representatives. Staff Records LPAs reviewed three (6) staff records. All staff have been subjected to criminal records review and have been fingerprinted and cleared with DOJ, FBI and CACI. The administrator meets the required qualifications and/or experience. LPA was not able to verify documentation of the required education and experience requirements are maintained in the personnel file. LPA was not able to verifty requirements for Facility Managers.. LPAs were unable to verify 40 hours of annual training for direct care staff. An exit interview was conducted, and a signed copy of this report, LIC811, LIC9102TA, LIC and appeal rights were provided to the facility administrator.

narrative: On May 4, 2022, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA), Claudia Portillo conducted an unannounced Case Management inspection at the facility above and met with the Carolyn Ruffin (Executive Director), Laura Daniels (Assistant Administrator). The purpose of the inspection was to gather information of an incident reported via Special Incident Report (SIR): 5/1/22. The STRTP reported that on May 1, 2022, Child Ref #1 (C1) (see Confidential Names form LIC811 dated 5/4/22). Regurgitated medication crushed it and then snorted it. Staff contacted medical personnel for an assessment/medical clearance and C1 was transported to Memorial Hospital for medical clearance and a psychiatric assessment. LPA Portillo interviewed Carolyn Ruffin (Executive Director), Laura Daniels (Assistant Administrator) and C1. LPA requested to review the JV-220, P-Mar and medical report. While reviewing documentation LPA Portillo, observed that the staff were not documenting the reasons for medication not being taken on May 1, 2022, and there was no addendum for the initial incident report that indicates client was in the hospital for two days and missed medication. However, staff indicated that C1 took the psychotropic medication at the hospital, but no medical records were provided to LPA to validate the statement. Staff indicated that the facility doesn't receive discharge papers when clients discharged from the Psychiatric Assessment Center (PAC). LPA Portillo contacted the PAC and the manager indicated that the discharge papers are provided to the client and only the CSW can obtain copies of the discharge papers. Based on LPA medication record review, the PMARs for M1 and M2, are missing several staff initials and/or reasons for refusal/omission on C1, for May 1, 2022. Any medication taken by the youth will be documented appropriately. Each staff who assists the youth with self administration, signs their full name, initials and position, one time only in the section indicated on the P-MAR. The P-MAR needs to be initialed each time/date staff assists the youth to verify that the medication was taken. Based upon the above information, it is determined that the facility is in violation of the Health & Safety Code 1507.6(b) (1) Mental health services; liability; use of psychotropic medicines. Psychotropic medications shall be used only in accordance with the written directions of the physician prescribing the medication and as authorized by the juvenile court pursuant to Section 369.5 or 739.5 of the Welfare and Institutions Code. The second citation will be issued under violation of Title 22 80061(b)(1) (E ) Reporting Requirements. Any unusual incident or client absence which threatens the physical or emotional health or safety of any client. It is determined that citations shall be issued: (see 809D). It was alleged that staff at the facility had withheld a client's medication from them for a period of approximately 1-2 weeks in November/December 2021. In an interview conducted, one child stated that their psychotropic medication was not necessarily withheld from them but was either stolen or lost back in December of 2021. The child stated that they could not state for sure who may have stolen the medication. The child was also unsure of any issues with staff picking up replacement medication but stated they were not able to take their medication for that time period. In an interview conducted, another child stated that they were unaware of the specific situation but staff would sometimes need reminders to administer medication to clients. However, they have not intentionally withheld medication in their experience. In interviews conducted, one staff member stated that there was an issue with one child's medication going missing back in December of 2021 but that staff immediately contacted the pharmacy to get replacements. However, the pharmacy needed to contact the child's medical provider to confirm the replacements and it caused a delay of approximately 1 week. Another staff member corroborated the above statement and revealed that the child's medication was eventually found in the back of the medicine cabinet where it had fell. Staff stated they would never intentionally withhold medication from clients. In an interview conducted with the child's probation officer, the probation officer stated that he was not completely familiar with the situation but from what he understood, staff members were delayed in picking up the client's prescription refills for a period of approximately 1 week. The Probation Officer stated that he did not believe the medication was intentionally withheld for any reason. A review of incident reports revealed that the child's medication could not be found and that staff immediately called in for a refill. It was also alleged that staff in the home did not arrange for at least one client in care to attend specialized classes as part of their treatment plan. In an interview conducted, one child stated that attendance in the classes took some time to finalize and there were no concerns about staff not doing their part in supporting them. In interviews conducted, staff stated that they were aware that the child needed to be enrolled in the classes but that it was up to their mental health professional to enroll them. In an interview conducted, the child's Probation Officer confirmed that the child was enrolled in the classes but that the programs could sometimes take 1-2 months to finalize. There were no concerns that staff did not assist with enrolling the child in the classes. A review of records indicated that staff would assist the child's team in facilitating the classes but that it would be a team effort and not solely the responsibility of facility staff. Based on interviews conducted and records reviewed, there is not a preponderance of evidence to prove that the above allegations occurred. narrative: Facility staff do not refill residents' medications on a timely basis, Facility staff do not ensure that residents are enrolled in school, Facility staff do not properly wash and sanitize dishes at the facility, Facility does not provide residents appropriate hair care products and hair services, Facility staff do not allow residents private phone conversations with social worker, Facility staff are emotionally and verbally abusive (including yelling) to residents, Facility staff threaten residents, Facility staff use inappropriate language toward residents, Facility staff do not allow residents to make phone calls, Facility staff do not allow residents to come out of their rooms, Facility does not provide a safe environment for resident(s), Facility does not provide adequate food for residents, Facility refrigerator is odoriferous, and Facility does not post licensing phone numbers. The investigation of the above allegations was conducted by this LPA and it consisted of but not limited to a review of records, including the children's needs and services plans, medical records, and interviews with 3 staff members ADM, S2 on 10/14/21, S3 on 12/6/21, and Clients C1, C2 on 10/14/21, C3 on 10/19/21, C4 on 11/09/21 and CSW's (CSW1, CSW2) on 10/28/21 (Reference Confidential Names Form LIC 811, dated May 25, 2022). Based upon information obtained during investigation into noted allegations, including, but not limited to interviews with clients and staff, observations during LPA's facility visits, and review of clients' files, the following was noted: As to the allegation that facility staff do not adequately supervise residents, during interviews with both clients and staff, this allegation was denied. Per staff and program statement, the facility minimum ratio is one staff for every four clients and for the six clients at the facility there is always a minimum of two staff and sometimes three depending on circumstances. As to the allegation that the facility does not provide activities for clients, although an outdated activity calendar from the prior month was observed posted during the visit to the facility, interviews with both clients and staff revealed that a variety of activities are offered; however, that some clients elect not to participate. As to the allegation that facility staff make inappropriate comments to clients, during interviews with clients and staff, this allegation was denied and further stated that no instances of this type of conduct was observed. As to the allegation that facility staff does not disperse correct allowance amounts to clients, although it is not usually permitted to deduct from a set allowance amount based upon a client's behavior, the facility has an approved program statement that allows this as a motivator to reinforce positive behavior. As to the allegation that facility staff do not refill clients' medications on a timely basis, per interviews with staff, this was denied and it was explained that upon a clients' admittance to the facility, if the social worker does not initially provide appropriate documentation to administer psychotropic medication, that facility staff are unable to administer that medication until they can get a doctor's appointment scheduled, which usually occurs within the first few days after admission. As to the allegation that facility staff do not ensure that clients are enrolled in school, per interviews with staff, this was denied and it was explained that upon a clients' initial admission, the enrollment process can take up to a few school days to obtain the required documentation and complete the paperwork. As to the allegation that facility staff do not properly clean/sanitize dishes, per interviews with staff, this was denied and it was explained that clients are given the chore of doing dishes as an opportunity for clients to take responsibility, that staff supervise this chore and utilize it as a learning opportunity by guiding clients through these tasks to complete them adequately. Per interviews with clients, clients explained that some of the clients definition of what is considered to be clean was different than that of staff and other clients. As to the allegation that facility does not provide clients appropriate hair care products and services, facility staff denied and further explained that staff goes beyond just obtaining necessary hair care products readily available and also will special order some products on the internet, so as to satisfy the clients' hair care needs. Per interviews with clients, it was indicated that necessary hair care items were provided, however, that some of the clients preferred specific brands that were not provided. As to the allegations that facility staff do not allow clients to make phone calls and that staff do not allow clients private conversations with their social workers, interviews with staff revealed that this was denied and further stated that clients may make phone calls and are provided privacy per needs and services plan during allowed hours. Further, interviews with clients revealed that these allegations were denied and that clients are allowed phone calls within the allowed hours and that privacy is given during calls with social workers and on other calls as outlined in needs and services plan. As to allegations that staff are verbally and emotionally abusive, including yelling at clients; facility staff threatens residents; and facility staff uses inappropriate language towards residents, interviews with clients and staff revealed that these allegations were denied. It was explained that although staff may have to occasionally raise their voice to obtain the clients' attention, that staff interact professionally and with compassion in their communications with clients. Per interviews with clients, these allegations were denied and some clients reiterated that the staff need to occasionally raise their voice for redirection. As to the allegation that facility staff do not allow clients to leave their rooms and congregate in the common areas of the facility, both clients and staff denied by further explaining that if a client does not attend school because they feel ill, that the client is expected to stay in their room and rest and not be out in common areas exposing other clients. As to the allegation that facility does not provide a safe environment for clients, per interviews with staff, this allegation was denied and per interviews with clients, this allegation was denied and clients further indicated that they felt safe at facility. As to the allegations that facility does not provide adequate food for clients and that facility refrigerator has a foul odor, these allegations were deemed unsubstantiated per interviews of clients and staff and observations made during facility visits. Per observations during facility visits, an adequate amount and variety of nutritious food was noted from the five food groups and no foul odors were noted anywhere in the facility. Per interviews with clients, if the facility ran out of their favorite "junk food", such as chips, etc., this was interpreted as the facility not providing adequate food. Per interviews with staff, it was indicated that a nutritious, well balanced meal plan is provided, however, that clients prefer to eat fast food / junk food on a daily basis. As to the allegation that facility does not post Licensing and other resource contact phone numbers, this allegation was deemed as unsubstantiated per interviews with clients and staff and per observations during facility visits. During facility visits, all required documentation was observed as appropriately posted in hall area. Per staff, this documentation was posted prior in the kitchen area and had recently been relocated into the hall. Per clients, it was stated that sometimes when clients become angry, the documentation will be torn down and that staff will have to print new copies to re-post this documentation. Therefore, based on the information received, the above allegations are determined to be unsubstantiated. Although the allegations may have happened or are valid, there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that the alleged violations occurred, therefore the allegations are found to be unsubstantiated. Appeal Rights were provided and discussed with the facility Administrator. There are no deficiencies to be cited at this time. Exit interview was conducted and a copy of the report along with the (LIC 811) was left with the STRTP Administrator.

narrative: On April 11, 2022 the Department received a complaint regarding a fight at the facility between two clients. The fight resulted in one client losing consciousness after being struck by another client with a coffee bowl. The investigation revealed that on April 4, 2022 a fight took place between two clients (C1, C2) (Reference Confidential Names Form LIC811 dated 7/21/22). Staff denied they failed to intervene during the fight. In addition, staff denied they were informed that a fight was planned by one of the clients. Per staff, the initial incident occurred in a client's bedroom when C2 confronted C1. Staff (S2) stated she was unable to physically intervene due to clients biting. S2 reported staff (S1) was outside the bedroom preventing other clients from entering the bedroom and did not physically intervene and support S2 with the clients who were fighting. Statements obtained from confidential interviews conducted revealed S2 was notified earlier in the day that clients intended on fighting. Furthermore, S2 responded to the notice by saying she would not intervene if a fight occurred. Four of the five clients interviewed reported staff did not verbally or physically intervene and were observed outside the bedroom during the fight. The consensus of the statements obtained during interviews conducted indicated the fight ended when C2 was bit by C1. C2 then walked out of the bedroom and into the kitchen. A subsequent altercation took place shortly after in the kitchen. Statements obtained from interviews conducted with staff and clients indicated C1 obtained a skateboard and threw it at C2, striking her. After she was hit with the skateboard, C2 obtained a coffee pot and swung it at C1 striking her head. C1 began bleeding from her head and lost consciousness. At this time during the incident, staff intervened and the clients were separated. Per statements obtained from interviews conducted with staff and clients, after staff separated the clients C2 obtained a bowl from the kitchen, walked to the front of the facility where C1 was located and struck C1 on the head with the bowl. (Continued) Based on information obtained through interviews conducted and records review, the allegation is substantiated. Facility cited for violation of Interim Licensing Standards, STRTP, Article Sec. 87065.2(b)(1) Personnel Duties. Facility staff failed to supervise and protect clients in care resulting in a physical altercation between clients and a client sustaining injury. Exit interview conducted. A copy of this report, Confidential Names Form LIC 811 dated 7/21/22 and LIC9099D were given to the above-mentioned facility representative. Appeal Rights provided and discussed. Per the new Civil Penalty laws, Health and Safety (H&S) Code section 1548(E), an Enhanced Civil Penalty (ECP) determination is pending due to the substantiated allegation. If an ECP is warranted, a Community Care Licensing (CCL) representative will return to the facility to deliver the penalty assessment.

narrative: Licensing Program Analyst Dina Camara conducted a case management inspection 08/25/22 at 10: AM based on the number of relevant law enforcement contacts reported by the facility, pursuant to Health and Safety Code section 1538.7. During this inspection, 10 out of Direct Care Staff and 6 out of 6 youth files were reviewed. 3 out of Direct Care Staff and 3 out of 6 youth were interviewed. (See the Confidential Names List, LIC 811, dated 08/25/2022). The Plan of Operation including policies and procedures were reviewed. Minutes from the board of directors' meetings related to the facility's incidents involving contact with law enforcement were reviewed. Based on the analysis of the confidential interviews and youth file review including the needs and service assessments and youth case plans, the licensee uses trauma-informed and evidence-based de-escalation and intervention techniques when staff is responding to the behavior of a youth residing in the facility. Interviews with youth and staff indicate the licensee prohibits calls or threats to call law enforcement as a form of discipline. narrative: On 7/21/22 at 2: PM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Christopher Larios conducted an unannounced case management inspection. During the inspection LPA Larios met with Assistant Administrator Ms. Laura Daniels. The purpose of the inspection was to issue citations for deficiencies discovered regarding the facility Plan of Operation (POO) and Inspection Authority of the Licensing Agency. While assessing an incident reported to the Department the following was observed: LPA Larios conducted a record review of staff #1 (S1) (See Confidential Names Form LIC 811 dated 7/21/22) file on 4/21/22. The file review revealed S1 was out of compliance on training regarding restraint and emergency intervention. Per the facility POO, if a client engages in self-harm or harm to others facility staff are required to use approved restraint techniques. While conducting an assignment regarding a reported incident at the facility, Community Care Licensing Division (CCLD) Investigations Branch (IB) attempted to interview S1. IB and S1 scheduled an interview for 6/13/22 at 2: PM in the area of the facility. S1 was not present. IB contacted S1 and rescheduled the interview for 6/15/22 at 11: AM. S1 did not attend the rescheduled interview. On 6/15/ IB attempted an in-person interview with S1 at a facility. Upon arrival, IB identified S1 and informed S1 that she missed the interview appointment. S1 walked to a vehicle and stated she could not speak at the moment due to transporting a client. IB asked S1 if another staff was able to transport the client. S1 stated she needed to transport the client. S1 then asked IB to text her and left. (Continued) Based in record review, information gathered from interviews attempted the facility is cited for violation of Interim Licensing Standards, STRTP, Article Sec. 80072(f) Plan of Operation. The licensee failed to ensure staff were in compliance with emergency intervention plan requirements as specified in its Plan of Operation. In addition, the facility is cited for violation of California Code of Regulations Title Div. Sec. 80044(b)(1) Inspection Authority of the Licensing Agency. The licensee failed to ensure that provisions were made for the Department to interview a staff. Exit interview conducted and a copy of this report, Confidential Names Form LIC811 dated 7/21/22, LIC809D were given to the above-mentioned facility representative. Appeals Rights were provided and discussed.

Staff denied the allegations. Statements obtained from confidential interviews conducted indicated clients have appropriate dresser space as required. narrative: It was alleged that the Licensee and staff members at the facility were not planning or providing adequate activities for clients in care, leading to boredom and behaviors among the clients. In interviews conducted with 3 clients in the home, all 3 clients stated that there were generally two paid outings each month which included activities such as going to the movies or having barbecues at the park. However, depending on client behaviors throughout the month, outings may sometimes get changed as a result of bad behaviors among the clients. Clients also stated that on normal days, staff would sometimes take them to the park, games would be played in the home, and clients would play sports like basketball or hit the punching bag. However, all 3 clients stated that most of the clients liked to just stay at home and rarely participated in activities that they were not interested in. One client (C1) did indicate that they felt as if a few of the staff members were uninvolved and did not try to encourage clients to participate in activities or make the effort to take them out into the community. In interviews conducted, staff members confirmed that the facility provided two paid outings a month. Outings included activities such as going to the movies, paintball, barbecues at the park, and more. Occasionally, the facility will take the clients on more than two outings a month, depending on behavior. However, because the clients sometimes act up or misbehave, extra outings may sometimes be taken away or changed as a form of discipline. In the home, the clients have the option of playing video games, board games, exercising, and more. Staff all agreed that clients mostly liked to stay at home and play on their electronics most of the time. Based on interviews conducted and records reviewed, there is not a preponderance of evidence to prove that the above allegation occurred. Although the allegation may have happened or may be valid, the preponderance of evidence standard has not been met. Therefore, the allegations are deemed UNSUBSTANTIATED. An exit interview was conducted and a signed copy of this report, along with the Licensee's Appeal Rights (LIC 9058 01/16) was provided to the Licensee.

narrative: Page The Department received a complaint regarding alleged Neglect/Lack of Supervision. The investigation revealed on 5/7/23 facility staff contacted 911 at around 1: PM after observing client (C1) in his room unresponsive, foaming at the mouth and bleeding from his nose. Upon arrival, paramedics resuscitated C1 and transported him to the hospital. Statements obtained from confidential interviews conducted revealed C1 was given a white, powdery substance by another client (C2) at the facility. C1 reportedly ingested the substance through his nose. A toxicology report revealed THC and fentanyl was present in C1's system. Staff denied lack of supervision led to C1 overdosing and denied lack of supervision led to C1 obtaining a controlled substance while in care. Statements obtained from interviews conducted with staff indicated staff on shift were actively supervising clients. Staff reported they do not allow clients to visit each other's room and were unaware C2 had entered C1's room through another entrance located in the hallway. Staff reported there were no prior incidents were both C1 and C2 were involved in regarding controlled substances. Statements obtained from confidential interviews conducted revealed the facility does not allow clients to possess contraband and have confiscated such items from clients. In addition, confidential interviews conducted revealed none of the clients previously observed C2 with a controlled substance. All clients interviewed denied staff fail to care for and supervise clients. Statements obtained from interview conducted with placing agency staff revealed they had no concerns regarding the facility's ability to provide care and supervision. Bases on information obtained from interviews conducted and records review the allegations are unsubstantiated. Although the allegations may have happened or are valid, the standard of the preponderance of evidence was not met. Exit interview conducted. A copy of this report and Confidential Names form LIC811 dated 6/22/23 were given to the above mentioned facility representative.

On May 29, 2024, the Department received a referral alleging that an STRTP client had a soda slapped out of his hand, was body slammed against a bed, breaking the frame, and then body slammed again, this time dislocating client's elbow, by an STRTP staff member. LPA's investigation revealed that on the evening of May 27, 2024, a client was experiencing behaviors which ultimately resulted in a restraint being employed by STRTP personnel after various forms of redirection were unsuccessful. STRTP staff reported incident to Community Care Licensing Division (CCLD), and documented restraint as required. It was revealed that the soda was not slapped out of client's hand, but was taken away due to client consuming too much soda throughout the day so far. Interviews with staff reported that the client was aggressive all day, swinging punches and slapping at staff before staff restrained client. A staff member present during restraint stated client dislocated their own elbow in an unknown fashion upon being released from restraint. Another staff member present stated client was released from restraint and immediately let out a yell, maintaining that the restraint was executed textbook, as per training. LPA was not able to obtain statements from clients as they refused to be interviewed. Social worker interviewed by LPA had no concerns regarding the allegation. Although the allegation may have happened or is valid, there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that the alleged violation occurred, therefore the allegation is determined to be Unsubstantiated. No deficiencies were cited at this time. Exit interview conducted. A signed copy of this report, LIC9099-C, and LIC811 were provided to Brenda Hurtado, Mental Health Specialist. Appeal rights provided.

The Following Allegation(s) were reported: 1. Staff are not keeping accurate records of youths in care. Staff members S1, S2, and S3 denied the allegations, stating that all client records are stored electronically and later transferred to the clients' binders for backup. During the initial 10-day visit, LPA reviewed three of the four client binders (C1, C2, and C3) and noted the absence of the Head of Services Progress notes/Services for September and October. Nevertheless, the Administrator provided these documents electronically to the LPA, explaining that they were being faxed to Yolo County as part of an audit response. 2. Staff are not ensuring that youths receive mental health services. Staff members S1, S2, and S3 categorically denied the assertion that mental health services are inaccessible to all clients. They underscored their organization's dedication to ensuring that every individual, irrespective of their background or situation, has access to the necessary mental health support. S1 highlighted the range of services offered, including counseling, therapy, and support groups, all tailored to address various needs. Additionally, S2 and S3 revealed that they strive to meet with clients three times a week or as required; however, there are instances when clients choose not to attend these meetings, which will be documented in each client's individual records. The information gathered from C1 and C2 corroborated the previously mentioned details, indicating that mental health services are readily available and accessible at the facility to support clients as required. Information collected from CSW1 and CSW2 indicated that there were no reported problems concerning their clients' access to mental health services, nor did the clients express any concerns. However, CSW1 noted that there were occasional challenges in acquiring requested documents or receiving return calls, with some response times from S2 extending beyond three days. Furthermore, CSW1 pointed out an occurrence where documents not pertaining to his client were received, although this matter was later resolved. Therefore, based on the information received, the above allegation(s) is determined to be unsubstantiated. Although the allegation(s) may have happened are valid, there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that the alleged violations occurred, therefore the allegations are found to be unsubstantiated. Appeal Rights were provided and discussed with the Foster Family Agency. There are no deficiencies to be cited at this time. An exit interview was conducted and a copy of the report along with the (LIC 811) was left with the STRTP Assistant Administrator.

narrative: The Following Allegation was reported: The staff does not ensure that minor(s) are adequately fed while in care. The staff members (S1, S2, and S3) rejected the allegations, emphasizing that every client receives three daily meals that include all five food groups, along with access to a variety of snacks between meals. They explained that grocery shopping occurs on a weekly basis, and they actively seek client feedback regarding preferred meals and snacks, ensuring that each meal is balanced with the five food groups. The staff firmly denied any claims of food being withheld from clients, and no clients have reported such issues. S1 stated that all staff are trained in trauma-informed care and understand the importance of creating a safe and healthy environment within the facility. They also mentioned that there have been no reports of staff mistreating clients, nor have any clients indicated experiences of misconduct by staff. Additionally, the accounts given by C1 and C2 supported the previously mentioned information, confirming that staff have never denied them food and that they have access to a range of snacks. Both C1 and C2 expressed that they feel secure living in the facility and that they receive assistance from the staff. Furthermore, the statement from CSW1 confirmed that there are no concerns about the care and supervision provided to their client (C1), and that C1 has never reported any incidents of misconduct by the facility staff. Therefore, based on the information received, the above allegation(s) is determined to be unsubstantiated. Although the allegation(s) may have happened or is valid, there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that the alleged violation(s) occurred, therefore, the allegation(s) is found to be unsubstantiated. Appeal Rights were provided and discussed with the STRTP Administrator. There are no deficiencies to be cited at this time. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of the report along with the (LIC 811) was left with the STRTP Administrator.

narrative: Multiple allegations were received by the Department alleging supervision, personal rights, reporting requirement and staff qualification issues. The client/victim stated that the altercation was an isolated incident and staff sought medical attention for client. Records show the incident was reported to law enforcement and licensing. Another report revealed that a client grabbed a scissor being used by staff. The incident was stabilized after staff intervened and client complied and returned the scissors to staff. This incident was also reported to law enforcement and licensing. Interviews reveal that no client is provided any preferential treatment while in placement. Clients are encouraged to go to the gym or play sports. These activities are not held back, regardless of client behavior. Laptops are provided by school district, not the facility, and any restriction to computer access is based on placement agency directive or court order. narrative: Investigation revealed the following: It was alleged staff did not intervene when minors engaged in inappropriate interactions while in care. Staff had similar statements and denied the allegation. Staff stated that two children were arguing in the home over a game. One child became upset and started attacking the other child. Staff stated that staff stepped between the children and redirected children from hitting one another. Additionally, staff stated that the one child who initiated the interaction started acting out and threatening to kill themselves and ended up leaving and damaging property. Interviews conducted with children had similar statements and denied the allegation. Children had similar statements of staff in an incident transpired and that staff intervened. However, child stated that the way that staff intervened was not adequate to resolve the issue. Interviews conducted with county social worker (CSW) and additional witnesses confirmed information provided by staff and child and did not identify any concerns or issues with staff not being present or not intervening and redirecting children from being in an altercation. It was also alleged; staff spoke inappropriately to minor(s) in care. Staff denied the allegation. Staff had similar statements and stated that one child had an issue with cursing and speaking inappropriately to staff and children. Children made no reference to staff speaking inappropriately to anyone in the home. Documents reviewed and interviews conducted with CSW and witnesses make no reference to any complaints or issues noted of any staff speaking inappropriately to staff or children in the home. Furthermore, it was alleged staff pushed minor in care. Staff denied the allegation and stated that during one altercation between two children staff intervened by stepping in the middle of the children to prevent children from hitting one another. Staff stated that no children were pushed but rather children were redirected to walking away from one another. Children had differing statements from staff in that one child stated that during the altercation one staff pushed them to the ground. Child identified what staff they believed pushed them to the ground, however, child stated that others in the facility would support and believe that staff as he is liked in the facility. LPA reviewed documents and interviews conducted with CSW and additional witnesses no documents of information received support that staff pushed children or pushed a child in any incident. Lastly, it was alleged staff inappropriately restrained minor in care. One child stated that a staff restrained them and held them on the ground. Child stated that this occurred during one incident after child struck another child. Child stated that staff restrained them for an unknown amount of time and that other staff stood by vacuuming. On the other hand, staff had similar statements and denied the allegation. Staff stated that staff stepped between children to prevent one child from hitting the other. Staff stated that one staff was vacuuming and that after the altercation from children one child started making threats of harming themselves and left facility and began damaging property. Interviews conducted with CSW and witnesses identified that one child has had a history of embellishing the truth and that no information provided supports that restraints were used or that staff intervening in altercation did any inappropriate restraints. Based on documents reviewed and information provided it is unclear as to if staff did not intervene or that staff's intervention was inappropriate. Documents reviewed illustrated an incident occurring between two children. However, no information identified that staff restrained children or staff spoke inappropriately to children in care. Although the allegations may have happened or may be true there is not a preponderance of evidence to support that the allegations did or did not happen. Therefore, this complaint is being closed Unsubstantiated. Exit interview was completed, no deficiencies cited, and a copy of this report was given to Administrator.

narrative: Staff stated that sometimes children say inappropriate comments to one another or to staff but staff have never been heard or observed speaking inappropriately to any child. Children stated that staff are always respectful and that they have had no issues with staff saying anything inappropriately. It was also alleged staff handle minors in a rough manner that caused injury. Staff denied the allegation. Staff stated they received no reports or documented incidents of children injuring themselves or being handled roughly causing injury. Staff stated they have observed no marks or bruises on children and have received no complaints regarding the ways in which staff handle children. Interviews conducted with 3 children stated they have never observed a staff handle anyone roughly. Three children stated that if they get into trouble or are having issues they get their electronics taken away or they are asked to stay in room for approximately 10-15 minutes. Interviews conducted with one child identified that one staff handled them roughly. However, child was unable to identify what staff did, or when it occurred. Child also stated no one was present to observe and that they were not injured based on staff handling them roughly. Furthermore, it was alleged staff are under the influence while providing supervision to minors in care. Staff and children denied the allegation. Staff stated they have never observed staff to be under the influence. Children stated that they have never observed staff to be under the influence or having issues with care an supervision. It was alleged, staff yell at minors in care. Children and staff denied the allegation. Staff stated that they do not yell at children. Staff stated that they may call to a child from another room but that children are not yelled at. Staff stated they encourage children and everyone to use their inside voices and remind children not to yell at one another. Children stated that they have not heard or observed any staff yell at a child or someone in the home. It was alleged, staff are not ensuring that minors receive services as necessary. Staff and children denied the allegation. Staff stated that children receive all services and obtain initial assessments for services in the times in which they are authorized. Staff stated if a child is new and there is a delay in services; staff will work with county in getting services started for child. Children stated they have never been denied services or not received services. Additionally, it was alleged staff force minors to stay in their rooms for an extended period of time. Staff and children denied the allegation. Staff stated if children are exhibiting aggressive behaviors they are asked to sit in their room for approximately 10-15 minutes to calm down. Staff stated that children are consistently monitored and are free to leave their rooms to eat, use the restroom or if calmed. Children stated that when in trouble they are asked to calm down in their rooms but stated that staff are present and that times are usually 10 to 15 minutes. It was alleged facility is not meeting the needs of clients in care. Staff and children denied the allegation. Staff stated that facility attends regular training and that children are able to obtain whatever they are in need of. Staff stated that facility has adequate staffing and are able to provide resources and monitoring to children. Children stated they felt as though facility has adequate staffing to meet their needs. Children stated they felt safe and comfortable in the home. It was alleged clients are allowed to smoke weed. Staff and children denied the allegation. Staff stated that no children smoke in the home or have been caught with any smoking paraphernalia. Children stated they do not smoke and have not observed anyone smoking weed or anything else in the home or near facility. It was alleged client treatment plans not followed. Staff and children denied the allegation. Staff stated that children receive updated needs and services monthly and children and family team meetings are conducted regularly. Children stated that staff are very good with following their treatment plans and getting them the services they need. It was alleged, staff are under the influence while transporting clients in care. Staff and children denied the allegation. Staff stated that they have never observed anyone to be under the influence caring for the children. Staff stated that there have been no incidents of incidents occurring while transporting children to and from locations. Staff stated that if anything occurs it is documented and reported to all associated parties. Children stated they have not observed any staff being under the influence in or out of the facility. Lastly, it was alleged the licensee does not ensure oversight and general supervision of the facility. Staff and children denied the allegation. Staff stated that they have adequate staffing in all shifts and have enough staff to meet the needs of the children. Children stated that there is adequate staff throughout the day and that staff are attentive and responsive to whatever they may need. LPA observed documents and documents identified children receiving all required services, staff received required training's and no incidents of children being injured or incidents of staff being rough. Documents reviewed also identified no issues or concerns with facility from outside agencies. Based on the information gathered, although the allegation may have happened or is valid, the preponderance of evidence to prove the allegation was not met, therefore the allegation is unsubstantiated. An exit interview was conducted. A copy of this report Confidential Names Form and Appeal Rights were provided to the facility representative via electronic mail. There were no deficiencies cited during this inspection.

On 04/30/25 at 11: AM, Licensing Program Analysts (LPAs) Olena Maico conducted an unannounced annual Inspection at the above facility. LPA met with Melissa Williams, Administrator. This STRTP is licensed to serve up to six (6) ambulatory children ages 10-15 years of age. The facility also provides services to non-minor dependents pursuant to W&I Code 16501.1 (C)(1). There are three (3) minors currently in placement. This facility is a 3-bedroom single story home. There are no bodies of water in the premises. There are no ammunition and firearms in the facility per the administrator's statement. LPA Maico conducted a walk-through of the entire facility alongside with the administrator and Facility Manager. LPA requested LIC 500, LIC 9020, LIC 610C, LIC 309 and LIC 308 as well as the Emergency Drill records and Board Meeting records to be provided to the LPA. Facility has current CARF accreditation expiring January 31st 2028, as well as Mental Health Services approval expiring November 16 2025. LPA observed the license, facility sketch, Personal Rights, Emergency Disaster form, Foster Youth Bill of Rights, Complaints/Grievance policy, menu and activity schedule posted in prominent, publicly accessible location in the facility. Physical Plant Facility has no cameras on premises. Disinfectants, cleaning solutions and sharps are kept inaccessible in a locked closet in the hallway. Facility has non-perishable food for at least one week and perishable food for at least two days and meet the licensing standards. Medications are centrally stored in a locked closet in the office. Sharps are locked in the hallway closet. Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors were tested and in proper working order. Fire extinguishers are fully charged. Room temperatures are maintained at 76 degrees F. The hot water temperature was tested and was measured at 114 degrees F. All sinks, showers and toilets were in working order. No more than 2 children share a bedroom. All beds are in good repair; equipped with good springs, clean mattresses and pillows. Adequate supply of beddings and linens were observed. Currently there is one client per room and there 2 beds in each room. The unoccupied beds have mattress and a bedsheet, but no pillows. Extra pillows are stored in the Administrator office which is next door, due to the clients misusing the extra bedding (like tearing it etc). Each client has a color coded towel and use it for the hygiene needs. If clients need paper towels, staff will provide it. Paper towels are not stored in the bathroom due to clients stuffing it inside the toilet and clogging toilets. Emergency exits are free from obstruction. Overall, the facility is clean, safe, sanitary and in good repair. Facility has basic laundry services. LPA reviewed insurance and registration for the facility's vehicles and it is current. Vehicles have first aid kit. Operations Facility maintains a register of clients and the register is available upon request with all the required information. The board of directors regularly conduct meetings to review and discuss the STRTP's operation. LPA reviewed the minutes provided. The facility has developed, maintained and implemented written complaint procedures which is posted in the office. Cash resources of the clients are stored in the Administrator's office which is the next door tot he facility. Disaster Preparedness Plan Facility maintains a current, written disaster and mass casualty plan of action. Facility conducts disaster drill at least quarterly for each shift. Facility maintains an emergency and disaster plan, register of clients, Needs and Services Plan for each client, medication records, and contact information for each client's responsible party and physician. Disaster and casualty plan is updated every year and posted at the facility. Client Records LPAs reviewed three (3) client records. Client records are available to the licensing agency to inspect, audit and copy upon demand. Client records contain required information including, but not limited to, consent forms, court orders, JV 220 forms, needs and services plan, medical assessment; safeguards for cash resources, personal property and valuables; education records; personal rights forms; removal/discipline/complaints form and medication administration records. LPA reviewed the JV 220 form and psychotropic medication administration log. LPA did not observe TB test in 3 clients' files, Administrator stated the clients have appointments scheduled for the TB tests. Facility will be issued a deficiency due to not having the records of TB test or the refusal of the test administration. Two technical assistance were issued to the facility. Due to time constraints, LPA will be back to continue the inspection. The copy of this report along with the Appeal Rights and LIC 9102TA and the LIC809d was issued to the Administrator.

Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) N. Strickland conducted a tele-inspections with Camry Group Home for Boys, Administrator (ADM) Cynthia Briscone to conduct a Technical Advisory (TA) call regarding the facilities transition to Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) and to conduct Component III Orientation. LPA discussed the following with ADM. Community Care Licensing'S (CCL's) decision to issue a provisional STRTP license with conditions to the facility. The following conditions are required to help ensure the ability of the licensee to maintain ongoing compliance with STRTP licensure requirements, and to meet the health, safety and well-being needs of children and nonminor dependents in care. These conditions are in addition to any existing requirements for STRTP licensure and are imposed on the license on Page 1 in accordance with Health and Safety Code sections 1520.1 and 1562.01; and California Department of Social Services (CDSS) STRTP Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) Sections 87030, 87031.1(b), and 87031.2(a)(1). On December 15, 2020, the Licensee agrees to the following conditions: 1.) Completion of STRTP Training. Within (6) six months of the effective date of this provisional license, Camry Home for Boys shall complete the STRTP Training Academy through Seneca, or another similar course preapproved by the Department. Within 30 (thirty) days after completing this requirement, Camry Home for Boys shall submit to the Department proof of completion. The Department may grant extensions as necessary for Camry Home for Boys to complete this training requirement, but such extension may not exceed the expiration of the provisional licensure period. ***Continued on Page 2.*** 2.) Record Keeping and Reporting Requirements Training. Within (90) ninety days of the effective date of this provisional license, Camry Home for Boys shall provide training to all facility management, treatment and care staff on applicable ILS standards specifically; facility, staff, and client record keeping and reporting requirements as specified in California Code of Regulations, Title 22, sections 80066 and 80070, ILS section 87061. Within 10 (ten) days after completing this requirement, Camry Home for Boys shall submit to the Department proof of training outline and signatures of training attendees. These conditions are effective for six (6) months from the effective date of the license on Page 1. Upon expiration of the conditions, Licensee may contact the Regional Office to request a provisional license without conditions. Failure to comply with the conditions set forth in this conditional license may be grounds for discipline, including but not limited to application denial, suspension, or revocation of the license, as applicable. The fact that CDSS may decline or omit to take immediate disciplinary action for a violation of a condition does not constitute a waiver of the right to raise that violation at a later date. You may contact your Licensing Program Analyst at the CCLD Regional Office if you have any questions or need assistance. To complete Component III of the STRTP orientation LPA also discussed incident reporting procedures, including those specific to law enforcement contacts; facility, client and staff record requirements; application of prudent parent standards and client personal rights with ADM. On this date, CAMRY HOME FOR BOYS is recommended for licensure on a provisional basis with conditions. License will expire one year from effective date.
