narrative: On December 13, 2022 at 2: PM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA), Val Wilson at CFLC Hemet Ranch to complete an annual inspection. The purpose of the inspection is to conduct an annual inspection of the facility. LPA was met at the facility by Administrator, Reyna Corona. There were three staff and two clients present at the time of the inspection. Appropriate staff/client ratios were verified during the inspection. The Administrator led the tour of the facility and were joined by Program Director, Sheila Stephenson at 3: PM. Facility has obtained Mental Health Certification effective 04/20/23. Licensee has obtained National Accreditation through CARF effective through 9/30/25. Licensing fee payments have been paid and there is currently a balance of zero. The facility consists of six bedrooms and three bathrooms. The facility includes a dining area, kitchen area, living room, and laundry room. The facility has a detached office area with four offices utilized by therapists, Administrator, and staff. Above the facility is a separate house with three bedrooms, living room, kitchen, and bath that is utilized for storage, group therapy, visitors, and weekly staff meetings. All bedrooms have individual beds, individual contraceptive boxes, and drawer space for each client. The facility ensures that there is one client per bed with appropriate clean linens, pillows, comforters, and mattresses in good repair. During inspection, LPA's observed two air vents were dusty in the main living area. Vents were cleaned at the time of inspection. Facility grounds are clean and free of debris and observable hazards. There is adequate indoor and outdoor activity space. Outdoor swing set is securely anchored to the ground. However, the set of swings near the pool level has packed dirt underneath. Gym equipment and other activities were observed for client's recreation time. All facility smoke detectors are in appropriate working order. The facility maintains an adequate supply of perishable and non-perishable foods and appears to be following the posted menu. All required forms are posted including the Grievance Procedures, Visitation Policies, Personal Rights form, and Foster Care Ombudsman poster. Medications are locked and centrally stored in the laundry room. . (continued) The hot water throughout the facility was measured to be between 105 degrees F and a maximum of 125 degrees F. Facility has a pool which is appropriately fenced and secured with a chain link fence. The enclosure was measured to be 5 feet in height, with a self-latching gate. Per facility staff, no firearms or weapons are allowed in the facility. Facility appears to be meeting the terms and conditions of their license. Based on the inspection, the facility is being cited type B in accordance with Interim Licensing Standards STRTP, Article 07. Physical Environment, Outdoor Activity Space Section 87087.2(b) Outdoor Activity Space (b) As a condition of licensure, the areas around and under high climbing equipment, swings, slides and other similar equipment shall be cushioned with material which absorbs falls. This poses/posed a potential health, safety or personal rights risk to persons in care. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this report and appeal rights were provided to Reyna Corona.

On December 12, 2022 at 1: PM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA), Val Wilson, arrived at CFLC-Sunset House, Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program, to initiate an annual inspection. The purpose of the inspection is to conduct an annual inspection of the facility. LPA was met at the facility by Program Director, Sheila Stephenson. The facility temporarily closed August 1, 2021, related to Covid and staffing resources. At the time of the inspection, there is no clients or staff in the facility. LPA provided and reviewed with the Program Director the Entrance Checklist and then the Program Director led the tour of the facility at 1: PM. Administrator, Rafaella Aguilar, joined the inspection around 2: PM. No Client files or Staff files were reviewed during time of inspection. Personnel Files are maintained off site at the corporate office in Hemet, Ca. During the time of inspection, there were no clients present in the facility for interviews. The Administrator stated there are no firearms or weapons allowed in the facility. Facility appears to be meeting the terms and conditions of their license. The facility consists of four bedrooms and two bathrooms. Smoothing of patching work repair and painting is needed in all four bedrooms. The facility includes a dining area, kitchen area, living room, laundry room, staff office, and a portable therapist office/visitor room located in the backyard. All bedrooms have individual beds and drawer space for each client with no more than two beds in a room. The facility ensures that there is one client per bed with appropriate clean linens, pillows, comforters, and mattresses in good repair. Facility grounds are clean and free of debris. There is adequate indoor and outdoor activity space. Gym equipment and other activities were observed for client use on the back patio. All facility smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are in appropriate working order. All required forms are posted including the Grievance Procedures, Visitation Policies, Personal Rights form, and Foster Care Ombudsman poster. Medications are locked and centrally stored in the medication room next to the front door. Water temperatures were noted between a minimum of 105 and a maximum of 125 degrees F. (Continued) (Continued) Facility has a pool which is appropriately fenced on three sides and secured with a rod iron fence. The enclosure was measured to be 5 feet in height, with a self-latching gate. The wood fencing on the walkway side of the pool that leads to the front door is leaning due to the weight of the greenery on the fencing. Based on the inspection, the facility is being cited in accordance with Title 22, Division 6, Chapter 1 and Interim Licensing Standards, STRTP, Article 07, Section- Physical Plant: 87087.2(a)(4)(A) - The fencing around the pool is leaning due to the weight of the greenery and 80087(a) - The walls in bedrooms one, two, three, and four need smoothing of patching work repair and painting. Additionally, Disaster Preparedness 80023(a) - The binder was thought to have been misplaced in the move. Program Director pulled the information from the Program Statement and plans to get a red binder to add the mass casualty and disaster plan for CFLC Sunset House. These technical violations pose a potential risk to the health and safety of the children. An exit interview was conducted, a copy of this report, and appeal rights were reviewed and given to Administrator, Rafaella Aguilar.

On April 25, 2023, Community Care Licensing (CCL) received a complaint alleging that facility staff did not adequately supervise a minor while in care. During investigation, Investigator Vasquez found no corroboration for the above allegation. Investigator, Vasquez received inconsistent information that facility staff did not adequately supervise C1 while in care. Confidential interviews revealed that an unknown adult male did access the facility with C1's and C2's help resulting in a sexual interaction between C1 and the adult male and C1 obtaining a marijuana vape pen while in care. Some confidential interviews stated that there were no signs that indicated that something unusual was occurring at the facility and added that staff supervision was being provided to clients in care through room checks every 15 minutes on the day of the incident. Confidential interviews further stated that staff became aware of the incident after C1 revealed the information to a staff member. There were no other known witnesses to the allegation. Investigator, Vasquez received inconsistent information about whether neglect or lack of supervision by facility staff resulted in the adult male accessing the facility, having sexual intercourse with C1, and providing C1 with a marijuana vape pen while in care. Based on confidential interviews, the allegation that staff did not adequately supervise C1 while in care, may have happened or is valid, but there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that the alleged violation occurred. Therefore, the allegation is unsubstantiated at this time. narrative: Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Carolyn Flynn and Stephanie Martinez, Student Assistant (SA) made an unannounced visit to the above listed facility to discuss findings from a complaint opened in the wrong facility. LPA and SA met with Amber Sanchez, Director of Therapeutic Services at 10: AM on 08/06/2021. LPA explained that there was a complaint filed in Powell regarding two clients (see confidential names list LIC811 date 08/06/2021) eloping at night back on January 6, 2021. Neither of the clients involved in the complaint were residing on the date of the complaint therefore the allegation could not be valid. LPA did discover during confidential interviews with eleven client and eleven staff that during the day, they are able to follow the protocol for clients eloping. However, from 10: PM - 7: AM there is only one staff in the cottage and a floater is to be on campus to help with issues such as elopement. On the night in question, four of the staff reported not having a floater on campus. This meant that when a child left, they could not follow or try to get them to stay because they had to provide supervision to the other clients in care and could not leave the cottage. The Interim Licensing Standard states that, "at least one direct care staff shall be on call and capable of arriving at the facility site within 30 minutes." Confidential interviews with four staff revealed that it is not common for the Manager on Duty (MOD) who is the on-call person at night to go to campus when a client is reported to have left campus. The MOD waits until the client arrives back on campus. As a result of the interviews and copies of incident reports LPA Flynn is issuing two deviancies as documented on LIC809D. At the time of this visit two deficiencies were cited as per California Code Regulation (CCR), Title 22, Division 6 and Interim Licensing Standards 3.1. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this report was provided to Amber Sanchez, Director of Therapeutic Services whose signature on this form confirm receipt of these document

An announced Office Meeting was held on Microsoft Teams to discuss a substantiated allegation of lack of supervision resulting in minor being sexually abused by an adult while in care. The meeting was conducted virtually over Microsoft Teams due the COVID 19 pandemic. Present in the meeting from Chamberlain's Youth Services - Acres were Administrator, Amber Sanchez, Interim Chief Executive Officer (ICEO), Brenda Jimenez, Director of Therapeutic Services, Melanie Davis, and Board Members, Pam Holmquist and Eric Taylor . Present from CDSS were Regional Manager (RM) Nelson Martinez, Licensing Program Manager (LPM) Helga Wong, and Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Carolyn Flynn. Additional attendees include: Sandi Shelgrove - DHCS, David Gutierrez - DHCS, Alexandria Andrew - DHCS, Sandi Shelgrove - DHCS, Marjana Jackson - SOC, Maxe Cendana - SBCBH, Joshua Mercier - Deputy Director San Benito County, Rachel White - Behavioral Health San Benito County, Melissa Lloyd - Sacramento County, Mia Buckner -Preston - Alameda County, Michelle Love -Alameda County, Laura Neal - Monterey County, Cynthia Elkins - Santa Clara County, and Temera Carson - Santa Clara County On 05/18//20/2021, the department received a complaint (Control Number: 26-CR-20210520130313) alleging lack of supervision resulting in minor being sexually abused by an adult while in care. The investigation was referred to and conducted by the Investigation Branch (IB). The investigation revealed that on 05/18/ C1 and C2 (refer to LIC811 - Confidential Names List), while in care, a 21-year-old male (V1) entered the facility without their knowledge, spent the night, and had sexual intercourse twice with C1 and had C2 perform oral copulation once. C2 disclosed to S1 on 05/19/2021 while on a walk the incidents from the night prior and was taken to Hazel Hawkins Hospital where C2 provided a statement to the San Benito Sheriff's Department and was then transferred to South Valley Medical and returned to Chamberlain's at 7: AM on 05/20/2021. C1 disclosed to S2 at 3: PM on 05/19/2021 that she had snuck her boyfriend into the cottage around 1: PM on 05/18/2021 and he remained there till approximately 9: AM on 05/19/2021. C1 also told S2 about the sexual relations that both clients had with V1 the night of the 18th. Based on IB investigation of confidential interviews with two clients and nine staff, incident reports, and the police report from San Benito Sheriff's Department the allegation lack of supervision resulting in minor being sexually abused by an adult while in care was determined to be valid. On 08/30/2021, the department issued substantiated findings for the allegation from 05/20/ Complaint Control Number 26-CR-20210520130313. The allegation lack of supervision resulting in minor being sexually abused by an adult while in care is a violation of Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) for STRTP Version 3.1, Article 6, Section Personal Rights (d) The licensee shall ensure that each child, regardless of whether the child is in foster care, is accorded the personal rights specified in Welfare and Institutions Code Section 16001.9, as applicable. In addition, the licensee shall ensure that each child is accorded the following personal rights: (11)To be free of physical, sexual, emotional, or other abuse, and from corporal or unusual punishment, infliction of pain, humiliation, intimidation, ridicule, coercion, threat, mental abuse, or other actions of a punitive nature including, but not limited to, interference with the daily living functions of eating, sleeping, or toileting, or withholding of shelter, clothing, or aids to physical functioning was issued. According to California Penal Code 11165.1 - "sexual abuse" means sexual assault or sexual exploitation...Section 261.5 (statutory rape) and Section 288a (oral copulation). The department has concluded an analysis and has determined that an Enhanced Civil Penalty is warranted for the sexual abuse Health and Safety Code section 1548(f)(1)(C): For a violation that the department determines constitutes physical abuse, as defined in paragraph (2), or resulted in serious bodily injury, as defined in Section 243 of the Penal Code, to a person receiving care at a therapeutic day services facility, community treatment facility, transitional shelter care facility, transitional housing placement provider, small family home, crisis nursery, group home, enhanced behavioral supports home licensed as a group home, group home for children with special health care needs, or short-term residential therapeutic program, the civil penalty shall be assessed as follows:(i) Two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) for a facility licensed to care for 40 or fewer children. (2) For purposes of subparagraphs (C), (D), (E), and (F) of paragraph (1), "physical abuse" includes physical injury inflicted upon a child by another person by other than accidental means, sexual abuse as defined in Section 11165.1 of the Penal Code, neglect as defined in Section 11165.2 of the Penal Code, or unlawful corporal punishment or injury as defined in Section 11165.4 of the Penal Code if the person responsible for the child's welfare is a licensee, administrator, or employee of any facility licensed to care for children. Today September 17, 2021, the department will be issuing a Civil Penalty per Health and Safety Code 1548(f1)(1)(c) for $2,500.00. The above was reviewed during the meeting and appeal rights were provided. This report was sent to Interim Chief Executive Officer Brenda Jimenez, who agreed to sign the report and email it back to LPA Flynn. Email was sent with a read receipt notification.

Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Carolyn Flynn and Stephanie Martinez, Student Assistant (SA) made an unannounced visit to the above listed facility to discuss findings from a complaint opened in the wrong facility. LPA and (SA) met with Amber Sanchez, Director of Therapeutic Services at 10: Am on 08/06/ LPA explained that there was a complaint filed in Powell regarding two clients (see confidential names list LIC811 date /8/06/2021) eloping at night back on January 6, 2021. Neither of the clients involved in the complaint were residing on the date of the complaint therefore the allegation could not be valid. LPA did discover during confidential interviews with eleven client and eleven staff that during the day, they are able to follow the protocol for clients eloping. However, from 10: PM - 7: AM there is only one staff in the cottage and a floater is to be on campus to help with issues such as elopement. On the night in question, four of the staff reported not having a floater on campus. This meant that when a child left, they could not follow or try to get them to stay because they had to provide supervision to the other clients in care and could not leave the cottage. The Interim Licensing Standard states that, "at least one direct care staff shall be on call and capable of arriving at the facility site within 30 minutes." Confidential interviews with four staff revealed that it is not common for the Manager on Duty (MOD) who is the on-call person at night to go to campus when a client is reported to have left campus. The MOD waits until the client arrives back on campus. As a result of the interviews and copies of incident reports LPA Flynn is issuing two deviancies as documented on LIC809D. At the time of this visit two deficiencies were cited as per California Code Regulation (CCR), Title 22, Division 6 and Interim Licensing Standards 3.1. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this report was provided to Patrick Ellis, Administrator whose signature on this form confirm receipt of these document.

narrative: Regarding the allegation that "Staff are being told not to follow reporting requirements",during the investigation, records review and interview evidence revealed that staff are trained and instructed to conduct proper reporting procedures. Other interviews claimed that staff are discouraged from implementing proper reporting procedures. LPA received multiple conflicting reports when asked about the allegations. LPA was able to obtain a copy of every requested report and was able to verify its submission to CRP. Based on the available information LPA gathered from interviews and observation, the preponderance of the evidence standard has not been met, therefore the allegation of "Staff are not following proper reporting requirements" has been found to be unsubstantiated. Regarding the allegation that "Staff face retaliation from management", During the investigation, staff interviews revealed that staff were retaliated against by management including cutting hours and even firing employees to retaliate against employees who spoke up against management practices. Other interviews disclosed that the staff are not retaliated against by management, and employees were let go due to not being good fits with the company or failing to obtain a criminal records clearance. LPA received multiple conflicting reports from staff when asked about the allegations. Based on the available information LPA gathered from interviews and observation, the preponderance of the evidence standard has not been met, therefore the allegation of "Retaliation from management" has been found to be unsubstantiated. An exit interview was conducted, during which LPA provided the Administrator with a copy of this report and a copy of their appeal rights. Facility is being cited for "staff having an altercation with a minor in care" based on LIS STRTP Personal Rights Section 87072 (c) (15): "The licensee shall ensure that each child, regardless of whether the child is in foster care, is accorded the personal rights specified in Welfare and Institutions Code Section 16001.9, and below, as applicable: To be accorded dignity in their personal relationships with staff and other persons." Regarding the allegation that "Staff are working without criminal clearance", LPA interviewed involved staff and clients. Interview evidence and record review revealed that the facility is allowing "staff to work without the proper criminal clearance." Interview, observation, and records evidence reveal that ate one time three staff members did not have the proper criminal record clearance yet were allowed to provide care, services, and supervision to the clients and have access to the facility. One staff (S1) was allowed to have access to the facility, to clean, drop off items, and access records, with out a criminal record clearance. Another staff (S2) was allowed to regularly provide rehab services to clients without the proper criminal record clearance. Staff (S3) was allowed to provide direct care and supervision to clients without a criminal records clearance. Based on the available information LPA gathered from interviews and records review, three staff members were found to be in violation, the preponderance of the evidence standard has been met, therefore the allegation of "Staff are working without the proper criminal clearance" is found to be substantiated. The Facility is being cited for violating Title 22, Division Chapter Article 03. Application Procedures Criminal Clearance (e) (2): "All individuals subject to a criminal record review pursuant to Health and Safety Code Section 1522 shall prior to working, residing or volunteering in a licensed facility: Obtain a California clearance or a criminal record exemption as required by the Department" An exit interview was conducted, during which LPA provided the Administrator with a copy of this report.

narrative: This report is continued from the attached LIC9099. On 10/9/2020, the LPA spoke with R1 who stated the facility staff took her cellphone and laptop at the direction of CSW. R1 said they had access to their laptop Monday through Friday between 8am and 5pm. R1 said they enrolled in 17 units at a Community College and was doing well at first then started to fall behind. R1 described an incident when they were allowed more time on their laptop to complete an assignment; due to personal triggers and staff's request for R1 to clean their room first, R1 became dysregulated. On 1/10/2021, the LPA spoke with Chelsea Silva, Facility Manager (FM) who stated that it was implemented by CSW that R1's laptop be kept at the school and brought to the facility for eight hours per day. FM said R1 used the laptop and cellphone for "Facetiming friends" and would show other clients' faces. FM stated that another reason the laptop was not kept at the facility was because R1 would try to breakdown the office door to retrieve it. The LPA also spoke with Amber Cepeda, Assistant School Manager (ASM) who stated restrictions on R1's cellphone and laptop were place by CSW and that, "Charis was expected to follow them." ASM said R1 was active with her classes but would "try to multitask using social media..." R1 had access to her laptop Monday through Friday between 8am and 5pm. ASM said facility staff allowed R1 to use the laptop outside these timeframes when they saw R1 was actively working on schoolwork. On 1/14/2021, the LPA spoke with Jessie Spears, Shift Facilitator who stated R1 "had plenty of access to tech...staff would observe her using social media...showed other clients' and staffs' faces." The LPA also spoke with a County Child Protective Services screener who confirmed there was no court order to restrict R1's laptop or cellphone on file. The LPA reviewed CFT Meeting Notes dated 8/28/2020 and signed by R1 that documented CSW directed R1 to hand in her cellphone, letting R1 know that they will not have their laptop until they turn in the phone for numerous safety reasons; a program was installed on the laptop so that R1 could communicate with other students as needed. The LPA reviewed the CFT Meeting notes dated 9/1/2020 that documented that R1's laptop will be charged prior to use because R1 will not have access to the charging cord. The LPA reviewed multiple SIRs dated between 8/19/2020 and 9/3/2020 documenting R1's escalated behaviors related to their laptop and cellphone restrictions. Although the allegation may have happened or is valid, there is not a preponderance of evidence to prove that alleged violation did or did not occur, therefore the allegation is unsubstantiated.

narrative: During shaving, the bathroom door is to remain open so staff can ensure residents do not self-harm. This rule applies to all residents in the household. Staff and residents also stated showers are limited to 15 minutes, and are scheduled for morning, afternoon or evening hours. Staff stated if a resident wanted to shower outside the schedule, they would be allowed to do so. Residents stated they would receive consequences if they exceeded the 15-minute time limit, but staff denied this to be true. Based on the LPA's observations; interviews which were conducted and record reviews, the preponderance of evidence standard has been met, therefore the above allegations are found to be SUBSTANTIATED. STRTP ILS Version 3. Section 87072(d)(6)(B), and 87072(d)(11) PERSONAL RIGHTS are being cited on the attached LIC 9099-D. Interim Licensing Standards version 3.1- PERSONAL RIGHTS (d) The licensee shall ensure that each child, regardless of whether the child is in foster care, is accorded the personal rights specified in Welfare and Institutions Code Section 16001.9, as applicable. In addition, the licensee shall ensure that each child is accorded the following personal rights: (6) To be provided with and allowed to possess and use adequate personal items, consistent with Welfare & Institutions Code section 16001.9(a)(23), which includes their own: (B) Toiletries and personal hygiene products, including enclosed razors used for shaving, as age and developmentally appropriate, and as appropriate to the child's or nonminor dependent's cultural, religious, ethnic, or racial background. Interim Licensing Standards version 3.1- PERSONAL RIGHTS 87072(d)(11) To be free of physical, sexual, emotional, or other abuse, and from corporal or unusual punishment, infliction of pain, humiliation, intimidation, ridicule, coercion, threat, mental abuse, or other actions of a punitive nature including, but not limited to, interference with the daily living functions of eating, sleeping, or toileting, or withholding of shelter, clothing, or aids to physical functioning. Residents stated this happens when another resident is violent. Residents stated staff will be in the room with the group and will lock the doors so "keep residents safe". Residents also stated there is a window in the recreational room but felt the window may not be big enough to escape through during an emergency. Staff stated they stay with the group in the recreation room with the keys during incidents where a resident becomes violent. Staff stated this is done to keep residents safe and prevent other residents from being triggered. The LPA found no records of residents being restrained inappropriately. Staff reported there is a training conducted on how to properly restrain a resident (Pro-Act), as well as ongoing in-house training on a regular basis. Staff reported some residents have sought medical attention after a restraint, but the diagnosis has been bruising, sore muscles or scratches. Staff records and Incident Reports confirmed staff reports. Residents interviewed who had been restrained at the facility did not state they were restrained inappropriately. Interviews were consistent between staff and residents that calls are not denied. All but one resident interviewed stated residents can request confidential calls and staff will step out of the room once the connection is established. Staff interviews confirmed that specific calls outside of restrictions in the resident's Needs and Services/Safety Plan, can be completed confidentially. Based on the information collected through file reviews and interviews, the IB was unable to determine the authenticity of the allegations or validate any violations of regulation. Although the allegation may have happened or is valid, there is not a preponderance of evidence to prove that alleged violation did or did not occur, therefore the allegation is UNSUBSTANTIATED.

AS and TS both stated several attempts were made to find C1 a more suitable placement, outside of returning her to her mother, which could have potentially been unsafe. narrative: No provisions were found in any of the residents' Needs & Services or Treatment Plans that spoke to the necessity of staff's presence during phone calls. All residents interviewed independently corroborate staff's presence or that staff is/are "always with [the residents]" when they talk on the phone; this policy does not allow for telephone calls to be confidential. Based on interviews and a review of records, the preponderance of evidence standard has been met; therefore, the above allegation is found to be SUBSTANTIATED. The facility is cited on the attached 9099D under the Interim Licensing Standards, Section 87072(d)(8) Personal Rights "To make and receive confidential telephone calls, unless prohibited by court order."

On February 28, 2022 at 3:00 pm, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA), Joon Choi conducted an unannounced case management inspection and met with Amanda Bell, the Quality Assurance Manager of ChildHelp Yvonne Fedderson and Sara O'Meara Short Term Residential Treatment Facility (STRTP), to discuss the incident report dated 01/28/2023 regarding Client 1 (C1). On 02/24/2022, Community Care Licensing received an incident report from the STRTP Facility. Per the incident report, on 01/28/2023, the facility reported that staff #1 (S1) did not follow correct Pro-Act restraint guidelines according to the Facility's Emergency Intervention Plan, when utilizing a restraint on FC1. It was reported that S1 utilized a single-person (single staff) restraint hold on C1, during an incident in which C1 was reported to be escalated in behavior. LPA Choi observed in the video that S1 did in fact utilize a restraint hold on C1, and that S1 restrained C1 by themselves, instead of, with the assistance of another staff member, which is mandated in Pro-Act training. LPA Choi was advised by QA that according to the facility's Emergency Intervention Plan and Pro-Act Training, S1 should have waited for the assistance of a second staff, at which time, both staff would have positioned themselves on either side of the client and utilized the minimum amount of force necessary to get C1 to baseline. LPA Choi observed S1 grab C1's shoulders and arms and physically move C1 to the front door exit. After S1 released C1, C1 fell to the ground. LPA Choi was advised by QA that after an administrative review of the video of the incident, that S1 was placed on leave from work. Based on confidential interviews, a records review of facility documentation, and the facility's video of the incident; the STRTP is being cited for violation of STRTP ILS, Personal Rights 87072(c)(11), To be free of physical...emotional, or other abuse, and from corporal or unusual punishment,...infliction of pain, humiliation, intimidation, ridicule, coercion, threat, mental abuse, or other actions of a punitive nature...This poses an immediate health, safety or personal rights risk to the children placed in care. Continued on the Next Page Exit interviewed conducted. A copy of this report, a technical violation for reporting requirements, LIC 811, and appeal rights were given and explained to Quality Assurance Manager Amanda Bell.

narrative: On June 29, 2023 at 08: AM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Joon Choi conducted an unannounced annual inspection at ChildHelp Joann Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP). LPA was met by Program Coordinator (PC) Heather Michelson. The facility is situated in a residential neighborhood and is a 6 bedroom, 3 bathroom - two story home with a living room/common area, dining room, kitchen, two car garage, and backyard with a patio. Please note, that the two upstairs bedrooms are used as a therapy office and a staff office. Also, two bathrooms are utilized for staff and one full bathroom is for the clients to share. There is a staff restroom in the staff's office upstairs and one downstairs. The garage is also used as a staff office. The facility's two registered vehicles are parked in the drive way full-time. LPA observed the following postings located in the front entry way and common area: facility license, grievance procedures, Personal Rights, Foster Youth Bill of Rights, the (contact information for the California Foster Care Ombudsman is on the Foster Youth Bill of Rights poster), visitation policies, and grievance procedures. LPA began a physical plant inspection at 9: AM assisted by Shift Supervisor Britnie Peluso. LPA inspected the facility's kitchen, dining area, refrigerator/freezers, food storage areas, garage, living room/common area, staff office, therapy office, three client bedrooms (B1,B2,B3) and one client bathroom. The bedrooms were arranged so that no more than two clients are were assigned to a room, and there is one client per bed and a shared closet. Each client room had the appropriate linens, pillows, comforters, and mattresses are in good repair. Each client had their own personal lockbox as well. Extra linens and client hygiene supplies are stored in two separate hallway closets. Additionally, each client was assigned a fully functional dresser drawer with adequate space for each client's belongings. The living room had two couches and a functional television. The dining room had a dining table with enough chairs for all the clients and some staff. There was a client activity schedule posted in the living room and a menu posted in the kitchen. Cleaning supplies such as chemicals are kept locked in the garage and downstairs staff restroom. Sharp utensils and cooking knives are inaccessible to clients and locked in a cabinet in the dining room. Licensee maintains an adequate supply of food and a variety of snacks for clients. LPA observed a minimum seven day non-perishable foods in the pantry and a two day perishable supply of food in the kitchen and garage refrigerators. Board games are kept in a separate closet in a downstairs closet. Continued Next Page There is adequate indoor and outdoor activity space; all exits, and walkways were free from obstruction. Client files were kept in a locked cabinet upstairs near the staff office. Per the Shift Supervisor, there are no weapons or guns on facility grounds. The facility's outside grounds (front yard, backyard and sides) were also inspected and were found to be clean, well maintained, and free of observable hazards. The backyard has a bike rack with bicycles for clients and there was one locked storage shed that had client's extra belongings and extra mattresses for the facility. The facility has an operable carbon monoxide detector located in the hallway and smoke detectors are located in each client bedroom and the common area. LPA observed the facility had three fire extinguishers, with one located in the kitchen, garage and upstairs. Each fire extinguisher was fully charged and inspected in May of 2023. The medications are centrally stored in the garage / staff office, in a locked cabinet. The facility had three First Aid Kits and were complete and kept in the garage. The washer and dryer are located inside of the garage and are accessible to clients with staff supervision. The laundry detergents are kept locked in a cabinet in the garage. The Kitchen had a fully stocked refrigerator and the gas stove and dishwashing machine were operational. There were no cleaning supplies observed to be in the kitchen. The kitchen cabinets had plenty of pots, pans, plates and bowls for the clients to use. The hot water in the client bathroom measured 109.7 degrees Fahrenheit and was within the specified 105 to 120 degree range. LPA observed that each client's hygiene items such as shampoo, toothpaste, soap, lotion, and deodorant were locked in a closet in the hallway. Facility staff explained that clients are given access to their hygiene prior to showering/bathing. LPA was also advised that clients are allowed to keep certain hygiene items in their rooms such as deodorant which they take to school. The facility has two vehicles used to transport clients to appointments and recreational activities. Each vehicle had no damage. The inside upholstery was intact for each vehicle. The brake lights and signals were operational. There was a fully stocked first aid kit in each vehicle as well as current registration and proof of insurance. At 09: AM, LPA observed that the client restroom had a slow draining sink, but the facility had work order in place so no citation was given. At 10: AM, LPA began interviews and conducted two staff interviews (S1, S2) and two client interviews (C1, C2). Continued on the Next Page At 11: AM, assisted by the Clinical Manager Brittany Kelly, Program Coordinator Heather Michelson and Shift Supervisor Brittnie Peluso, LPA began review of four Client Files. At 12: PM with the assistance of Program Coordinator, we then reviewed the facility's Operational Requirements. All of the documentation pertaining to these areas of the inspection were provided, and no deficiencies were noted. At 1: PM with the assistance of Program Coordinator, we then reviewed the facility's Disaster Preparedness Requirements. All of the documentation pertaining to these areas of the inspection were provided, and no deficiencies were noted. Based on observations and record reviews, no deficiencies were cited during this visit. Due to time constraints, LPA will return to complete the inspection at a later date. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this report was provided to Program Coordinator Heather Michelson.

narrative: On July 28, 2023 at 08: AM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Joon Choi conducted an unannounced annual inspection at ChildHelp Johnson Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP). Please note: although the facility is open, there are currently no clients placement as the facility is undergoing renovations. LPA was met by Program Manager (PM) Dana Butler. The facility is situated in a residential neighborhood and is a four bedroom, two full bathrooms (one for staff, one for clients) - one story home with a living room/common area, dining room, kitchen, two car garage, therapy room and backyard with a patio and storage shed. The garage is used as a staff office. The facility's two registered vehicles are parked in the drive way full-time. LPA observed the following postings located in the front entry way and common area: facility license, grievance procedures, Personal Rights, Foster Youth Bill of Rights, the (contact information for the California Foster Care Ombudsman is on the Foster Youth Bill of Rights poster), visitation policies, and grievance procedures. LPA began a physical plant inspection at 8: AM assisted by PM. LPA inspected the facility's kitchen, dining area, refrigerator/freezers, food storage areas, garage, living room/common area, staff office, therapy office, three client bedrooms (B1, B2, B3, B4) and one client bathroom. The bedrooms were arranged so that no more than two clients are were assigned to a room (two bedrooms have two beds, and the other two bedrooms have one bed), and there is to be one client per bed and a shared closet. Each client room had the appropriate linens, pillows, comforters, and mattresses are in good repair. Each client had their own dresser drawer. Extra linens are stored in a hallway closet. There is no hygiene as of yet, as there are currently no clients in the facility. The living room / common area had two couches and a functional television. The dining room had a dining table with enough chairs for all the clients and some staff. Cleaning supplies such as chemicals are kept locked in the garage. Sharp utensils and cooking knives are locked in a cabinet in the kitchen. Licensee will maintain an adequate supply of food and a variety of snacks for clients, once they are place. Board games are kept in a separate closet in the front entry way. Continued on the Next Page There is adequate indoor and outdoor activity space; all exits, and walkways were free from obstruction. Client files will be kept in the the staff office/garage. Per PM, there are no weapons or guns on facility grounds. The facility's outside grounds (front yard, backyard and sides) were also inspected and were found to be clean, well maintained, and free of observable hazards. The backyard has a grass lawn and one locked storage shed that had room for storage and bicycles. The facility has an operable carbon monoxide detector located in the bedroom hallway and by the water heater, and smoke detectors are located in each client bedroom and one in the common area. LPA observed the facility had two fire extinguishers, with one located in the kitchen and staff office / garage. Each fire extinguisher was fully charged and inspected in May of 2023. The medications will be centrally stored in the garage / staff office, in a locked cabinet. The facility had one First Aid Kit in the garage, but PM explained the facility would acquire more, when clients are placed. The washer and dryer are located adjacent to the kitchen and are accessible to clients with staff supervision. The laundry detergents are kept locked in a cabinet above the washer and dryer. The Kitchen had a functioning refrigerator and the induction stove and dishwashing machine were operational. There were no cleaning supplies observed to be in the kitchen. The kitchen cabinets had plenty of pots, pans, plates and bowls for the clients to use. The hot water in the client bathroom measured 109.5 degrees Fahrenheit and was within the specified 105 to 120 degree range. There are no client hygiene items as of yet. PM explained that clients will be given access to their hygiene prior to showering/bathing. LPA was also advised that clients will also be allowed to keep certain hygiene items in their rooms such as deodorant which they take to school. The facility has two vehicles used to transport clients to appointments and recreational activities. Each vehicle had no damage. The inside upholstery was intact for each vehicle. The brake lights and signals were operational. There was a fully stocked first aid kit in each vehicle as well as current registration and proof of insurance. At 9: AM, LPA conducted one staff interviews (S1). At 9: AM with the assistance the PM, we then reviewed the facility's Operational Requirements. All of the documentation pertaining to these areas of the inspection were provided, and no deficiencies were noted. Continued on the Next Page At 9: AM, assisted by the PM, LPA reviewed the facility's Emergency Intervention Procedures. All of the answers pertaining to these areas of the inspection were automatically inputted by Care Tools as n/a, and no deficiencies were noted. Please note: client records were also automatically inputted by Care Tools as N/A. At 9: AM with the assistance of Program Coordinator, we then reviewed the facility's Disaster Preparedness Requirements. All of the documentation pertaining to these areas of the inspection were provided, and no deficiencies were noted. At 9: AM with the assistance of Program Coordinator, we then reviewed the facility's Core Therapeutic Services. All of the documentation pertaining to these areas of the inspection were automatically inputted by Care Tools as "n/a", and no deficiencies were noted. At 9: AM, LPA began one staff file review, with the assistance of Compliance Coordinator Heather Michelson and Program Manager Dana Butler. Please note, there were no client files to review. Based on observations and record reviews, no deficiencies were cited during this visit. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this report was provided to Program Manager Dana Butler.

Confidential interviews revealed that C1 was absent without leave (AWOL) from the facility and was located at another state licensed facility nearby. Confidential interviews revealed that once S1, S2, and S4 arrived to pick up C1, C1 refused to cooperate with S1, S2, and S4 and C1 ran away from S1, S2, and S4. Confidential interviews revealed that once S1, S2, and S4 located C1 a second time, a restraint was applied to C1 for the safety of C1. Confidential interviews revealed that no one had observed S1 push C1 or any other group home children to the ground; however other confidential interviews revealed S1 did push C1 to the ground to apply a restraint for C1. Confidential interviews revealed that no one had observed S1 inappropriately touch group home children; however other confidential interviews revealed S1 did graze C1's chest during the application of a restraint on C1. Confidential interviews and documents obtained revealed that C1 did have past documented bruises and injuries; however, there were no new bruises or injuries on C1's body. Based on confidential interviews and record review, the allegations that C1 inappropriately touched group home children, C1 inappropriately handled group home child, and C1 hit a group home child may have occurred; however, are not supported or proven by evidence. Therefore, the allegations are unsubstantiated at this time. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this report, LIC 811, and appeal rights were emailed to the facility representative for signature. The original signed report will be placed in the facility file.

narrative: On June 22, 2023 at 9: AM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Joon Choi conducted an unannounced annual inspection at ChildHelp Baker Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP). LPA was met by Teaching Family Specialist (TFS) Latoya Hollis. The facility is a four bedroom, 2 bathroom -one story home with a living room, dining room, kitchen, two car garage, and backyard with a patio. Please note, that one of the bedrooms is used as a therapy office and in the therapy office is a bathroom that is not used by clients. Also, the garage is used as a staff office. The facility's two registered vehicles are parked in the drive way full-time. LPA observed the following postings located in the front entry way and dining area: facility license, grievance procedures, Personal Rights, Foster Youth Bill of Rights, the (contact information for the California Foster Care Ombudsman is on the Foster Youth Bill of Rights poster), visitation policies, LPA began a physical plant inspection at 9: AM assisted by TFS. LPA inspected the facility's kitchen, dining area, refrigerator/freezers, food storage areas, garage, living room, staff office, therapy office, three client bedrooms (B1,B2,B3) and one client bathroom. The bedrooms were arranged so that no more than two clients are were assigned to a room, and there is one client per bed and a shared closet. Each client room had the appropriate linens, pillows, comforters, and mattresses are in good repair. Extra linens are stored in the hall closet. Additionally, each client was assigned a fully functional dresser drawer with adequate space for each client's belongings. The living room had two couches and a functional television. The dining room had a dining table with enough chairs for all the clients and some staff. Cleaning supplies such as chemicals, and cooking knives are inaccessible to clients. Cleaners and chemicals are locked in a cabinet in the garage. The cooking knives and cutlery are locked inside of a cabinet in the kitchen. Licensee maintains an adequate supply of food and a variety of snacks for clients. LPA observed a minimum seven day non-perishable and a two day perishable supply of food. and current menu. Board games are kept in the therapist office and books were observed to be in the shelves in the living room with no restrictions to access. There is adequate indoor and outdoor activity space; all exits, and walkways were free from obstruction. Per Administrator there are no guns or weapons on facility grounds. Continued on the Next Page The facility's outside grounds (front yard, backyard and sides) were also inspected and were found to be clean, well maintained, and free of observable hazards. The backyard has a bike rack with bicycles for clients and there were two locked storage sheds and a client garden. The facility has an operable carbon monoxide detector located in the hallway and smoke detectors are located throughout the facility. LPA observed the facility had three fire extinguishers, with one located in the kitchen, garage and therapy room. Each fire extinguisher was fully charged and inspected in May of 2023. The medications are centrally stored in the garage / staff office, in a loced cabinet. The First Aid Kit is complete and kept in the garage / staff office as well. The washer and dryer are located inside of the garage / staff office and are accessible to clients with staff supervision. The laundry detergents are kept locked in a cabinet. The Kitchen had a fully stocked refrigerator and the induction stove and dishwashing maching were operational. There were no cleaning supplies observed to be in the kitchen. The kitchen cabinets had plenty of pots, pans, plates and bowls for the clients to use. The hot water in the client bathroom measured within 109 degrees Fahrenheit (within the 105 to 120 range). LPA observed that each client's hygiene items such as shampoo, soap, lotion, deodorant and cosmetics were locked in a closet in the hallway. Facility staff explained that clients are given access to their hygiene prior to showering/bathing. LPA was also advised that clients are allowed to keep certain hygiene items in their room such as lotion. The facility has two vehicles used to transport clients to appointments and recreational activities. Each vehicle had no damage. The inside upholstery was intact for each vehicle. The brake lights and signals were operational. There was a fully stocked first aid kit in each vehicle as well as current registration and proof of insurance. At 10: AM, LPA observed that the outside window screens were missing for client bedroom 2 and 3, placing the facility out of compliance with CCR 80088(b)...all window screens shall be in good repair. LPA conducted three staff interviews (S1, S2, S3) and three client interviews (C1, C2, C3). At 12: PM LPA began review of five Staff Files and Operational Requirements, assisted by the Program Coordinator. All of the documentation pertaining to these areas of the inspection were provided, and no deficiencies were noted. Based on observations made during the inspection, see LIC 809D, a deficiency was cited. Due to time constraints, LPA will return to complete the inspection at a later date. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this report and appeal rights was provided to Program Coordinator Heather Michelson.

narrative: On August 13, 2020, the Department received a complaint alleging that staff demonstrates an inappropriate form of discipline towards minors while in care. During confidential interview, it was revealed, staff would squeeze client's hands when they were acting up. Also, that staff squeeze client's hands so hard that they make them cry. Clients would tell staff that the hand squeezing was too tight, and staff would continue to hurt them. During interviews with Social worker (A1), C1 informed her that C1's hand was hurt from being squeezed from staff and that it hurt when staff squeezed C1's hand. Social Worker also stated that C1 was not listening and staff grabbed C1's hand and squeezed it to discipline them. Interviews with staff revealed that client's hands have been held to prevent them from getting to other clients. It was also revealed that it was possible that a client's hand was held too tight because they are younger and smaller so it could have felt like squeezing. During interviews with APM, it was stated, that clients are disciplined by loss of privileges and at no time is staff to put hands on a client unless they are a danger to themselves. CSW stated that C1 disclosed during a meeting that C1 had been hurt by a staff by having their hand squeezed. Based on interviews, the preponderance of evidence standard has been met in regard to the allegation that staff squeezed the hand of C1 as a form of discipline. Therefore, the allegation is Substantiated. This poses a Health, Safety or Personal risk to children in care. The Facility is cited for violation of the STRTP Interim Licensing Standards, Chapter 7.5, Version 3.1, section 87072(d)(11): Personal Rights. narrative: On December 22, 2020 at 10: AM, an informal office tele-conference was held with representatives from Childhelp Merv Griffin Village Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) via Microsoft Teams video platform. In attendance were: STRTP representatives Administrator Jessie Jorrin, Quality Assurance Program Coordinator Marlo Felix, Residential Manager Dorothy Waybrant, Residential Manager Felicia Ware, Executive Director Lawren Ramos, and Senior Director of Program Operations Beth Coty. Also in attendance were: Christina Barnes, Licensing Program Manager (LPM) and Lorena Valenzuela, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA). The following was discussed with the facility: -High number of complaints -Various personal rights violations -Staff training -Oversight of staff in cottages Regarding the high number of complaints, LPA Valenzuela and LPM Barnes have observed an increase in complaints in the last year regarding personal rights and supervision. LPM Barnes and LPA Valenzuela inquired about what steps the facility is taking to reduce the number of complaints. (Continued on page 2) Administrator Jessie Jorrin stated the facility is implementing a new training plan which will include licensing required training and an additional week for new employees to shadow staff in the facility, in which the new employee will get to observe and learn their job duties as well as make suggestions on how the facility can improve its processes. Administrator added that Quality Assurance Program Coordinator Marlo Felix is conducting more "check ins" with staff in the cottages. Mr. Felix stated, the management team is making unannounced visits to the cottages to provide support to staff. Mr. Felix stated, the facility reviews video footage of the cottages one to three times a week as a quality assurance measure. Furthermore, Mr. Felix stated he has covered cottage staff shifts to observe staff and provide onsite coaching, when necessary. Executive Director Lawren Ramos explained that they are currently restructuring the facility's administration roles and filling job positions to ensure there is more oversight/monitoring of staff. Administrator stated the human resources department has implemented an "open door" policy, so staff can report incidents and talk to administration with issues they may have. In addition, Administrator stated the facility is looking at cottages will a low record of incidents to model their best practices in other cottages. At the conclusion of the conference, LPM Barnes and LPA Valenzuela thanked the facility representatives. A copy of this report was emailed to Administrator Jessie Jorrin for signature. narrative: On January 28, 2021, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Lorena Valenzuela met with the Short-Term Residential Treatment Program (STRTP) Administrator Jessie Jorrin and Executive Director Lawren Ramos to discuss information received during a review of an incident that occurred at the STRTP facility. During the review of this incident the following information was obtained. LPA received video footage of Cottage 3B taken on 01/03/2021. LPA observed video footage taken at approximately 9:01 am showing Staff #2 (S2) and Child #3 (C3) in the living room area near the dining tables. After a verbal exchange between S2 and C3, LPA observed footage of S2 grabbing C3's right upper arm, forcibly pulling on C3's arm and subsequently grabbing C3's wrist to force C3 to sit down on a chair. C3 is observed attempting to stand up from the chair but S2 pushes C3 down to prevent C3 from standing. Shortly after, LPA observed footage of Child #2 (C2) approach C3 who was sitting on the chair. C2 is seen hitting C3's head several times with a closed fist. S2 is then observed pulling C2 away from C3, by performing a one-person restraint in which S2 grabs C2 by the shoulder and upper arm. LPA asked for written documentation of C2 and C3's physical altercation, as well as written documentation for the physical restraint S2 performed on C2 and C3. The facility was not able to find or produce written documentation of the incidents to Community Care Licensing. In addition, LPA reviewed video footage taken on 01/03/2021, at 9:12 am, showing Child #1 (C1) sitting at a table near the living room. Child #2 (C2) is observed sitting on the couch in the living room area. Staff #1 (S1) is observed standing in between the living room and table appearing to be having a verbal exchange with C1 and C2. LPA observed S1 approach C1 who was sitting in a chair and S1 is seen standing over C1 and talking to C1. LPA also observed S2 standing in the hallway facing the living room area. (continued on page 2) Moments later, C2 stands up from the couch walks toward S1 and C1. C2 is observed pushing C2's body against C1, while thrusting C2's knee in C1's direction at least four times. C2 is observed grabbing and pulling C1's hair and punching C1 with a closed fist. S2 is observed approaching C1, C2 and S1, grabbing C2 and placing C2 in a one-person restraint. S2 is observed physically restraining C2 and pulling C2 away from C1. C1 is observed being on the floor under the table. Moments later, Client # 4 (C4) which is standing near the table, approaches C1 and pulls on C1's arm, while attempting to hit C1. S2 and S3 are observed pulling C4 away from C1. LPA observed C2 returning towards C1 which is under the table appearing to be lying on the floor. LPA observed C2 using C2's feet to stomp (at least 4 times) on what appears to be C1's head. LPA also received witness statements which corroborated C2 stomped on C1's head. S3 is then observed performing a one-person restraint by pulling on C2's shirt and directing C2 away from C1 and into a seating area of the facility. C4 is then observed approaching C1 again and punching C1 while C1 lays on the floor under the table. After the physical altercation ended, C1 continues to sit on the floor under the table and S1 and S2 are seen putting C1 in a two- person restraint by grabbing C1 by the wrists and being pulled upwards. S1 and S2 are then seen escorting C1 into a room. On 01/05/2021, during an interview with C1 using a video conference application, LPA observed C1 to have injuries on C1's face. LPA observed bruising and swelling to C1's face, specifically in C1's left temple area. LPA also observed C1 to have a vertical imprinted linear mark on C1's left side of C1's face. LPA asked for written documentation of the incident involving C1, C2 and C4. LPA received an internal incident report written by S1; however, the report did not include the full details of the incident. The internal incident report failed to provide details about C1 being stomped on or that C1 suffered injuries. The incident report also failed to indicate that C1, C2 and C4 were placed in restraints. In addition, the facility reported to the LPA, that S1 had filled out an "ouch report", which is a report to notify the facility's medical department that a child sustained an injury. The facility was unable to find or produce the "ouch report" regarding C1's injuries. (continued on page 3) Based on review of video footage, the Department has determined there is a preponderance of evidence showing Staff #2 (S2) did not accord Child #3's (C3) personal right be accorded dignity in his or her relationship with staff, due to S2 pulling on C3's arm and forcing C3 to sit down in a chair. The facility is cited for violation of the Short- Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards (ILS), Version 3.1, Section 87072 (d)(10) Personal Rights. Based on review of video footage, the Department has determined there is a preponderance of evidence showing Staff #2 (S2) and Staff #3 (S3) did not follow the facility's Emergency Intervention Plan as outlined in the facility's Plan of Operation, which states "manual restraints require two trained staff". The facility is cited for violation of the Short- Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards (ILS), Version 3.1, Section 87022 (f) Plan of Operation. Based on review of video footage and interviews conducted, the Department has determined there is a preponderance of evidence showing S1, S2, and S3 did not ensure Child #1 (C1) was kept away from harm. S1, S2, and S3, did not prevent Child #2 (C2) and Child #4 (C4) from physically assaulting C1. Therefore, the facility did not ensure C1 was in a safe environment, where he or she is treated with respect. The facility is cited for violation of the Short- Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards (ILS), Version 3.1, Section 87072 (d) Personal Rights. Based on review of video footage, interviews conducted, and documentation gathered, the Department has determined there is a preponderance of evidence showing Staff #1 (S1) made false or misleading statements in the written internal incident report, which failed to include that on 01/03/2021, C1 was physically assaulted by C2 and C4, which resulted in C1 sustaining injuries. The facility is cited for violation of Title 22, Division 6, Section 80012 (a) False Claims. An exit interview was conducted. A copy of this report, LIC 809-D and Appeals Rights were provided to Jessie Jorrin

narrative: On December 9, 2020, Community Care Licensing (CCL) received a complaint alleging staff have not received trauma informed training and that the facility is out of ratio in terms of their staff to children ratio. It was also reported the facility ratio is "often 11 children to one staff". Regarding the allegation of staff not receiving training on being "trauma informed", confidential interviews revealed staff did not receive enough training to deal with the children's behaviors while practicing trauma informed care. LPA Valenzuela reviewed 17 staff training records for Cottage 2A. LPA discovered Staff #1 (S1) and Staff #2 (S2) did not receive trauma informed training in 2020, and both staff have been working at the facility for over two years. Regarding the allegation of facility being out of ratio, confidential interviews revealed the facility morning shift at Cottage 2A is often short staffed. Interviews revealed the facility staff to child ratio in the morning when children are awake is one staff to four children. Confidential interviews and documents review revealed that during the morning shift of 12/14/2020 to 12/19/2020 there was two staff to 12 children. Interviews revealed Staff #3 (S3) was scheduled to work that week but was unable to make it to work. The facility stated that there was another staff at the cottage to cover S3's shift, however, LPA asked for written documentation and the facility was not able to produce the documentation. Based on interviews and records review, there is a preponderance of evidence to prove facility Staff #1 and Staff #2 are not trained and facility is out of ratio. The allegations are, therefore, found to be substantiated. The facility is cited for violation of the STRTP Interim Licensing Standards (ILS), Section 87065.1 (c) (3) (t) Training Requirements and STRTP ILS Section 87065.5 (b) (1) (C) Direct Care Staff/ Child Ratios. Furthermore, witness statements indicated that there have been several times when staff was not able to pass out medications due to being short staffed. Based on interviews and records review conducted during the investigation, there is a preponderance of evidence to prove clients (C1, C2, C3) are not being given their medication(s) in a timely manner. The allegation is, therefore, found to be substantiated. The facility is cited for violation of Title 22, Division 6, Section 80075 (b)(5)(B) Health Related Services. An exit interview was conducted. narrative: On July 21, 2021, Licensing Program Manager (LPM) Christina Barnes, and Licensing Program Analysts (LPAs) Lorena Valenzuela and Jazmond Harris arrived at Childhelp Merv Griffin Village Short Term Residential Therapeutic Residential Program (STRTP). LPA's and LPM, were met and granted access by Executive Director Lawren Ramos. The purpose of the visit is to conduct an annual inspection of the facility. At 9: AM, Executive Director Lawren Ramos and Administrator Jesse Jorrin, led the physical inspection of the facility with LPM Barnes and LPA's Valenzuela and Harris. A physical plant inspection was completed and included the facility's, activity center, gaming room, swimming pool area, kitchen area, refrigerator/freezers, food storage areas, client cottages, bathroom/showers, and farm area. Facility grounds are clean and free of debris and observable hazards. Sports equipment/toys/books/games/computers were observed for children's recreation time. There is adequate indoor and outdoor activity space. Facility smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are in appropriate working order; fire extinguisher is properly charged and serviced. Licensee maintains an adequate supply of perishable and non-perishable foods and the menus were posted. All required forms are posted including the Grievance Procedures, Visitation Policies, Personal Rights form, and Foster Care Ombudsperson poster. Medications are locked and centrally stored inside staff's cottage offices. Individual beds were observed with appropriate clean linens, pillows, comforters, and mattresses in good repair. The hot water in the client's bathrooms was measured to be between 105 and 120 degrees. Per the Administrator, no firearms or weapons are allowed in the facility. The facility has a dining area, kitchen area, living room, open common area/formal living room, a clinician's office for therapeutic services, an entertainment room, and a room where the washer and dryer are located. All bedrooms have individual beds and drawer space for each client. The facility ensures that there is one client per bed with appropriate linens, pillows, comforters, and mattresses in good repair. Chemicals and/or poisons, sharp objects/knives are locked in a cabinet in the hallway closet. First Aid Kits are stored in a locked cabinet in the staff office. LPM and LPA's reviewed the facility's disaster and mass casualty plan. The facility has cameras in common areas of the facility. The facility has a waiver on file to use the cameras and are meeting the terms and conditions. Facility has a pool which is appropriately fenced and secured. The facility currently has two or more children sharing a bedroom in all Cottages. Based on observations, the facility is cited for violation of the Short- Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards (ILS), Version 4.1, Section 87087 (b)(1) Physical Grounds. The facility is required to provide locked containers with keys, for the purpose of storing contraceptives. Based on observations and interviews, the facility is not providing the locked containers for clients. The facility is cited for violation of STRTP ILS, Section 87075(b) (1) (A) Health Related Services. The facility does not have a signal system in place, which is a system to be used by children and staff to summon additional staff during an emergency. The facility is cited for violation of STRTP ILS, Section 87088 (e)(1) Fixtures, Furniture, Equipment , and Supplies. Due to time constraints, LPM and LPA's will return to complete the inspection at a later date. An exit interview was conducted and a copy of this report, and appeal rights were provided to Administrator Jesse Jorrin.

*This is an amended report of the report that was issued on 07/12/2021* On July 12, 2021, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Lorena Valenzuela met with Marlo Felix, Quality Assurance Coordinator, and Jesse Jorrin, Administrator to discuss information received during a review of an incident that occurred at the STRTP facility. The incident occurred on or around 03/24/2021, and involved Child #1 (C1), Staff #1 (S1), Staff #2 (S2) and Staff #3 (S3). See LIC 811, Confidential Names List form dated July 12, 2021. During interviews conducted, it was disclosed to LPA that facility staff (Staff #1, Staff #2, and Staff #3) did not allow Child #1 (C1) to eat a meal C1 obtained from a visit with a family member. Witness interviews revealed staff require children to eat at least two items from the meal provided by the facility before the children can eat the meal/food brought from outside of the facility. Additional interviews revealed C1 refused to eat the facility food, which resulted in staff not allowing C1 to eat C1's personal food. Witness interviews revealed C1 forcibly took the outside meal from staff and ran outside of the cottage with the outside food, where C1 ate the outside meal. Based on interviews and records review, the Department has determined there is a preponderance of evidence showing facility staff (S1, S2. S3) did not accord Child #1's (C1) personal right to have access to C1's personal belongings, due to S1, S2, and S3 denied C1's right to eat C1's personal food during a mealtime. The facility is cited for violation of the Short- Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards (ILS), Version 3.1, Section 87072 (d)(6) Personal Rights. An exit interview was conducted where the citation and plan of correction was discussed. A copy of this report, LIC 809-D, appeal rights and LIC 811 were provided to the Administrator, Jesse Jorrin.

On May 6, 2021, the Department received a complaint alleging that staff encouraged a minor to cause harm to another minor while in care. It was alleged that S1 told C2 to hit C1 for being bad. LPA was informed during confidential interviews that C1 took S1's purse and cellphone. S1 found C1 in possession of the cellphone and yelled "get him". It was further disclosed that C1 began to run and C2 caught C1 and hit him on the back. However, C1 did not remember how C1 obtained the cut to the lip. It was disclosed that C1 was acting up during the time of the incident and another child asked S1 if they could "get" C1 and S1 replied "yes". During interviews it was reported that staff did not remember C1 taking the cellphone or belongings of S1. S1 did not allow any child to hit or attack C1 and would not encourage a child to cause harm to another child. Interviews with CSW revealed that there was never a mention of this specific incident happening. CSW stated that C1 did not know the reason behind being hit. An additional allegation was received that a minor is being harmed by another minor while in care. It was alleged that C1 was hit by other children in the facility. LPA learned during confidential interviews that C1 was hit in the back by C2. Also, that there is always fighting in the cottage and that the "little kids" get punched in the face by the bigger kids. It was disclosed that children are told to separate when fighting and that no one remembers how or when C1 sustained the cut to C1 lip. CSW revealed that C1 did disclose that the other children in the facility were hitting C1. CSW also informed LPA that C1 was told to inform staff when being hit by the other children at the facility. CSW did inform LPA that C1 expressed feeling safe while at the facility. Based on interviews, the allegation that S1 told C2 to hit C1 for being bad and that C1 was hit by other children in the facility, may have occurred, however, is not supported by evidence. Therefore, the allegations are unsubstantiated at this time. An exit interview was conducted and a copy of this report, LIC 811, and appeal rights were given to Administrator Jesse Jorrin.

narrative: On October 28, 2021, an office meeting was held with Childhelp Merv Griffin Village Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Executive Director Chris Ruble per his request. In attendance were: LaCresha Cook , Regional Manager, Christina Barnes, Licensing Program Manager (LPM) and Lorena Valenzuela, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA). The purpose of the meeting was to discuss the regulation Section 87087 (b)(1) Physical Grounds, regarding having no more than 2 children in a bedroom. On 10/01/2021 and on 10/15/2021, the facility was cited for having more than two children in a bedroom and are continuing to accrue daily fines in form of civil penalties, until the violation is corrected. In regard to the "2 to a room" issue Executive Director Chris Ruble stated he plans to convert the therapist room located in each Cottage to a bedroom. The conversion will result in each Cottage having 4 bedrooms which will house 8 children per cottage. The facility will reduce its capacity to 48 children and use 3 buildings (6 cottages) to house 48 children and use one building (1 cottage) to house the therapists offices in the interim. Mr. Ruble stated the facility will work towards increasing the capacity to 64 once it finds a place where the therapist offices will be placed. Mr. Ruble stated he can make these changes while meeting children to staff ratios. Mrs. Cook agreed with the facility's plan. Mrs. Barnes reminded Mr. Ruble that while the conversion and changes are being implemented the facility will continue to be fined civil penalties daily until the facility is in compliance with the no more than two children to a room regulation. The Department will request a fire clearance, the facility will submit and updated Program Statement/Plan of Operation detailing the changes to the STRTP and updated facility sketch. In addition, the following was discussed with the facility: Administrator Duties - Facility is to provide Community Care Licensing (CCL) with notification of the staff designated to perform duties of the Administrator, when the Administrator is not present. narrative: On November 5, 2021, Licensing Program Analyst's (LPA's) Lorena Valenzuela and Valerie Wilson met with Childhelp Merv Griffin Village Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Facility Direct of Support Services Manny Barragan and Clinical Quality Coordinator Jessica Fox. In addition, the board meeting minutes did not reflect the board is discussing documents specified in Health and Safety Code 1520.1 (f) which includes documents such as licensing reports, program audit reports of its program operations, special incident reports, and any administrative action against its employees. narrative: On 08/10/ Licensing Program Analysts (LPAs) Stephannie Verna and Shoua Xiong arrived at the above facility and met with Joelle Gomez, facility Administrator, for the purpose of conducting a required unannounced annual inspection. The facility is licensed for 28 clients, and currently has a census of 21. The facility is comprised of three cottages: Alpine, Delta, and Shasta. There is also a main building and office building on the campus which hold the main lobby, staff offices, Human Resources office, and training department. LPA Verna inspected the cottages inside and out and the following was observed: The facility license, and emergency exit plans were posted in a prominent place. LPA observed working smoke alarms, and up-to-date fire extinguishers, and first aid kits with required supplies. There is one week of perishable foods and two weeks of non-perishables for the clients in each cottage. Each client has an individual or shared bedroom (with no more than two to a room), with a bed, clean linens and pillow(s), and furniture to store their belongings, dressers and closets. The clients had hygiene supplies, laundry supplies, and cleaning supplies properly stored and provided for use. There is a locked pool on the premises, which has a life guard on duty, and has fences at least five-feet high and constructed so that the fence does not obscure the pool from view. Sharps are stored in locked container in the kitchen or staff offices. Prescribed psychotropic and other medications were present, locked, and MARs were documented thoroughly. The cottages were clean and in good condition with the exception of pending repairs in Shasta Cottage pertaining to holes in the walls. Maintenance request orders have been submitted. No bugs were observed during the inspection. LPA Verna requested current youth rosters for each cottage, and Needs and Service Plans for two youth and facility provided the current Needs and Services Plans for the two youth to LPA. continued on 809-C LPA Xiong began reviewing 10 client files and observed that two clients did not have documentation of a TB test and its results, and three clients had documentation of going to get a TB test but there were no documents of the results. The facility is being cited for violations of the California Code of Regulations, Title 22, division 6, chapter 1, section 80069(c)(1) client medical assessments: (1) The results of an examination for communicable tuberculosis and other contagious/infectious diseases. LPAs were unable to complete the annual inspection on today's date. The inspection will be continued and completed at another date and time. Licensing Program Analysts (LPAs) Stephannie Verna and Shoua Xiong completed an exit interview. A copy of this report, along with the appeal rights, has been provided to Joelle Gomez, facility administrator.

narrative: Interviews and documentation reviewed were inconsistent that the facility followed their runaway policy and procedure as outlined in their Program Statement and runaway plan. Per the facility Program Statement and policy and procedures pertaining to youth AWOL/runaway, "When a student does run away...despite all efforts to prevent them, staff do the following: 1. Notify the Cottage Manager, Residential Clinician, Facility Manager or On-Call Administrator as soon as possible so a coordinated effort can be put into place to locate the student. 3. Follow the student off campus if possible and if safe. Attempt to verbally persuade them to come back using positive and encouraging reasons for them to return, i.e. "We want you to be safe." If the student does not respond to this approach, do not "chase" them, as this could potentially cause them to make poor decisions such as running into traffic, etc. 4. Drive around the surrounding neighborhood in search of the student if possible and if safe, in to persuade them to return. 5. Call local law enforcement once you lose sight of the student and have determined the student is not likely to be found or likely to return very soon."
