narrative: On 8/31/22, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Jessica Caplinger, conducted an unannounced inspection for the purpose of conducting a case management regarding reports of the bathrooms being locked. During two confidential interviews, it was reported that the bathrooms are kept locked. LPM Campos had observed the bathrooms locked during a previous inspection and when discussed with staff it was determined that it was a one time incident due to a youth destroying property in the bathroom. A Technical Violation for Interim Licensing Standards, Regulation 87072(c)(11) regarding Personal Rights is being issued. ILS 87072(c)(11) states that "The licensee shall ensure that each child, regardless of whether the child is in foster care, is accorded the personal rights specified in Welfare and Institutions Code Section 16001.9, as applicable. In addition, the licensee shall ensure that each child is accorded the following personal rights: To be free of physical, sexual, emotional, or other abuse, and from corporal or unusual punishment, *exploitation,* infliction of pain, humiliation, intimidation, ridicule, coercion, threat, mental abuse, or other actions of a punitive nature including, but not limited to, interference with the daily living functions of eating, sleeping, or toileting, or withholding of shelter, clothing, or aids to physical functioning." Locking the bathroom interferes with the child's toileting thus violating the child's personal rights. LPA met with Amy Whitlock, Cottage Manager, to review case management inspection report. Exit interview was conducted with Amy Whitlock, Cottage Manager and a final copy of this report was left at the facility.

the facility staff stated they didn't have enough staff to send someone to pick C1 up but did contact law enforcement for assistance. Documentation received from the facility indicates that the community member and/or the other individual who called on C1's behalf alerted the facility of C1's whereabouts at 6: PM but C1 was not picked up until 11: PM by Stockton Police Department. C1 was back at the facility by 11: PM. During confidential interviews, LPA was informed that staff in the cottages supervising youth were alone and could not leave the cottages. Staff indicate that the normal protocol would be to go pick youth up when called about their whereabouts but during this incident, they were pretty "short staffed" preventing them from being able to go get C1 due to staff calling out. LPA asked about individuals on call to go get youth or to come to the facility to substitute staff on shift and staff state that they were and continue to struggle with staffing due to the downsizing and closing of cottages along with high behaviors with other youth on campus. Staff indicated that usually there are staff to pick youth up but this day they were short the additional help they usually had. Further interviews with C1's county social worker indicates that it is the county's expectation that a youth would be picked up in a timely manner and having to wait several hours would not be acceptable, especially if youth are in the company of strangers or at risk as C1 was. LPA also reviewed the program statement and discovered that the Transportation section states "In the event a child or nonminor dependent runaway and then contacts the agency asking to return, the agency will make a reasonable effort to provide transportation for their return, assuming the authorized representative has not close the youth's bed." This did not happen in this incident. Based on interviews conducted, information obtained, documents received, and other documents reviewed the complaint that staff failed to pick up a client in a timely manner is SUBSTANTIATED, meaning that the "preponderance of the evidence" standard has been met. The facility was cited for Direct Care Staff/Child Ratios 87065.5(d)(1). The facility did not make an effort to pick C1 up from a community member's home for over five hours. The facility can be "temporarily be out of compliance with the direct care staff to child ratio" for emergencies or to follow a child during an unauthorized absence as long as replacement staff are called and can arrive at the facility within 30 minutes. LPA observed that it would have taken the facility staff six minutes to drive the distance to the community member's home and an additional six minutes to return to the facility meaning that they would have returned within the allotted 30 minutes specified in this regulation. Exit interview was conducted with Ms. Brown and documentation was provided to the facility. Community member stated that when the facility was contacted, the staff informed them that they did not have enough staff to come and pick up C1 but they had been in contact with law enforcement about C1 being picked up by them. When another individual with whom C1 was familiar also contacted the facility to alert the facility of the whereabouts of C1, they too were told that there were no available staff to pick C1 up. In review of the documentation provided by the facility, the facility was in ratio on the date of the incident, however, the regulation related to direct care staff to child ratios allows for the facility to be "temporarily out of compliance" during an emergency with a child or when following a child beyond the premises of the facility. As a result of the facility being in ratio at the time of the incident, the allegation that staff has an insufficient amount of staff is unsubstantiated meaning the allegation may have happened or is valid, but there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that the alleged violation occurred. LPA did advise the facility of the regulation related to ratios and did advise that the facility work with their assigned Licensing Program Analyst to ensure that the program statement reflects their understanding of this regulation and with the training staff to ensure that all staff are trained appropriately on implementation. Exit interview was conducted with Ms. Brown and documentation was provided to the facility.

narrative: Confidential interviews reveal that the identified client was 18 years old and was in placement at the facility for five years. The identified client was employed and was transitioning to an independent living placement. The identified client admitted to engaging in substance abuse during placement and voluntary attended an outpatient rehab program. The investigation revealed that the identified client left the facility the night before to drive a family member to work. The identified client returned to the facility after an hour and did not show any sign of being under the influence. The identified client showed another client three pills that were in a plastic baggie. The other client observed the identified client go to the bathroom and assumed the identified client took the pills. The identified client went to sleep and was found deceased the following morning by staff, who tried to wake up the client. A small plastic baggie with two and a half small blue pills was found in the identified client's pants pocket. Additional interviews and records reviewed showed no evidence to support the allegation. Staff regularly conduct room cleaning and room checks; staff never found any illegal drugs in the identified client's room. Staff will search clients' belongings if there is any suspicion of drug use. Staff conduct bed checks at night to make sure clients are in their bedrooms asleep and not AWOL. The police incident report did not suspect any foul play. The coroner's report is still pending but the cause of death indicated was "probable acute fentanyl toxicity" and the secondary cause as "cardiomegaly." Based on the above information, the allegation is closed as unsubstantiated due to the lack of preponderance of evidence to support it. A copy of the following reports were provided at the conclusion of the inspection: LIC9099, LIC9099-C and LIC Confidential Names. Appeal rights were provided and explained. There was no deficiency citation issued.

narrative: The question of whether or not a Program Supervisor was counted towards the staffing ratio was not made explicit by the documented statements obtained by LPA Eunice-McLean from children and staff-CRH management stated that whenever a scheduled Residential Counselor calls off, and no other previously unscheduled replacement can cover by the time the shift starts, the facility's Program Supervisor or Supervisor-on-Duty (SOD) leaves that position's post in the supervisor hub to slot in for the call-off at the dorm in need, ensuring that the ratio is met. It is reasonable that, because the children (or even some staff) may not understand this protocol as it happens, they may still describe the situation as being "short-staffed" simply because of the call-off; but the proper staffing ratio can still be met if a supervisor is present in that dorm. Such language is recurrent in several incident reports written by these direct-care Residential Counselor staff: i.e. "unable to shadow due to limited staff/being the only staff," etc.-particularly when documenting children who go AWOL (unauthorized absence or leaving of the facility). However, it is also consistently documented that a supervisor, program manager, or other supporting staff do attempt to follow absconding minors per the facility's program protocol. After further review, there is not enough corroboration among the obtained statements to definitively determine an actual out-of-ratio incidence, let alone regular occurrence. Based on the above, the preponderance of evidence standard has not been met; therefore, the allegations are found to be UNSUBSTANTIATED. Although the allegations may have happened or are valid, there is not a preponderance of evidence to prove the alleged violations did or did not occur. LPA observed four client bedrooms and one bathroom per dorm (each bathroom having two separate shower stalls and two toilet stalls) for a total of 16 client bedrooms matching the facility's current licensed capacity. LPA inspected and/or reviewed the following: LPA observed the proper posting of the facility's license and of the Foster Youth Personal Rights; disinfectants/cleaning solutions were secured and kept inaccessible from clients; the refrigerators' temperatures were at 39 and 38 degrees Fahrenheit, and the walk-in freezer temperature was at 0 degrees Fahrenheit; nonperishable foods were sufficiently in-stock for at least one week, and fresh perishable foods were observed to be on-hand sufficient for at least two days; menus were posted and showed an offering of alternative items; each dorm has at least one working landline telephone that clients reported they could use to make confidential phone calls; there were carbon monoxide detectors in all four dorms which were tested and found to be in good working condition; smoke detectors were also observed in all four dorms; there is a common room available for each dorm; the dining area was observed to have enough seating; the youths' medications were centrally stored, locked and inaccessible to the clients; hot water from taps used by youths were measured to be between 105-120 degrees Fahrenheit; fire extinguishers were placed throughout the facility in appropriate locations and were found to have been inspected within the past year; the toilets, wash basins/sinks, bath and shower fixtures were all in good repair; there was soap and paper towel supplies in the (, 809-C) restrooms; the youth bedrooms contained the required linen and furnishings; and no indication of rat or vermin infestation was detected; the disaster and mass casualty plan was posted and observed to be current; in the file review, staff training documentation was present, as well as verified criminal record clearances; documentation of personnel qualifications' verification was also observed; the Needs and Services Plans for the interviewed clients were found to be current and in compliance; the JV223 documents-where available-were also reviewed; separate Psychotropic Medication Administration Records were found where appropriate; based on client interviews, this facility utilizes trauma-informed practices in providing care and supervision to its youth. Regarding the allegation that Staff do not communicate with responsible party regarding minor's care, there is no standard of notifying an authorized representative to which the facility can be held regarding certain personal developments a youth experiences. And with respect to a medication administration issue, though staff did communicate with the responsible party about the matter, further clarification could have been made for the responsible party to better understand what had transpired. Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Misty Valencia and Bianca Mendez arrived unannounced for the purpose of a case management inspection, following a record review. As the facility is closed, LPAs met with and discussed the case management with former Lindsey Gunsauls, Asst Director (AD), and Sarah Perry former Director of the facility, at Children's Legacy Center Foster Family Agency, located at Cypress Ave., Redding, which is owned by the same licensee. During a meeting with the Department and the facility (STRTP) on June 26, 2024, a Harm Reduction policy was discussed, with regards to a former client's marijuana usage. Licensing Program Manager (LPM) Hillary Hall requested additional records which were received and reviewed by LPA Wendy Brown and LPM following the meeting client was placed at the facility with a history of substance abuse and unauthorized absences. During the meeting on June 26, 2024, the facility indicated that as a Harm Reduction measure, the facility allowed the client to smoke outside of the facility, as a means to encourage the client to remain on site, and not leave without permission to engage in unsafe behaviors of soliciting illegal substances from strangers in the community. LPM indicated this is not an approved Harm Reduction approach. After the meeting, the facility provided all records regarding the client's substance usage and harm reduction measures. The facility documented multiple incidents where the client left without permission, engaged in aggressive and unsafe behaviors, and used substances on the property and away from the property. Upon review of the records, the Department determined that during the client's two months in placement, there was one incident where the client asked for the client's marijuana which the staff had previously confiscated. The staff provided the client with "scraps" of marijuana which were so small, the client was unable to get them to light. On four occasions, the client smoked marijuana which they had acquired while away from the facility. The staff stayed near where the client was smoking outside of the facility, monitoring the client's safety, and encouraging the client to turn in the contraband. A total of two clients were placed in the facility between March 11, 2024 and May 20, 2024. A subsequent meeting was held with the facility on July 15, 2024 to discuss their future plan, and the facility voluntarily closed on July 19, 2024. No citation was issued at the time of this report as the facility is closed and a Plan of Correction could not be completed. Copy of this LIC 809 case management was provided to AD.

During an interview with RP, they reported that C1 had disclosed that staff had ransacked clients' bedrooms and stolen allowances. In interviews with clients C1-C5, three clients stated their money had been stolen or was missing. One of these clients stated their wallet went missing at school and then reappeared at the facility a few days later, but the money inside was missing. The second client whose money went missing stated they didn't see who had taken it but just "know" that it's a staff member, although no name was given. The third client stated that their money also went missing and believes it was staff because an X-Box controller had also gone missing. This third client stated they believe it was staff because a client wouldn't steal the controller. However, C1-C5 made consistent statements that staff do not ransack client bedrooms and only does bed checks. Consistent statements were made that bed checks consist of staff checking in to make sure clients were okay, and then leaving without doing much. In interviews with staff members S1, S2, S4, and S5, consistent statements were made that staff do not go into client's bedroom to "ransack" or go through client's belongings, taking their personal belongings. S1 stated that the client(s) who claimed that money had been stolen had then gone Absent Without Leave (AWOL) that evening and returned back with food and candies. S1 stated that when they spoke to the client over the telephone and asked about how client was able to purchase the food and candies if their money/allowance had been stolen, the client didn't answer and instead hung up the phone. Based on LPA's observations, interviews which were conducted, and records reviewed, the preponderance of evidence standard has not been met, therefore the above allegation is found to be UNSUBSTANTIATED. Although the allegation may have happened or is valid, there is not a preponderance of evidence to prove the alleged violations did or did not occur. No title 22 regulations were cited during today's inspection. Exit interview conducted and a copy of this report along with appeal rights was left with the Administrator, Raynisha McDonald.

narrative: On December 27, 2021 at 12: PM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Stephannie Verna arrived at the above facility to conduct an unannounced annual/required inspection of the facility. There are four out of six clients who share a bedroom, and do not have this documentation; Six out of six client files did not contain education goals on the Needs and Services Plans, Money Management, and Visitation or restrictions to visits, and are not individualized NSPs; The initial medical assessment does not include the ambulatory status of the clients; and Six out of six client files did not contain education goals on the Needs and Services Plans, Money Management, and Visitation or restrictions to visits, and are not individualized NSPs. On December 28, 2021 at 10: AM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Stephannie Verna arrived at the above facility to conduct an unannounced annual/required inspection of the facility. LPA Verna met with Angela Duhart, Assistant Administrator. LPA continued the annual/required inspection on today's date. LPA conducted four client interviews. One client refused to interview, and one client was not present. LPA completed four staff interviews. LPA reviewed the facility's emergency intervention, disaster preparedness plan, and plan of operations and found that the facility had all required pertaining documentation completed with the exception of disaster drill logs. The Administrator stated that a new drill binder was created after the old binder was destroyed. The facility stated that they conduct monthly drills, but current documentation for 2021 was not located or provided. LPA continued the review of client files, client medications and logs, and LPA observed that: One out of six client files did not contain the JV-220. The facility does not utilize or maintain a register of clients, containing the current necessary information; and Six out of six client files did not contain a standard appraisal form. The pool is located indoors in a covered sun room. The pool area was free of hazards, and the sliding door to the home was equipt with an audible alarm, which sounded non-stop when the door would open. The facility had weekly meal menus posted, and had healthy and available food options for youth to chose from. More than one week of non-perishable foods and two days of perishable foods were observed to be present in the facility fridge and pantry. Sharps and hazardous chemicals and cleaners were locked in the facility. The facility had necessary first aid supplies. Medications were stored in a locked closet and locked containers. During the visual inspection, LPA observed that: The hot water was tested at multiple sources and measured at 150 degrees F. The staff lowered the water heater setting and the water temperature will be tested again. One out of two carbon monoxide detectors (upstairs) was inoperable. The annual inspection was completed and finalized on today's date. The facility is being cited for deficiencies to the following regulations: Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) regulations, section 87070(b)(11); California Code of Regulations, Title 22, section 80088(e)(1); California Code of Regulations, Title 22, section 80023(d)(2); ILS regulations, section 87095.65(d)(1); California Code of Regulations, Title 22 section 80066(a)(12)(B); California Code of Regulations, Title 22, section 80066(a)(10); California Code of Regulations, Title 22, section 80066(a)(11); ILS regulations, section 87065.1(d)(7); ILS regulations, section 87065.1(c)(5); ILS regulations, section 87065.1(c)(6)(A); ILS section 87070(b)(15), and Health and Safety Code section 1503.2. See 809-Ds and Plan of Corrections for additional information. LPA Verna completed an exit interview with Angela Duhart, Assistant Administrator, and Raynisha McDonald, Administrator. A copy of this report and appeal rights was provided to Angela Duhart, Assistant Administrator, and Raynisha McDonald, Administrator. LPA Verna completed the staff file review, reviewing a total of ten staff files and observed that: Ten out of ten staff files did not contain training documentation for Emergency Intervention Staff Training; Six out of ten staff files did not contain documentation of the criminal record clearance or exemption received; Five out of ten staff files did not contain the LIC 198A, CACI check; The staff files did not contain staff evaluations; There is no signed documentation by STRTP staff regarding staff being over the age of 21 in the staff files; The personnel record was missing information including date of hire, and duties of the employee; Nine out of ten staff files did not contain a health screening report; Six out of ten staff files did not contain documentation of a TB test and its results; Multiple staff files reviewed did not contain education or experience information; Training assessments were not filed in ten out of ten staff files; Three out of ten staff files did not contain current CPR/First Aid completion certificates; and Documentation of training completed by staff was missing or incomplete in ten out of ten staff files. LPA Verna completed a visual inspection and walk-through of the facility. The facility sketch and license was posted in a prominent place. The facility is located in a rural location. LPA observed that the facility was clean, organized, and free of clutter. The facility is comprised of four bedrooms, two bathrooms, a kitchen and dining room, a living room, staff office, and a media/game room. The youth in care have ample space to conduct meetings with visitors, and complete homework or extracurricular activities. LPA tested and observed that the facility had working smoke detectors. One out of two carbon monoxide detectors (upstairs) was inoperable. LPA observed that the facility had multiple fire extinguishers, which were fully charged, and were serviced within the last year. The outside of the facility was free of potentially hazardous or dangerous items, and had ample space for outdoor activities. The facility had a large backyard and basketball court. There was a locked utility room for the pool pump and supplies, located outside.

LPA's observation, interviews conducted, and records reviewed were consistent that there were occasions that FC1 did not attend medical appointments and court hearings as scheduled. AD's statements corroborated that on one occasion the facility staff did not ensure FC1 attended a court hearing. Medical Documentation provided to the Department was reviewed and is consistent that FC1 did not attend all scheduled medical appointments as required or needed, and the facility was unable to provide documentation regarding proof of medical care FC1 received related to multiple injuries reported by facility staff in statements given. Additionally, while the facility staff obtained a dental appointment for FC1 after an injury, his treatment was not obtained and completed in a timely manner and while in care of the facility. Additionally, there were multiple incidents involving FC1 and/or other clients in care that the Department was not made aware of and/or was not reported to the Department as required per Title 22 and STRTP ILS regulations. Based on LPA observations, documentation reviewed, and interviews which were conducted, the preponderance of evidence standard has been met, therefore the above allegations are found to be SUBSTANTIATED. The facility is being issued two citations for deficiencies related to STRTP ILS Regulations, Personal Rights, section 87072(c) and CRC Title Regulations, section 80075(a). An exit interview was conducted with and a copy of this report and Appeal Rights were provided to Eric Mahan, Facility Manager. LPA's observation, interviews conducted, and records reviewed were inconsistent that the facility did not prevent injury to a youth in care and is not ensuring a safe environment for the youth in care. Based on multiple interview statements, an injury was sustained by FC1 during rough housing with another client in care and in the presence of facility staff. AD stated they needed to cover the fireplace to prevent it from happening again, but there is inconsistent information regarding verbal or other redirection given or not given by staff present during the incident that may have prevented the injury from occurring. Additionally, the facility reported an incident, involving FC1 and Law Enforcement searching the facility for weapons but there were no weapons located. Also, the facility was observed to have property damage, including broken windows. All incidents of property damage have not been reported by facility staff to the Department, and therefore a review of Incident Reports, photographs, visual observations, and statements given by individuals interviews were inconsistent in regard to date(s) when the damage to the windows occurred. Interview statements and subsequent observations showed that repairs to the windows were made by the facility, but in an untimely manner. Based on LPA interviews conducted, and records reviewed, the preponderance of evidence standard has not been met, therefore the above allegations are found to be UNSUBSTANTIATED. Although the allegation may have happened or is valid, there is not a preponderance of evidence to prove the alleged violations did or did not occur. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this report was provided to Eric Mahan, Facility Manager.

Confidential interviews were conducted with eleven individuals and attempted with one individual during the period of 11/21/2022 to 06/23/2023. Multiple statements gathered during interviews were consistent that grocery and household items are purchased and stocked in the facility, and that food is of good quality, however documentation reviewed were inconsistent regarding the quality of food being served to clients in care. Receipts were requested for purchases made during the months of September 2022 to December 2022 pertaining to groceries and household item purchases, allowance/gift card purchases, and costs and purchases made for repairs. The facility provided the Department with a total of three receipts, for months September, October and December 2022. One of three receipts provided to the Department included a purchase for alcohol. Copies of meal menus were requested for all weeks included in the months September 2022 - December 2022 and the facility provided the Department with a meal menu for the week of December 26, 2022 - January 1, 2023. The facility was unable to provide additional requested documentation to the Department regarding food service compliance, and LPA was unable to determine if the required amounts of food were purchased by the licensee for the total number of clients in care. Additionally, a Solvency Audit was conducted and finalized on June 07, 2023 by Jacqueline Juarez, Auditor, which indicated that the licensee is making sufficient income to meet operating expenses; however, funds are not being managed to ensure solvency. This was evident based on information gathered regarding the licensee accessing a local Food Bank for food items for clients in care. Based on interviews provided and documentation review, including two invoices for the Food Bank, LPA could not determine the quality of food or how the food items are selected, stored, prepared and served. Three additional grocery receipts submitted to the Department showed the licensee utilized a community membership club to obtain groceries for the youth in care as well and it is unclear why the licensee utilizes the Food Bank. Based on interviews conducted and LPA's review of documentation, along with the findings of the Department's Solvency Audit, the Department was unable to determine that the licensee is in full compliance with the food service requirements set forth in Title 22 regulations. continued on 9099-c USDA Guidelines for ages 14-19 averaged for male and female, amount for December 2022 is $277.10 per person. The total amount to be spent for eight clients is $2,216.80. The amount calculated from bank statements and food bank receipts totaled $323.07. Licensee's total amount spent equated to $40.38 per client. The Licensee underspent on food provisions by <$1,893.73>. Based on LPA observations, documentation reviewed, and interviews which were conducted, the preponderance of evidence standard has been met, therefore the above allegations are found to be SUBSTANTIATED. The facility is being issued one citation for deficiencies related to CCR Title Regulations, section 80076(a), Food Services. An exit interview was conducted, and a signed copy of this LIC-9099 report, LIC-9099D and the Appeal Rights were provided to the facility. LPA's observation, interviews conducted, and records reviewed were inconsistent that staff are not providing adequate supervision. Statements given during interviews regarding staff's level of supervision of clients in care were consistent that multiple staff are present in the facility and supervise the clients in care, as well as conduct periodic room checks when clients are in their bedrooms. However, levels of supervision were stated to vary between clients in care based on if a client exhibits unsafe behavior. For clients who exhibit unsafe behaviors, staff may increase the number of staff present or increase the frequency of supervision and/or room checks for specific clients. Based on LPA interviews conducted, and records reviewed, the preponderance of evidence standard has not been met, therefore the above allegations are found to be UNSUBSTANTIATED. Although the allegation may have happened or is valid, there is not a preponderance of evidence to prove the alleged violations did or did not occur. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this report was provided to Raynisha McDonald, Administrator.

narrative: The Department's Audit Section conducted a Solvency Audit pertaining to the allegations: the facility is in financial distress and the Facility Administrator is misusing funds. The audit was finalized on June 07, 2023, by Jacqueline Juarez, Auditor and concluded "Based on the documentation and information provided, the Licensee does not have a sound financial plan as described in Section 80062. As of March 2023 utilities were not being paid timely, and food receipts submitted show amounts spent on food were inadequate to meet the USDA guidelines. During the period of September 2022 multiple loans were taken out, bank statement provided for the same period had a low beginning and negative ending balances, with overdrafts. The audit report also indicated that the licensee is making sufficient income to meet operating expenses and licensee is current with payroll; however, funds are not being managed by the licensee to ensure solvency. Based on the Department's Solvency Audit findings, as well as LPA's observations, interviews conducted, and documentation and records reviewed, the preponderance of evidence standard has been met, therefore the above allegations are found to be SUBSTANTIATED. The licensee is being issued two citations for deficiencies related to CCR Title 22 section 80062(a), Finances; and section 80063(a), Accountability. An exit interview was conducted, a signed copy of this LIC-9099 report, LIC-9099D and the Appeal Rights were provided to the facility. LPA's observation, interviews conducted, and records reviewed were consistent that minors have engaged in physical altercations in the facility, however inconsistent regarding a lack of staff supervision or use of interventions to prevent or stop a physical altercation within the facility. Based on multiple interview statements, when clients display unsafe behaviors, such as verbal or physical aggression, staff redirect clients with verbal cues, offer coping skills, separate clients, and de-escalate unsafe behavior with additional interventions as necessary to ensure the safety of youth in care. Clients receive supportive services within the facility to address the aggressive or unsafe behaviors and youth goals related to decreasing unsafe behaviors are documented on their Needs and Services Plans. During instances of imminent danger to self or others, staff contact Law Enforcement for support and/or utilize physical interventions. Additionally, based on a review of documentation, including Incident Reports, the facility submitted Incident Reports regarding physical altercations of clients in care, as well as Law Enforcement Reports when Law Enforcement was contacted to assist staff in de-escalating clients in a physical altercation with staff or peers. Based on LPA interviews conducted, and records reviewed, the preponderance of evidence standard has not been met, therefore the above allegations are found to be UNSUBSTANTIATED. Although the allegation may have happened or is valid, there is not a preponderance of evidence to prove the alleged violations did or did not occur. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this report was provided to Raynisha McDonald, Licensee.

On February 5, 2021, CCL received an allegation of Staff member (S1) had an inappropriate relationship with group home minor(s) (C1). Specifically, it was reported that S1 "hooked up" with either C1 or C2. Record review revealed on February 19, 2021, S1 was booked into the Las Colinas Detention Facility on nine felony counts regarding the inappropriate relationship S1 had with C1. Record review revealed several inappropriate text messages and voicemails sent between S1 and C1. Record review and confidential interviews revealed that S1 was the only staff on duty over nights at the facility at which time the inappropriate interactions between S1 and C1 occurred. Confidential interviews report S1 sent C1 inappropriate pictures on at least one occasion. Confidential interviews confirmed an ongoing relationship occurred between S1 and C1 beginning in October or November 2020. Based on confidential interview and record review, the allegation Staff member (S1) had an inappropriate relationship with group home minor(s) (C1) is substantiated. The preponderance of evidence standard has been met. Facility is cited and an immediate civil penalty was issued for violation of Interim Licensing Standards 87072(d)(11) Personal Rights. narrative: On April 29, 2021 at 11:00 am, Associate Governmental Program Analyst (AGPA) Kim Robinson met with the Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) administrator, Yoshita Conrad, to assess an Enhanced Civil Penalty (ECP). On March 23, 2021, the Department concluded a complaint investigation alleging that Staff #1 (S1) (See the Confidential Names List, LIC 811, dated April 29 2021) engaged in sexual acts with fourteen-year-old client #1 (C1). S1 acknowledged performing lewd and lascivious sexual acts with C1 during multiple encounters, inside and outside the STRTP. The allegations were substantiated and the STRTP was cited under the Interim Licensing Standards, Section 87072(d)(11) Personal Rights. S1 willfully participated in multiple lewd acts with C1 by use of S1's employment with the STRTP Based on the analysis of the interviews, the Department has determined that an enhanced civil penalty is warranted for the physical abuse. The Penal Code section 288a (b)(1) and 288a(b)(2) define sexual conduct with a minor as physical abuse. This section describes a number of more or less direct and (always) willful acts that constitute sexual assault. Pursuant to the Enhanced Civil Penalty law, Health and Safety (H&S) code section 1548 (f)(1)(c), the Department will be issuing an immediate civil penalty of $2,500.00. An exit interview was completed, and appeal rights discussed. A copy of this report, the Confidential Names List, Appeal Rights, and a Civil Penalty Assessment - Serious Bodily Injury/Physical Abuse (Form 421-D) were provided to the administrator.

On 06/21/2021 at 9: AM Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Marisol Lopez arrived at the above facility for the purpose of conducting an Annual Inspection. LPA met with Program Manager Freddy Mancias and inspected the facility inside and out. The facility consists of a one story four-bedroom, two bathroom building with a staff sitting room/office, living room two hallways, laundry room, kitchen, dining area and two car garage. Bedroom #1 is occupied by one client; it contains one twin bed, all required linen, mattress, closet space and dresser with enough space for clients belongings. Bedroom #2 is not occupied; it contains two twin beds, all required linen, closet space and two dressers with enough space for two clients belongings. Bedroom #3 is occupied by one client; it contains two twin beds, all required linen, closet space and two dressers with enough space for two clients belongings. Bedroom #4 has an attached bathroom and is occupied by one client; it contains two twin beds, all required linen, closet space and two dressers with enough space for two clients belongings. A physical plant inspection was completed and included the following checks: Facility grounds are clean and free of debris and observable hazards. There is adequate indoor and outdoor activity space. Sports equipment/books/games were observed for client's recreation time. LPA observed sufficient perishable food for six clients for two days and seven days of non-perishable foods and appears to be following the posted menu. LPA tested the water temperature which measured 117.0 degrees Fahrenheit(F) which is within the acceptable range of 105 degrees and 120 degrees F. The living room hallway contains a locked closet which contains sharp knives, medications are locked and centrally stored in the locked closet inside a locked tool box. Licensee has provisions for contraceptives to be held in individually locked containers by clients. Individual beds were observed with appropriate clean linens, pillows, comforters, and mattresses in good repair. The laundry room contains a washer and dryer with built-in cabinets and a utility sink. The living room contains a large screen TV, two couches and a dining area with seven chairs. LPA observed the bathrooms were clean and in good repair. In the garage LPA observed a second fridge, a locked medications refrigerator, locked cabinets with tools, chemicals and poisons, and storage area. All hazardous items were made inaccessible to residents. Cleansers and chemicals were stored in a locked garage cabinet. The facility's smoke detectors located in each of the bedrooms and the living room and hallway were checked and were operable. The carbon monoxide detector located in the hallway area was tested and is in operable condition. The single fire extinguisher housing is located next to staff office and has a current inspection tag. The following required posted items were observed and accessible to children: Ombudsman Poster, Foster Youth Bill of Rights, Grievance Procedures, Personal Rights, and current menu. LPA observed that the personal rights was updated to meet the current Interim Licensing Standards (ILS). Per facility staff, no firearms or weapons are allowed in the facility. Facility appears to be meeting the terms and conditions of their license. Licensee has obtained National Accreditation through CARF and the Accreditation is valid through November 2021. LPA discussed the following with the Program Manager: Incident reporting, including incidents related to Assembly Bill 388 law enforcement contacts as well as incidents involving emergency interventions. Personnel Files are maintained off-site and transported to LPA within reasonable time. All appropriate personnel who require caregiver background checks have received criminal record and child abuse index check clearances or exemptions. A review of client records was also completed on this date including the Medication Administration Record (See Confidential Name List- LIC 811 dated on June 21, 2021). Personnel files were reviewed to ensure they contained all required documentation. Children and staff records are organized. Staff's CPR and First Aid card were current. Child's records contain original needs and services plan signed by the child and their authorized rep. Child's records contain authorization for emergency medical care signed by each child's authorized rep. Licensee has a current needs and services plan for each resident on file. Facility personnel meet staff training requirements Program Administrator is present at the facility a minimum of 20 hours a week, as verified by staff schedule. Appropriate staff/client ratios were verified during this inspection. Based on observations made during the inspection, no deficiencies observed during today's visit. An exit interview was conducted and this report was reviewed with Program Manager Freddy Mancias and a copy of this report was provided.

On June 29, 2021, an office conference was held with Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) provider, Circle of Friends (COF) via Microsoft Teams, due to COVID-19 pandemic. In attendance were: Community Care Licensing representatives Regional Manager (RM) LaCresha Cook, Licensing Program Manager (LPM) Ann Valenzuela, LPM Stephanie Hudak, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Marisol Lopez, LPA Danielle Garcia; COF representatives- Program Administrator Yoshita Conrad; San Diego County Representatives included: Senior Deputy Probation Officer Maria Arreola, Supervising Probation Officer Yovana Cortez, Institutions Evaluation Unit (IEU) Child Welfare Protection Services Supervisor Eileen Marshall, IEU Manager Natasha Hood, IEU/Contracts Supervisor Lyn Worthington, and IEU Contract Monitor Susan Hayes. The following issues were discussed: Complaints Law Enforcement Contacts Extension for the Provisional STRTP license During the meeting, LPM Valenzuela addressed that this meeting is to support and discuss how CCL and San Diego County can assist the facility in avoiding health and safety issues and to discuss the provisional STRTP license. LPM Valenzuela discussed the recent increase in complaints and requested information on what the facility has changed; how the facility is incorporating resources to assist with difficult clients and how staff is being trained. (see continuation form LIC809-C dated 06/29/21) In response, the facility representative responded with an explanation of difficulties the facility had in obtaining assistance from the social worker when working with extremely difficult clients. It was discussed how the facility will use their resources and elevate contacts when having a difficult time obtaining answers. The facility was made aware there is no further extensions after 24 months. RM Cook inquired about what the facility is doing to support staff's and clients wellbeing, including self-care and trauma informed training. The facility discussed having a therapist on site available for clients, having a recent additional trauma informed care training and providing staff time-off as needed. The facility highlighted the importance of staff wellness and the encouragement for self-care. All recommendations/suggestions and requirements given during the meeting by CCL were acknowledged by STRTP representatives. County and CCR representatives had no recommendations to add. In closing, all parties were satisfied with all information that was discussed during the meeting. Program Administrator Yoshita Conrad designated Program Representative Kathryn Rimington to sign receipt of the report and meet with LPA via tele-inspection to answer any questions. narrative: On 06/03/2021, the Department received an allegation that due to a lack of staff supervision minor ingested pills resulting in death, client has access to weapons, client caused injury to another client in care, staff are not providing adequate supervision to clients, staff did not provide a safe environment to clients in care and staff did not report incidents. Confidential interviews stated the facility is limited to conducting searches and putting hands on the clients however the facility has taken measures to prevent the clients from entering the facility with alcohol and contraband by conducting routine checks. Confidential interviews stated staff were unaware that minor #1(M1) ingested street drugs prior to M1's shower and staff was unable to provide immediate first aide because it is underdetermined how long M1 was unresponsive prior to Paramedics and Fire Department arriving. Confidential interviews stated the facility has recently added additional staff to maintain continuous supervision of clients. Confidential interviews stated staff conduct room searches when it is suspected the individual client is in possession of an illegal substance, cigarettes, weapons, or belonging of others. Confidential interviews stated clients have been involved in physical altercations with each other however staff follow the emergency intervention plan and intervene to the best of their ability by placing their bodies between clients to de-escalate clients and law enforcement is contacted as a last resort however, the clients have rights and it would be a violation on the facility staff to search or place hands on clients or their personal belongings without the clients consent. Confidential interviews stated staff actively supervise and conduct 10-15 minute random night checks however when a client is AWOL, staff are unaware of clients behaviors or actions until they are reported by law enforcement or other. Confidential interviews stated all incidents that occur at the facility are reported to the appropriate parties including AWOL's. Confidential interviews stated during an AWOL attempt, staff follow the emergency intervention plan, staff follow client until staff lose sight of client, staff drive around looking for client, staff contact law enforcement and staff report AWOL's to appropriate parties. Confidential interviews stated staff meet with social workers and work with client to come up with behavioral contracts or incentives. Confidential interviews stated staff are limited to verbal interventions to stop an AWOL and bad behaviors and cannot physically restrain clients. Confidential interviews stated the facility provides a safe environment to clients in care however other witnesses allege otherwise. Confidential interviews contradicted the information provided and denied the allegations occurred however; other information provided alleged the incidents occurred. Based on confidential interviews, the allegations that due to a lack of staff supervision minor ingested pills resulting in death, client has access to weapons, client caused injury to another client in care, staff are not providing adequate supervision to clients, staff did not provide a safe environment to clients in care and staff did not report incidents may have occurred, however are not supported or proven by evidence. Therefore, the allegations are unsubstantiated. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this signed report was provided to Program Administrator, Yoshita Conrad.

narrative: On May 3, 2023, at 8: AM Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Lucero Jauregui conducted an unannounced annual facility inspection. LPA met with Nicole Wilson, Facility Representative who provided LPA with a guided indoor and outdoor tour of the facility. The facility is a four-bedroom, two-bathroom one story home with a living room, dining room, kitchen, staff office, laundry room, two car garage, and small back patio. The living room was observed to have two couches, a TV, board games, and ample space for activities. The living room contained hallway closet that was observed to be locked. The dinning room connects with living room and dinning table was observed with six chairs. The kitchen area was observed to be clean and no observable hazards. LPA observed sufficient perishable food for six clients for two days and seven days of non-perishable foods. Bedrooms one and three serve one client. Bedroom two serves two clients with a bathroom and shower, and bedroom four serves two clients. All beds were observed with appropriate clean linens, pillows, comforters, and mattresses in good repair. The closet in the hallway contained towels for client use. The bathroom located in the hallway was observed clean and in good repair. The laundry room contains washer, dryer, with built-in cabinets and a utility sink. LPA observed cabinets to have extra blankets and linens for client use. The garage is always maintained locked. LPA observed two couches, and small desk that is utilized for therapy sessions. Sharps, detergents, and chemicals are maintained in a locked cabinet in the garage. LPA observed locked lockers for client use. LPA observed a second refrigerator in working condition and in good repair. Continued..... A physical plant inspection was completed and included the following checks: Facility grounds are clean and free of debris and observable hazards. There is adequate indoor and outdoor activity space. Sports equipment/toys/books/games were observed for children's recreation time. All facility smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are in appropriate working order; fire extinguisher is properly charged and serviced located in the staff office. LPA tested the water temperature which measured 117.0 degrees Fahrenheit(F) which is within the acceptable range of 105 degrees and 120 degrees F. First aid kit is centrally stored in the living room closet with all required items. Medications are centrally stored in a locked toolbox in the locked living room closet. Per staff there are no firearms in the home. LPA observed the following items posted Personal Rights, Grievance Procedures, Visitation Policy, Facility sketch, Activity Schedule, Menu, Staff Schedule and Emergency Plan. Personnel Files are maintained off-site and transported to LPA within reasonable time. LPA reviewed five staff files and six client files. All appropriate personnel who require caregiver background checks have received criminal record and child abuse index check clearances or exemptions. Based on observations made during the inspection, no deficiencies were observed during today's visit. An exit interview was conducted with Enrique Hernandez, Facility Representative. A copy of this report along with appeal rights was provided to Enrique Hernandez, Facility Representative.

On August 31, 2020, at 11: AM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Belinda Torres conducted a Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) pre-licensing inspection. The LPA met with Rafik Philobos, Executive Director. The licensee is temporarily relocating from the Community Access Network (CAN) facility number 336426251, Steps STRTP located at Tava Lane Riverside, CA 92505 to this facility. The CAN Steps STRTP has a septic system failure. The clients can no longer be present due to health and safety issues. The licensee expects to complete the relocation move within the next two weeks. Let it be noted the street name for this facility is spelled incorrectly and was corrected yesterday to Briarwood Dr. The correction takes up to 48 hours to update in the CCL database. The facility is a two story residential building with four bedrooms and three bathrooms. The facility is currently unfurnished. On the first floor, there is one bedroom, one staff office with a staff restroom, kitchen, dining area, great room, and laundry room. There is a two car attached garage. In addition, there is a separate casita with one bedroom and one bath. The casita is used for the corporation's foster family agency storage. The clients will not have access to the casita. A physical plant inspection was completed with Rafik. The LPA observed the following: Facility grounds are clean and free of debris, observable hazards, and insects. The LPA observed an approximately 4" x 5" hole in the wall and the window blinds were missing a slat in bedroom #6 (second floor). The hole was patched during this inspection. There was no screen on the staff office window (first floor) There is adequate indoor and outdoor activity space. All facility smoke detectors and the one carbon monoxide detector downstairs were tested and observed to be in working order. A fire clearance is still needed. Per Rafik, the facility has an operating telephone line but there was no phone equipment to test the line. The LPA called the number, (951) 277-0016, and it appeared to be operating. The hot water was tested and measured to be 115 degrees Fahrenheit downstairs and Fahrenheit upstairs. The downstairs water temperature is in the required range of 105-120 degrees Fahrenheit, however the upstairs was not. The water heater temperature was adjusted during the inspection from the "very hot" setting to the "hot" setting. Per Rafik, no firearms or dangerous weapons will be kept or allowed in the facility. Smoking is prohibited. *** *** The LPA informed Rafik of the Interim Licensing Standards, Articles 1-10, 87088(e)(2) and (f) Fixtures, Furniture, Equipment, and Supplies which states the following facilities shall maintain a signal system which meets the requirements specified in (e) and (f) below. Such system shall be used by children to summon staff during an emergency: (2) All facilities having separate floors and not providing full-time staff on each floor whenever children are present. (f) The signal system shall have the ability to meet the following requirements: (1) Operation from each children's living unit. (2) Transmission of a visual and/or auditory signal to a central location, or production of an auditory signal at the specific children's living unit which is loud enough to summon staff. (3) Identification of the specific children's living unit from which the signal originates. Rafik stated the facility will have a full-time staff on each floor whenever children are present. Once the facility has relocated, the licensee will ensure that photos will be sent to LPA Torres including but not limited to: Furniture, fixtures and equipment. Locked storage for personnel files, client files, medications, sharps and client funds. The following required forms posted in the facility: Weekly Menu, Personal Rights form, and Foster Care Ombudsman poster. Each of the four client bedrooms having proper lighting, adequate drawer space, beds with appropriate clean linens, pillows, blankets, comforters, mattress pads, and mattresses in good repair. A fully equipped first aid kit and a current first aid manual approved by the American Red Cross. Hot water reading for the second floor bathroom. The following documents will be sent to LPA Torres: Updated LIC Facility Sketch reflecting the usage for each room, dimensions and exits. Updated LIC Application For A Community Care Facility with the current facility telephone number and the correct facility number and licensing agency for question #14. Control of property. On July 27, 2022, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA), Lisi Leon, met with Community Access Network Steps 2, CEO, Rafik Philobos, to provide a copy of the technical violation issued on 07/20/2022. LPA met with CEO at Community Access Network FFA/STRTP Headquarters located at: S Main St, Suite 201, Corona, CA 92882.

Regarding the allegation that facility staff did not follow the Emergency Intervention Plan to prevent minors from AWOLing, information gathered from interviews stated that facility staff are trained and go over the emergency intervention procedures in accordance with their plan of operation. Confidential interviews disclosed that facility staff attempts to redirect clients and engage in other activities when they express that they want to AWOL. In addition, confidential interviews stated that staff will follow clients in care until they lose sight of clients. Other interviews revealed that staff will go over the emergency plan with resident clients in care. Other information received stated that staff were not always following their emergency intervention plans resulting in client's chronic AWOL. Regarding the allegation that the facility is allowing minor unapproved visits in care, confidential interviews stated that clients at times would not follow program rules and would invite unauthorized visitors to the facility. Information obtained from confidential interviews stated that the facility staff would contact law enforcement to report when unauthorized visitors were at the facility while other confidential interviews stated staff would allow unauthorized visitors to come to the facility. Regarding the allegation that group home minors are intoxicated while in care, confidential interviews confirmed that minors are intoxicated while in care however it is upon returning from AWOL's. Additional information gathered stated that when clients are absent from care they may sometimes return to the facility under the influence. Staff will offer clients medical attention and will contact law enforcement if staff cannot talk clients down from intoxication. Additional information gathered from interviews denied the allegation that clients get intoxicated in the facility or under the supervision of staff. Based on interviews and confidential information obtained during the course of this investigation, LPA received inconsistent information regarding the allegations. The allegations that facility staff did not follow the Emergency Intervention Plan to prevent minors from AWOLing, facility is allowing minor unapproved visits in care, and group home minors are intoxicated while in care, may have occurred, however is not supported, or proven by evidence. Therefore, the above allegations are unsubstantiated at this time. Exit interview conducted and a copy of the report along with appeal rights were provided to Administrator Assistant, Guadalupe Arellano.

Based on observations, interviews, and record reviewed, the facility is being cited for violation of Title 22, Division 6, Chapter 1, Article 07 (a) The facility shall be clean, safe, sanitary and in good repair at all times for the safety and well-being of clients, employees and visitors. The Department received a complaint on July 28, 2020, that a staff member stole money from the facility and a staff member violated group home minors' rights for safety in the group home. Specifically, there was a suspicion that staff (S1) had stolen some of the money from the home. It was also alleged that one of the minors stated that (S1) had taken a client and another minor while purchasing bullets for S1's gun. It was also reported that a client saw the gun but did not have access to it. On July 31, 2020, S1 submitted a resignation letter to the facility via email that indicated S1 submitted a formal letter of resignation from the position of Child Care Worker and decided to resign from the facility. S1 denied the allegations. S1 stated S1 is no longer working for the group home because S1 has another job. S1 reported S1 did not know where the money was kept. S1 reported other staff did have access to the money anytime for client requests. S1 reported $300 was stolen from the facility before S1 resigned, and no one was held accountable for it. S1 stated staff at the facility reported clients were always breaking into the office taking cash. S1 reported S1 received a call from the police, and S1 reported to them S1 had nothing to do with it. S1 reported S1 has never brought any clients with S1 to purchase ammunition or showed them a gun. S1 stated S1 did not have any problems with any other staff or residents that would want to retaliate against S1. S1 reported S1 has another job and no need to steal money. S1 stated S1 was working 90 hours per week with both jobs and it was too much for. STRTP administrators reported that S1 was placed on administrative leave before his resignation due to multiple concerns, including crossing boundaries. It was reported that S1 was not a good fit for the facility. STRTP administrators reported the money was noticed stolen before S1 resigned. Witnesses reported there were no issues with staff taking money from the residents. Witnesses reported there was no issue with staff taking residents to buy ammunition or showing them a gun. It was reported that there were no problems with staff or residing at the facility; it was just boring there. Additional witnesses reported they were not aware of any staff stealing money. It was reported that staff could keep clients' money if they want, it is optional. Confidential interviews reported they feel safe at the facility. () The lead facility manager (LFM) reported no assigned person was solely in charge of where the cash was kept. LFM reported that S1 had access to the locked location where the money was kept. LFM stated to his observations in just understanding what took place but not actually seeing S1 take the money; S1 took the money on the last day worked and never returned to the facility. LFM reported LFM believes the amount stolen was approximately $125-$150, definitely over $100 and was mainly the clients' allowances. LFM stated S1 took all the money from the locked location. LFM stated they noticed the money was missing the next day. S1 worked the PM shift, in which, to LFM's knowledge, the money was taken that night and was noticed missing the next day. The LFM reported LFM is not aware of any concerns regarding S1 taking the clients to buy bullets. CSW's reported clients had no complaints regarding the facility. Some clients may have felt the consequences for their actions were too harsh, but nothing regarding money being stolen or weapon involvement. CSW's reported none of the assigned clients at the facility ever reported concerns about money being stolen or staff involving clients around a gun or purchasing bullets. CSW stated that the assigned clients were protective of their money and said something if there was concern at the facility. Additional CSW's reported there was never any mention about being placed at the facility, specifically no concerns regarding the allegations of money being stolen or personal rights violations. Based on confidential interviews and record reviews, the allegations that a S1 stole money from the facility and S1 violated group home minors' rights for safety in the group home may have occurred; however, they are not supported or proven by evidence. Therefore, the allegations are unsubstantiated at this time. An exit interview was conducted, appeal rights explained, and a copy of this report was provided to Kelsey Gomez.

Administrator stated that the incident began when two facility clients (C3 and C4) were denied use of another client's (C2's) personal gaming system. narrative: On November 04, 2024, the Department received a complaint alleging that the STRTP did not prevent a physical altercation between clients, allowing a verbal argument to escalate. It was further alleged that a client sustained injuries during the altercation and that the STRTP did not provide medical care for an injured client. Furthermore, It is alleged that facility staff allow clients to smoke marijuana in the home. LPA's investigation revealed that on November 1, 2024, there was an argument between clients C1 and C2 of the STRTP. C1 and C2 were engaged in a verbal argument in the living room downstairs, with S4 attempting to de-escalate. C1 had a home-made weapon, C2 picked up a chair to shield himself. C3 and C4 were upstairs outside their bedrooms, C3 tossed a desk fan towards C1. Law enforcement was called. A second flare-up between same participants occurred the following day, again staff de-escalated and averted physical altercations between C1 and C2. Staff denied that they allowed a physical altercation between clients, stating they were present and were de-escalating both clients verbally, and that a physical altercation was averted by S4 by walking C1 away from the danger zone and confiscating the weapon. Staff denied client was not provided medical attention. Staff disclosed that contraband is not allowed in the facility and that they confiscate the items when discovered during room searches. Staff stated that when they see a client smoking, they ask them to stop, remind them of the facility policy, and ask them to hand over the contraband. Confidential interviews returned statements that did not corroborate the allegations, stating that staff was present and verbally de-escalating before calling law enforcement, that they provided medical aid, and denying that staff allow clients to smoke marijuana in the home. Although the allegations may have happened or are valid, there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that the alleged violations occurred, therefore the allegations are determined to be Unsubstantiated. No deficiencies were cited at this time. Exit interview conducted. A signed copy of this report, LIC9099-C, and LIC811 were provided to Desia Dunn, Administrator. Appeal rights explained and provided.

(See attached LIC 811) LPA Galvan reviewed medication files, medical incident reports, and staff file. LPA spoke to CTC's Program Direct regarding the concerns of staff administering C1 incorrect medication, the importance of staff verifying and confirming the correct medication is being administered and maintaining medication quality assurance. LPA spoke to facility representative (FR) Abagail Zavala, FR stated S1 is contracted Licensed Vocational Nurse to oversee medication and medical well being of all clients at CTC. S1 admitted to giving the incorrect medication to S1. S1 was given S1's evening medication dosage in the morning and missed a medication dosage. S1 was directed on making sure to review and verify that the correct medication is being administered to clients. The medical case manager has been providing additional medication oversight to prevent medication error. narrative: On the above date, Licensing Program Analysts (LPAs) Shanae Pharaoh and Babatunde Aborchie, and Licensing Program Manager Abdoulaye Traore met with Administrator Erin Franco and CEO Darryl Monteilh who granted access to the facility. The purpose of this visit was to conduct a pre-licensing inspection of the Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP). Applicants are applying for a maximum capacity of six ambulatory clients age 12-17 including non-minor dependents. The facility was toured both inside and out. The facility is a one story residence with 4 bedrooms and 2 and a half bathrooms. The half bathroom will be used for staff. Bedroom #1: the room was furnished with two twin-size beds - Vacant Bedroom #2: the room was furnished with one twin-size bed - Vacant Bedroom #3, the room was furnished with two twin-size bed - Vacant. Bedroom #4, the room was furnished with one twin-size bed - Vacant There was one group meeting/therapy/ activity area There was a common area There was a dining room area with a table that fit 6 client Bedrooms were arranged so that no more than two clients share a room, and there was one client per bed. There was adequate shelves and closet space for clients' belongings. There were additional linens located in the hallway closets and client towels were stored in a bathroom cabinet. The bathrooms were clean and in good repair. The hot water in the client bathroom was measured to be 110.8 degrees. All hazardous items have been properly made inaccessible to areas where clients will have access. The medications will be stored and locked in a cabinet in the staff office. Cleansers/chemicals were locked and stored in the garage storage closet. Sharp knives were inaccessible and stored in a locked storage pantry in the kitchen. The First Aid Kit was located in the staff office and contained all required supplies. The facility's smoke detectors in the rooms and hallways were checked and they were operable. The carbon monoxide detectors located in common area outside the kitchen were also operable. There were two fireplaces located in common areas and they were properly screened. Toys were observed to be safe, clean and age appropriate for the age group of children to be cared. There were no guns or weapons in the facility as stated by the Administrator. LPA observed a minimum 7-day non-perishable and a 2-day perishable supply of food. Proper storage of all food was noted. Food will be stored in kitchen cabinets and accessible to clients. Additional food storage will be stored in a locked pantry in the kitchen. An operable fire extinguishers was located in the kitchen and another fire extinguisher was in the garage. There was an additional refrigerator and freezer in the garage. The laundry was located in the garage. Client files will be stored in a locked cabinet in the staff office. The following required posted items were observed accessible to clients: Grievance Procedures, Personal Rights, visitation policies, menu, Emergency Disaster Plan and facility sketch. The facility outside ground was also inspected and it was observed to be clean and maintained. Emergency exits were free from obstruction. There is a swimming pool located in the backyard of the facility, which was unlocked and inaccessible to clients. The pool was surrounded by a wrought iron fence measured to be 5 feet tall with a gate that self-latches and opens outward. Administrator's First Aid and CPR cards expire on June 2023. Based on this inspection of the STRTP, the facility will need the following corrections: Lock box for clients personal items and contraceptives Lock box for refrigerated medications After corrections are completed, the applicant will send verification of corrections to LPA.. Also, the applicant has been scheduled for a Component III on August 24, 2021. An exit interview was conducted and a copy of this report was discussed and provided to applicant on this date.

narrative: On August 17, 2022 at 4: PM, Associate Governmental Program Analyst (AGPA) Kim Robinson met with the Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Licensee, Darryl Monteilh, to assess an Enhanced Civil Penalty (ECP). On July 20, 2022, the Department concluded a complaint investigation alleging that child care staff neglected to provide comfortable and safe environment to minors, resulting with a fifteen-year-old child #5 (C5) sustaining serious bodily injuries. (See the Confidential Names List, LIC 811, dated August 17, 2022). The allegations were substantiated and the STRTP was cited under the Interim Licensing Standards, Section 87072(c) Personal Rights with a $500.00 immediate civil penalty assessment. The investigative evidence gathered shows two minors assaulted C5, without staff supervising to ensure the health and safety of all minors placed in care. Based on the analysis of the police and medical reports, including interviews, the Department has determined that an enhanced civil penalty is warranted for STRTP staff neglecting to provide a safe and comfortable home for the wellbeing of all minors in care as required in the Interim Licensing Standards. Section 11165.2 of the Penal Code defines severe neglect as negligent treatment or maltreatment of a child when a person responsible for the child's welfare permits any child to suffer unjustifiable physical pain. This section describes a number of more or less direct and (always) willful acts that constitute physical abuse. Pursuant to the Enhanced Civil Penalty law, Health and Safety (H&S) code section 1548 (f)(1)(A), the Department will be issuing an immediate civil penalty of $2,000.00. An exit interview was completed, and appeal rights discussed. A copy of this report, the Confidential Names List, Appeal Rights, and a Civil Penalty Assessment - Serious Bodily Injury/Physical Abuse (Form 421-D) were provided to the licensee. **Due to technical difficulties this is an electronic copy of a written report that was issued on 8/17/22. narrative: On September 8, 2022, at 9:30 am a virtual informal office conference was held via Microsoft Teams with the Creekside Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP). The following people were in attendance: Community Care Licensing (CCL) Regional Manager (RM) LaCresha Cook, Licensing Program Manager (LPM) Abdoulaye Traore, Licensing Program Analysts (LPAs) Cynthia Urena and Anne Visaya, San Bernardino Behavioral Health Representative Diane Wolkenhauer, Social Services Practitioner (SSP) San Bernardino County Children Family Services (CFS) Amy Guisa, Andria Innerbichler, Sr DPO Riverside County Probation Juan Bretado, Riverside University Health Service- Behavioral Health (RUHS-BH) Deputy Director Janine Moore, CCL Provider Policy Implementation Unit Manager Policy and Technical Assistance Bureau, System of Care Branch Alicia Bernstein, LPM Law Enforcement Contact Review Unit (LECRU) Statewide CCLD Angela King, California Department of Social Services (CDSS) Child Trafficking Program Support Units Leeland Turner and Darrin Holt, Social Service Practitioner (SSP) Susan Maday, STRTP Coordinator SB County CFS Evelyn Martinez, CFS, SSP II Ivette Barcena, Creekside Consultant Tony Walker, Supervisor CFS San Bernadino County Hannah Gutierrez, Out of Home Investigations Supervisor Riverside County Karin Atkins, Deputy Director SB County CFS Nancy Satterwhite, Department of Behavioral Health Melissa Graham, RUHS-BH Children's Administrator Miranda DeShields, Manager CFT SB County Tracy Raymond, Creekside Consultant Courage Ekhaguere, Alain Dominique Riverside Department of Public Social Services (DPSS) Placement Monitor, Administrative Analyst Riverside County (DPSS) Jenell Ross, STRTP Representative Dr. Samita Kapoo, STRTP Representative Monica R. Williams, and CEO Creekside Daryl Monteilh The following information was discussed: · Lack of oversight of the facility by management. · Lack of trauma informed milieu · Emergency Intervention Plan (Needs to be trauma informed) · Harm Reduction [Continued on page 2] ·Law Enforcement Contact Unit update (AB388) · Mental Health Program Approval update · Administrator duties and Qualifications · Reporting Requirement (Deficiencies) · Lack of Required Staff Training · Serious Complaints Allegations ( Substantiated allegations and Enhanced Civil Penalty) · Maintaining Staff/Clients Records · Client Services · Technical Support Program referral The meeting included a discussion regarding the above concerns. At the beginning of the discussion, Regional Manager (RM) Cook and Licensing Program Manager (LPM) Traore explained the reason for the meeting and explained that the meeting would be a collaborative meeting which included the participation and input of all departments listed above that provide services to the Creekside STRTP. During the discussion, LPM King shared data regarding the facility law enforcement contacts and Special Incident Reports. LPM King discussed the importance of reporting accurate information and contacting law enforcement as a last resource unless there is imminent risk of danger. LPM Traore will provide LPM King's contact information for the STRTP to reach out to LPM King for additional information and virtual training. RM Cook and LPM discussed CCL's concerns regarding the above-mentioned issues and requested input from the various oversight agencies participating in the meeting discussion. Alicia Bernstein discussed trauma informed milieu. ILS Standards 87078. Trauma Informed Interventions and Treatment practices. Alicia specified the importance of providing trauma informed care for the population served. Specific resources, assessments and intake should come from a trauma informed perspective. The STRTP should provide individualized care that specializes on the individual needs of each client. Links to the following resources were provided regarding information on trauma informed care and treatment practices: NTCTSN (nctsn.org), Traumatic Stress Institute, and Dr Nadine Burke Harris. Leeland Turner and Darrin Holt, CDSS CTR, CDSS, Child Trafficking Program Support Unit provide information regarding Harm Reduction, focusing on treating behaviors overtime and ensuring it is client specific. Not every client shares the same needs. Documentation in the client's needs and service plan is important. When a client's plan is not working, provider should ensure communication with all entities is occurring and involve CCL, and the county social workers and other providers who are involved in the case. [Continued on page 3] The facility was given until 09/16/2022 to submit a plan of correction to Community Care Licensing for approval. The licensee agrees to the following: · The licensee will submit a plan on how the Board of Directors will provide additional oversight to ensure a trauma informed care milieu is implemented including individualized trauma informed activities for each client in care. · The licensee will submit an updated training plan regarding what Trauma Informed trainings facility staff will received. · The licensee will submit a plan regarding how the Board of Directors will ensure facility staff comprehend the concepts of trauma informed care. · The licensee will submit proof of daily administrative rounds completed by Administrator or administrative staff. Overnight rounds should be included between the hours of 9pm and 6am to check on the well-being of clients and staff. The visits shall be at various hours, a minimum of 15 minutes, and shall be documented in the daily logbook and/or an administrative rounds sheet.
