narrative: Regarding the allegation that staff is not properly trained, it was specified that a staff was never trained from January to June 2022 and was often with clients and didn't know how to do anything for them. During investigation, confidential interview stated that staff received a minimal training. It was added that staff was only given a computer training, commercial sexual exploitation of children (CSEC) training, incident report training, and trauma informed care training. Another confidential interview indicated that staff stated they went through orientation with a group of new hires and received training on how to fill out documentation but was not provided 24-hour required training prior to working with the clients. Confidential interviews stated client thought that staff were good at interacting with clients but did not know how long staff had to train prior to supervising clients at the facility. LPAs were not available to receive documentation showing that the required training's were completed during inspection. Based on confidential interviews and record review the allegation that staff is not properly trained is substantiated. The preponderance of evidence standard has been met. Facility is cited for violation of Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) standard 87065. Supervision, Evaluation and Training Requirements (c)(2). The training plan shall address the initial 24-hour training for newly hired direct care staff. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this report along with the appeal right were provided to facility representative. Regarding the allegation that the facility drills are not being conducted, it was specifically alleged that the facility didn't conduct fire drills and had no logs. During investigation, confidential interview stated that fire drills were conducted and logged in a logbook in the staff office. Confidential interviews indicated that a fire drill was conducted when they were present at the facility. It was added that they did not know how often drills were conducted or if they were documented. Confidential interviews stated that the facility conducted a fire drill and all clients and staff went to the field during the drill. However, LPA received a conflicting information and LPAs observed the fire drills log was documented ahead and it was inconsistent. In regard to the allegation that residents are not being provided activities, it was specifically alleged that the clients don't get to do any activities. Confidential interviews disclosed that clients are provided with activities but could not provide a written plan for activities. Confidential interviews stated that clients were taken to movies and dinners, but she had not seen if they were documented. Confidential interviews stated that they did get taken out on outings like the movies and the carnival. It was added that they had water balloon fights and other activities around the facility. Based on confidential interviews, the allegations that facility drills were not being conducted and clients were not being provided activities, may have happened or valid, but there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that the alleged violations occurred. Therefore, these allegations are unsubstantiated at this time. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this report along with the appeal right were reviewed and provided to facility representative.

On August 23, 2023, at 9: AM a virtual informal office conference was held via Microsoft Teams with the Creekside Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP). The following people were in attendance: Community Care Licensing (CCL) Regional Manager (RM) LaCresha Cook, Licensing Program Manager (LPM) Abdoulaye Traore, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Rafael Enriquez, CDSS Rates Consultant, Rates Oversight Unit, System of Care, Carrie Salisbury, Staff Services Manager II John Sanfilippo, CDSS, Rate Analyst, Rates Oversight Tera Tapp, CFS SB County, Manager PRD Ana Del Nogal, Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) Staff Service Manager Andrea Bluford, DHCS Analyst Gabriel Pacheco, DHCS Analyst Steve Conn, DHCS SSMI David Gutierrez, Deputy Director SB County CFS Nancy Satterwhite, Supervisor CFS San Bernadino County Hannah Gutierrez, System of Care Branch Alicia Bernstein, County Social Worker Simika Jones, CDSS CCR SSA (Rates Analyst) Brandy Crosby, Social Services Practitioner (SSP) San Bernardino County Children Family Services (CFS) Amy Mierzwik, Admin. The following information was discussed: · Lack of Medi-Cal Certification · Lack of Mental Health Program Approval · Possible Application Withdrawal continues on page The summary of the meeting included a discussion regarding the above concerns. At the beginning of the discussion, Licensing Program Manager (LPM) Traore explained the reason for the meeting and explained that the meeting would be a collaborative meeting. During the discussion, LPM asked CEO Darryl Monteilh of the STRTP for update regarding the Mental Health contract with San Bernardino County as the Department received information that STRTP is still in process of getting his mental health contract executed with DBH. Diane Wolkenhauer from the Department of Behavioral Health (DBH) reiterated that the application was approved but the contract has not been executed yet as today 08/23/2023. Dianne added that she didn't know when the contracted will be executed, however, Medi-Cal certification will still need to go through a process, and she couldn't say if it would be done by September 03, 2023. RM Cook indicated CCL's concerns regarding the above-mentioned issues and asked DHCS if the facility would be able to meet all requirement and be approved before the expiration of the provisional license on 09/3/2023. David Gutierrez, DHCS SSMI stated that the STRTP's MHPA application was received on 08/16/23 and assigned to Analyst Stephen Conn. The application still needs a full review, feedback, corrections and onsite inspection. David Gutierrez stated that this process was unlikely to be completed within one week. David Gutierrez added that Med-Cal Certification needed to be submitted along with the application which was not included with the application submitted on 08/16/2023. David Gutierrez stated they should not be pressured to approve a facility that treats children in 7 days. David Gutierrez invited Gabriel Pacheco to provide information. Gabriel Pacheco stated that the first application was denied in February of 2023 and that a new application was finally received and assigned on 08/16/23. David Gutierrez stated that Medi-Cal Certification and contract must be in place in order to approve the MHPA. Regional Manager (RM) Cook asked CEO Darryl Monteilh what his contingency plan was if it were not to be able to receive MHPA before the deadline. Regional Manager (RM) Cook stated options to use and guided STRTP members to make decisions whether to withdraw the STRTP application and be able to re-apply within the same year or he could apply for a different kind of facility as CCL will not be able to extend the provisional license after 24 months. Regional Manager (RM) Cook told CEO Darryl Monteilh that he needs to have a contingency plan so that social workers can take care of what they need to do for the children. continues on page CEO Darryl Monteilh stated he preferred using all his resources first in attempt to be approved before the deadline, however, if he didn't get to achieve his objective, he will withdraw his application and re-apply immediately. He indicated that he has no interest applying for another type of facility and he would like the team to expedite his application if he was to re-apply. LPM Traore stated that the application process could be much faster but that STRP application will need go through a full review. LPM Traore stated if he applies again, he would get a new license and that he needs to address the changes the agencies and department that has previously worked on his application LPM Traore advised CEO Darryl Monteilh to send the closure plan to CCL by August 30, 2023. Nancy Satterwhite commented that if the facility were to close that it would be a great impact to the children in placement at Creekside. She stated that we should try and help Creekside. CEO Darryl Monteilh asked for all hands-on deck. CEO Darryl Monteilh stated that if he chooses to submit his withdrawal, he will submit his application right away. LPM Traore stated that if CCL didn't receive a closure plan and the application withdrawal notification by August 30, 2023, the STRP application will be denied on September 3, 2023 at the expiration of the provisional license. After completion of the conference, LPM Traore thanked the facility representatives and all attendees. A copy of this report was emailed to CEO Daryl Monteilh for signature. Original signed reports will be placed in the facility file.

On September 12, 2024, at 10:15AM Rosslyn Gray, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) arrived at the above facility for the purpose of conducting a Case Management - Incident investigation. LPA met with Paris Ukattah Facility Administrator and a health and safety assessment was conducted prior to entering facility. The department received an Special Incident Report (SIR) dated July 25, 2024. The Incident Report, disclosed that at 12:45am C1 was throwing up and appeared to be drunk. S1 asked C1 if he was ok. C1 stated his stomach was hurting. While C1 was in the bathroom, at 1:15 am, C2 resident gave S1 a bottle of D"usse Cognac VSOP with a small amount left. S1 called to the Administrator to inform her that C1 was throwing up and reported that C1 came out of the bathroom and then went into the kitchen stumbling. S1 gave C1 water and continued to monitor C1 throughout the night, and made sure that C1 was laying on his side. S1 informed S2 of the incident and S2 informed inform the Mental Health Team. During the investigation LPA interviewed S2 and the following information was requested: The current Personnel Report LIC 500, the client roster, the LIC 500 and the client roster on the day that the incident occured. narrative: An unannounced SB Psychotropic Medication Tele-Inspection was conducted by Licensing Program Analysts (LPAs) Jean Herring, Pamela Silva and Gilbert Gutierrez on May 19, 2021 at 11: AM via Microsoft Teams Meeting. Remote "tele-inspection" of facilities is a part of Community Care Licensing Division's emergency response to the spread of Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19). During the tele-inspection, LPAs spoke with Trina Smith, Facility Administrator. Prior to the tele-inspection, LPA Herring requested all pertinent staff and client records from the licensee. LPAs conducted a facility tour with Ms. Smith at 11: AM. Overall, the facility is clean, safe, sanitary and in good repair. All prescribed medications are centrally stored, locked and inaccessible to unauthorized persons. There is adequate staffing in the facility to provide care and supervision for the children per the facility's Plan of Operation. Five(5) records of clients taking psychotropic medications were reviewed at 11: AM. LPAs observed the following: - C2 and C3 missed medications (M1 and M2) for several days. Staff noted on the Psychotropic Medication Administration Record (PMAR-LIC622B) that the clients were "out of medications". Staff explained that this was due to the TAR (Treatment Authorization Request) taking a while to get approved by Medi-Cal. - Facility used LIC622A (Medication Administration Record-MAR)) instead of LIC 622B (Psychotropic Medication Administration Record -PMAR) to log the following psychotropic medications: M1 (PMARs dated March, April, May 2021), M3 (PMARs dated March, April 2021); M4 (PMARs dated March and April 2021); M5 (PMARs dated March, April, May 2021; M6 (PMARs for March, April, May 2021); M7 (PMARs for March, April, May 2021); M8 (PMARs for March, April, May 2021); M9 (PMARs for March, April, May 2021) (continued...) - JV Court Orders authorizing the use of psychotropic medications for C1 and C4 have expired. - Needs and Services Plans (NSPs) for C1, C2, C3, C4, C5 are not signed by either the child or the placement worker or both. LPAs reviewed 2 staff files prior to the tele-inspection. LPAs interviewed 2 staff members at approximately 12: PM. LPAs interviewed 2 clients at approximately 12: PM. One (1) of the clients was not available at the time inspection. Two (2) of the clients refused to be interviewed. LPAs reviewed the facility's Plan of Operation prior to the tele-inspection. A signed copy of this licensing report was provided to the licensee via email along with Confidential Name(s) list (LIC 811).

narrative: Other allegations are that staff do not safeguard clients' personal belongings, and that staff purchases client's personal property. All ten (10) staff members and two (2) out of the three (3) clients that were interviewed denied these allegations. Based on interviews and observation, the facility provides clients with lockers where they can lock their valuables in, or clients can request staff members to lock their valuables for safekeeping inside the office. Statements from interviews consistently indicated that no staff or client ever witnessed any staff ask a client to steal from other clients, then sell the item to the staff. Of the ten (10) staff members and three (3) clients that were interviewed, only one (1) client alleged witnessing staff members smoke marijuana at the facility. Although this one (1) client also alleged that he observed a staff wiping what seems to be cocaine off his nose coming out of the bathroom, he did not witness the staff in the act of sniffing cocaine. None of the ten (10) staff members and two (2) clients ever observed a staff member under the influence of drugs while providing care and supervision to clients. Two (2) out of the three (3) clients that were interviewed expressed that they like living in the facility. Interviews revealed that staff members treat them good and are respectful to clients. An interview with the CSW indicated that C1, while living at the facility, had never disclosed any of the said allegations to her. CSW has no concerns or issues regarding the facility and its staff. Based on the information gathered, there is not enough evidence to corroborate the allegations. Although the allegations may have happened or are valid, the preponderance of the evidence to prove the allegations were not met, therefore the allegations are unsubstantiated. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this report was provided to the Adminsitrator for signature. There were no deficiencies cited during today's inspection.

narrative: On March 07, 2023, Licensing Program Analysts (LPAs) Juliet Robles, Raymond Wu and Joe Martinez conducted an unannounced inspection at the Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) facility at 9: AM. LPAs met with Abraham Nesheiwat, Administrator. The purpose of the inspection was to conduct an Annual/Required inspection of the facility. The STRTP's Mental Health Program will expire on 03/19/23. The STRTP has COA accreditation valid until 09/30/26. The STRTP is licensed up to twelve (12) ambulatory children ages 11-17 years of age and provides services to non-minor dependent. Currently, there are three (3) clients in placement. This is a two-story home with six (6) bedrooms, three bathrooms, three (3) offices, a full kitchen, living rooms, dining room and recreation activity room. PHYSICAL PLANT: A tour of the facility was conducted at 10: AM, along with Administrator. LPAs observed the required posted items are accessible to clients like: License, Mental Health Program Approval Certificate, Grievance Procedures, Personal Rights, Ombudsman Poster, monthly activity calendar, weekly menu, facility sketch and emergency disaster plan. All hazardous items have been properly made inaccessible to areas where clients will have access. The medications were stored and locked in one of the offices designated for the Social Workers. Cleansers/chemicals are locked and stored in the garage. Sharp knives are inaccessible and stored in a locked cabinet in the garage. There are two (2) First Aid Kits that are checked and are complete. Supplies of staples non-perishable foods for one week and perishable foods for two days are maintained in the facility. The facility has smoke detectors and carbon monoxide that are in all bedrooms, kitchen, living room and hallways. The hot water in the client bathroom was measured to be 115 degrees (F). The facility outside grounds was also inspected and it was observed to be free of debris or hazardous things. Emergency exits were free from obstruction. There is a swimming pool located on the premises of the facility, which is locked and inaccessible to clients. The pool is surrounded by a wrought iron fence measured over 5 feet tall with a gate that self-latches and opens outward. Operations Facility maintains a current, written plan of operation that meets licensing standards. Facility maintains a register of clients and the register is available upon request. The board of directors regularly conducts meeting to review and discuss the STRTP's operation. Disaster Preparedness Plan Facility maintains a current, written disaster and mass casualty plan of action. Facility conducts disaster drill at least every month for each shift. The drills are documented, and the documentation is maintained in the facility for at least a year. Facility maintains an emergency and disaster plan, register of clients, Needs and Services Plan for each client, medication records, and contact information for each client's responsible party and physician. Core/Therapeutic Services Facility provides core services and supports to children as appropriate or necessary that are trauma informed, culturally relevant, age and developmentally appropriate and include the following: Medi-Cal specialty mental health services; transition port services; educational and physical, behavioral, and mental health supports; activities to support children with services to achieve permanency. Emergency Intervention Plan: Facility utilizes technique of group and individual behavior management like crisis prevention and alternative methods of handling aggressive and assaultive behavior. Staff have trainings on manual restraint if needed to be utilized. Client Records LPAs at 12: PM started to review six (6) client records. All client records are available to the licensing agency to inspect, audit and copy upon demand. Client records contain required information including, but not limited to, consent forms, court orders, appraisal/needs and services plan, removal/discipline/complaint procedures; medical assessment; safeguards for cash resources, personal property and valuables; education records; personal rights forms; and medication administration records. Staff Records: During the inspection review, LPA inspected six (6) staff files and verified that all facility staff was subject to criminal records review, fingerprinted and cleared DOJ, FBI and CACI. All staffs signed the Criminal Record Statement and acknowledgement to report Child Abuse. Personnel records are maintained on the licensee, administrator, supervisor, and each employee. Documentation of the required education and experience requirements are maintained in the personnel file. LPA interviewed two (2) clients and three (3) staffs. LPA was provided with Board Minute Meetings and staffs schedule/personnel report. On today's inspection, there is one (1) Type B citation issued, see LIC809D. An exit interview was conducted, and a signed copy of this report, LIC809D, LIC811 and appeal rights were provided to the facility administrator. The facility representative was provided information on where to locate Provider Information Notices (PINs), and Compliance and Regulatory Enforcement (CARE) Tools, for Children's Residential licensees please visit the Program website at www.cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/community-care-licensing/inspection-process.

narrative: Investigator Lomeli conducted confidential interviews of the following: Facility Personnel on 3/22/23 and 5/25/23. Follow up interviews were attempted and conducted on 6/5/23. Five clients were interviewed between 5/16/23 and 5/22/23. Investigators Lomeli and Ruben Munoz made attempts to obtain a statement from the client who sustained the injury on 3/22/23 and 5/26/23, but client refused to provide any information. Confidential interviews reveal that clients engaged in a physical altercation after two clients (C1 and C2) went in the bedroom of client (C3) during bedtime. C1 became upset and started a fight after C1 was asked by C3 not to lay on C3's bed. The two clients started punching each other and was later redirected by the nocturnal shift staff to stop. Staff did not observe any serious injuries; clients declined any medical attention. The following day, both clients complained of pain and were taken by staff to seek medical care. C1 was diagnosed with mandible fracture and dental trauma. There were conflicting statements provided by the interviewed parties during the investigation. It's not known how the clients were able to be in the same bedroom together. One staff insists that staff was supervising the hallway of the clients' bedrooms and that clients usually get in and out of bedrooms through the bedroom windows. C1 was reported to have been intoxicated but the nocturnal staff denied smelling alcohol and observed that C1 was coherent after staff broke up the fight. C1 was reported to be bleeding profusely after the fight but staff denied observing this. C2 denied witnessing the incident and reportedly left the bedroom through a back door when the fight started. C1 refused to provide any information regarding the incident. The other clients in placement denied witnessing the incident. There were no other staff present when the incident occurred. facility_name: DANIEL AND NANCY MARBLE CASA DE NINOS
narrative: It was alleged that facility staff were not meeting client's needs by dropping them off late for school. In interviews conducted, two clients stated that they were usually late for school due to a variety of reasons such as morning staff coming into work late or other clients taking too long to get ready. Both clients stated that staff would generally take clients to school in separate trips depending on who was ready, but that they would also sometimes have to wait on clients that were not too far behind. This would often lead to them showing up to school late. Three other clients stated that they were usually late to school due to clients waking up too late or taking too long to get ready but did not indicate whether staff were showing up to work late. In interviews conducted, all facility staff members stated that the clients would often get to school late because most of them would either wake up late and/or take too long to get ready. All staff members indicated that there were multiple facility vehicles used to transport clients to school and they would take the ones that were ready first to go to school. Staff indicated that on occasion, they would be late for work but that there was always enough coverage from the overnight shift to take clients to school and it was not a factor in their lateness. Interviews conducted with social workers revealed no pertinent information related to the allegation. A review of attendance records revealed that clients were consistently late to school multiple times a week. It was also alleged that facility staff do not pick up youth from school in a timely manner when they are supposed to. In interviews conducted, all clients stated that they have not had to wait an unreasonable amount of time for facility staff to pick them up from school. Sometimes staff may take longer than usual, but it would not be for an unreasonable amount of time. Four clients stated that most days after school, they will call the facility manager and ask if they can stay out on a community pass to spend time with friends. Afterwards, they will meet with staff at a designated time and place to be picked up or call to be picked up. One client stated that they do not generally stay out on community passes and will generally get picked up in a timely manner by staff. In interviews conducted, all staff members confirmed the above statements and stated that clients are afforded the privilege of community passes unless they have done something to lose the privilege. Therefore, they are not always picking up clients right after school ends. Staff stated that sometimes they may run a bit late, but it is never unreasonable. Staff further stated that sometimes they are called by the school to pick up clients that are being sent home for the day. In these instances, staff will try to send someone as soon as possible but they may not always respond immediately due to staffing ratio requirements when clients are present. In interviews conducted, multiple social workers stated that they did not have any immediate concerns regarding staff not picking up clients in a timely manner. (Continued) It was also alleged that on one occasion after school, facility staff drove off and left one client in care stranded. However, the exact client was unable to be identified. Individuals interviewed were not aware of or familiar with the alleged incident. In interviews conducted, all clients denied ever being left stranded after school or seeing anyone be left behind during pickup. In interviews conducted, facility staff denied the allegation and were unaware of any incident of that nature. In interviews conducted, multiple social workers stated that they were unaware of any incidents of that nature. Social workers indicated that they did not have any immediate concerns of the safety of their clients in the home. It was also alleged that clients are allowed to drink alcohol in the facility. In interviews conducted, all clients denied the allegation and stated that if they were ever caught with any type of alcohol or contraband, it would immediately be confiscated, room searches would be triggered, and clients may lose certain privileges. The clients denied staff ever providing any alcohol for them and stated that they generally obtained their alcohol by other means. In interviews conducted, facility staff denied the allegation and stated that they would never provide or allow any type of illegal substance use in the home. Staff are aware that clients are sometimes able to obtain these items through certain means and stated that when caught, the items are immediately confiscated and discarded. In interviews conducted, social workers stated that they were aware that their clients would sometimes obtain alcohol but did not have any concerns or reason to believe that staff may be providing it or allowing it in the facility. It was also alleged that clients are allowed to physically fight each other in the home. In interviews conducted, all clients denied the allegation and stated that staff do not allow or encourage any type of fighting between clients in the home. If it appears that clients may be escalating an argument towards a physical altercation, staff will redirect and separate the clients. In interviews conducted, facility staff denied the allegation and confirmed that they would redirect clients immediately when an argument begins to occur. Staff stated that clients past and present have gotten into physical altercations before, but it was never allowed or encouraged by staff, and it usually happened off-site without staff present. In interviews conducted, social workers stated they have not seen or heard of instances in which staff allowed or encouraged fighting in the home. Social workers stated that they did not have any immediate concerns regarding the safety of their clients in the home. Based on interviews conducted and records reviewed, the preponderance of evidence standard has not been met. Although the allegations may have happened or may be valid, there is not a preponderance of evidence to suggest that the allegations occurred. Therefore, the allegations are deemed UNSUBSTANTIATED. An exit interview was conducted and a copy of this report was provided to the Licensee.

narrative: It was alleged that around March of 2023, facility staff failed to prevent one client in care from possessing hazardous items to include a lighter, lighter fluid, and a knife. In interviews conducted, four other clients denied ever seeing or hearing of any minors in the facility having access to those items. The clients indicated that they have secretly brought other prohibited items into the facility before but that they would be confiscated if staff discovered them. All four clients confirmed that staff will conduct body checks and room searches if they have probable cause to do so. In interviews conducted, facility staff members denied the allegation and stated that when they were made aware of the allegation, they immediately searched the client's room for the above-mentioned items and did not find anything. Facility staff confirmed that they will conduct body checks or room searches when they have reason to believe that clients may be hiding something or bringing something into the facility. In interviews conducted, outside sources stated that they have seen clients in possession of prohibited items such as nicotine products but not the items listed above. In interviews conducted, multiple social workers stated that they had not seen or heard of clients in care having access to items such as knives and lighter fluid. It was also alleged that around March of 2023, facility staff failed to prevent one client in care from severely harming themselves with the items mentioned above. In interviews conducted, four other clients denied the allegation and stated that they did not see or hear of any instances in which the one client harmed themselves with the items mentioned above. In interviews conducted, facility staff denied the allegation and stated that when they were made aware of the allegation on the same day, they immediately conducted a body check on the client and did not observe any injuries. In interviews conducted, outside sources denied observing any injuries on the client that matched the description in the allegation. Interviews conducted with social workers also revealed no knowledge or observations of the alleged injuries. It was also alleged that facility staff encouraged clients to physically assault one other client in care. In interviews conducted, four clients denied the allegation and stated that facility staff will always attempt to redirect clients when arguments begin to occur. In interviews conducted, facility staff denied the allegation and stated that clients will get into altercations sometimes but staff will always try to redirect them and stop the arguments from escalating. In interviews conducted, outside sources revealed no pertinent information related to the allegation. Multiple social workers also revealed no knowledge of the allegation and stated that they did not have immediate concerns regarding the allegation. It was also alleged that facility staff members speak inappropriately to clients in care. In interviews conducted, four clients denied the allegation and stated that staff have always been kind and warm towards them. All clients indicated that they had great relationships with the staff members. In interviews conducted, facility staff denied the allegation and stated that they were close with the clients and would never verbally abuse or speak to them inappropriately. Outside sources revealed no pertinent information regarding the allegation. In interviews conducted, social workers revealed no concerns regarding the allegation. It was also alleged that facility staff members physically abuse clients in care. In interviews conducted, four clients denied the allegation and stated that staff were kind and they felt safe with them. Facility staff members denied the allegation as well. In interviews conducted, outside sources revealed no knowledge or concerns regarding the allegation. Social workers also revealed no concerns regarding the allegation and stated that clients have never complained about physical abuse by facility staff. It was also alleged that facility staff members did not allow one client in care to have a private conversation. In interviews conducted, four clients stated that they were unaware of the specific allegation but stated that staff have never infringed on their right to have private conversations both in-person and on the phone. In interviews conducted, facility staff denied the allegation as well. Outside sources revealed no pertinent information regarding the allegation. In interviews conducted, social workers indicated that they did not have any concerns regarding privacy in the facility Based on interviews conducted and records reviewed, there is not a preponderance of evidence to suggest that the above allegations occurred. Although the allegations may have happened or may be valid, the preponderance of evidence standard has not been met. Therefore, the allegations are deemed UNSUBSTANTIATED. An exit interview was conducted and a copy of this report was provided to the Licensee.

narrative: The Following Allegation(s) were reported: 1. The facility staff excludes a minor from outings. Staff members (S1, S2, and S3) refuted the accusation by asserting that no client is left out of any excursion by staff. Nevertheless, in order to take part in outings and enjoy specific benefits, clients are required to follow their program diligently and finish daily responsibilities like household chores, school assignments, and exhibiting positive behavior and attitude. S1 stressed that staff will support all clients in reaching their weekly objectives. In case a client is observed failing to meet their responsibilities, staff will aim to inspire them verbally and propose different strategies to assist them in accomplishing their goals and joining outings. C2 denied the allegations, stating that the staff treats all clients with fairness and respect, and encourages them to take part in both daily activities and weekend excursions. 2. The staff does not ensure that the minor is adequately fed, The accusation was denied by staff members (S1, S2, and S3), who emphasized that all clients receive three meals a day consisting of the five food groups, along with the option of various snacks between meals. The facility has an abundant food supply due to its size, and clients are consulted about their food preferences as long as they meet the requirements of the five food groups. Additionally, staff revealed that C1 would refuse to eat while playing on the gaming system and would become upset when asked to stop in order to have a meal. In such cases, any uneaten food is packed and provided to the client when they are ready to eat. C2 also stated that every client is provided with three meals per day, along with snacks between meals and the opportunity for seconds if requested. 3. The staff conduct poses a risk to the children in care. narrative: On 07/03/24, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Joe Martinez conducted a follow-up case management inspection at the Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) and met with the facility representative above. On 07/07/23, the STRTP submitted an incident report (IR) to the Department reporting that on 07/07/23 a youth was found deceased. The STRTP reported that the youth left the facility on 07/06/23 without permission. After a search for the youth, law enforcement was notified and a missing person report was called in. On 07/07/23, STRTP staff was notified that the youth was found deceased in the surrounding orchards. On 07/07/23, LPA Karen McGee conducted a case management inspection and interviewed S1 and S6. On 08/18/23, LPA Martinez conducted a followed up case management inspection and obtain follow up records. The Department Investigations Branch (IB) conducted a full investigation, completed on 06/25/24. Investigator Jorge Jauregui investigated the allegation of Neglect/Lack of Supervision. The investigation included a review of records and confidential interviews. IB Investigator reviewed pertinent records on 04/04/24, 04/12/24, 04/15/24, STRTP staff interviews on 05/23/24, 06/11/24, with staff 1,2,3,4,5,6 (S1, S2, S3, S4,S5,S6 ) Foster Youth interviews on 05/23/24, with Foster Youth 2,3 ( FC2,FC3 ) Collateral Interviews on 05/28/24. With Collateral 1 (C1). On 07/06/2023, FC1 was admitted into hospital regarding a panic attack and medication refill. Youth was discharged and returned to the STRTP facility. Upon his return, FC1 mentioned to S2 that he was not having a good day and went to his room. STRTP staff checked on FC1, who stated he wanted to be left alone. S2 and S4 left the facility on a planned outing. FC1 was left under the care of S5. S5 believed S2 and S4 had taken the youth on the planned outing. S2 and S4 returned to the facility and realized youth had runaway. STRTP Staff reported they conduct checks on the residents every 15 minutes. However, staff did not communicate and failed to supervise youth FC1. Staff interviews indicated they did not implement a plan to address youths mental health needs upon his return from the hospital. The next morning, FC1 was found deceased. Kern County Coroner's department determined the cause of death to be suicide. During the inspection the LPA Martinez generated (1) deficiency (see attached 809D). LPA Martinez discussed plan of corrections, appeal rights with the STRTP representative. LPA Martinez conducted an exit interview and a signed LIC809 and LIC809(D)was provided to the STRTP representative. Per the new Civil Penalty laws, Health and Safety (H&S) Code section 1548(e)(3), an Enhanced Civil Penalty ECP) determination is pending due to the substantiated allegation. If an ECP is warranted, a Community Care Licensing (CCL) representative will return to the facility to deliver the penalty assessment.

narrative: On September 09, 2024, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Joe Martinez conducted a case management inspection with the above facility to assess an Enhanced Civil Penalty (ECP). LPA Martinez discussed the following with the facility representative named above. The ECP is related to an incident where a youth left the Short-Term Residential Treatment Program (STRTP) without permission on July 06, 2023, and was found deceased on July 07, 2023. The STRTP staff failed to implement a plan to address the youth's mental health needs following his return from the hospital. Based on the investigation conducted by Investigation Branch, the Department cited the facility for Section 80078(a) Responsibility for Providing Care and Supervision. The Department has concluded an analysis and determined that an Enhanced Civil Penalty is warranted. Under Health and Safety Code Section 1548(e)(3)(A), a violation that the Department determines resulted in the death of a person receiving care from a Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program with a licensed capacity between 40 or fewer will result in a civil penalty of $7,500.00. A copy of LIC809, Confidential Names Form, Appeal Rights and form LIC 421-D(CRP) for a Civil Penalty Assessment - Death, was provided to the facility representative.

In addition, some clients stated that majority of the client's would horseplay amongst each other causing marks on their bodies. Based on the information gathered during confidential interviews, it cannot be determined whether the allegation occurred resulting in the staff not ensuring the minor is provided a safe environment while in care. Despite these efforts to mitigate the introduction of contraband, there have been cases where such items were discovered in a client's room, as clients sometimes conceal these items in areas inaccessible to staff. These contraband items are typically recovered and confiscated during random visual inspections of the rooms or while staff are engaged in cleaning activities. The staff additionally noted that clients gain access to prohibited items while absent without leave, during school hours, or during authorized overnight stays with family members. Continued.... Additionally, confidential statements acquired from the previously mentioned clients verified that four or more staff members are supervising the clients and that the clients have access to mental health services or programs, wherein clients express no concerns about the care and supervision provided. narrative: Investigation revealed the following: It was alleged staff do not intervene when minors engage in altercations with other minors. Interview conducted with all staff denied the allegation. Staff stated that if children get into altercations or are horse playing with one another staff verbally redirect children. Staff stated that if children are in a more physical fight staff will try to separate children and if needed use MAB training techniques which incorporate 2 or more staff. Staff identified two incidents of fighting specifically occurring during the time of this investigation. Staff stated that one child was leaving for school and came back into the home and a fight ensued between two other children for an unknown reason. Staff stated that they immediately intervened as soon as it was recognized a fight was occurring and tried separating the children. Staff stated that children were assessed, and no children wanted to discuss, and no injuries were reported. The other fight that occurred in the home was investigated but staff stated they intervened and stop all potential fights, horse playing or verbal altercations with redirection before the situations escalate. Interviews conducted with four (4) children stated that horse playing has been occurring in the home but that no one is trying to hurt the other person. narrative: On 07/11/25, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Joe Martinez initiated an annual review at the Short Term Residential Treatment Program (STRTP) and met with the facility representative listed above. LPA Martinez began the tour of the facility with the STRTP administrator (R1), and the following was observed. LPA Martinez toured the interior and exterior of the facility. All common areas, bedrooms, and bathrooms appeared clean, sanitary, and in good repair. A current license and personal rights poster were observed in the hallway leading to the staff office. At the time of the inspection, the STRTP has 12 youth placed in the home.The bedrooms each accommodated two youth, providing unobstructed pathways around beds and ample closet space. No rooms served as passageways, and no more than two residents shared any bedroom. Cleaning solutions, sharps, and chemicals were stored in a locked area away from food areas. No firearms or ammunition were present on the premises. The in-ground swimming pool in the rear yard was enclosed by a fence measuring five feet in height. During the inspection, LPA Martinez observed the pool gate locked. LPA Martinez observed that windows were intact and screened; lighting was adequate in all rooms. Walkways and exits remained clear of obstructions. There were no deficiencies specific to Building and Grounds regulations were identified during this visit. LPA Martinez interviewed 2 youth and began to review 2 youth files. Due to time constraints, the annual review will need to be completed at a later time. There are no deficiencies to be cited at this time. LPA Martinez conducted an exit interview and provided the STRTP Representative with a signed copy of the LIC 809 and LIC809C.

Information obtained from the Group Home Administrator and Group Home Staff revealed that from 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. there are 4 staff members always present and from 11:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m. only 2 staff members are present. At no time are clients allowed to leave the facility without first getting approval by a staff member. Due to the layout and the location of the facility staff will allow clients to step outside to the playground that is fenced in to get some fresh air or to give a client time to cool off. While clients are at the playground, staff will routinely check on them every fifteen to thirty minutes to make sure the clienst are ok. Staff also has access to cameras that are placed in common areas inside the facility as well as outside of the facility to better protect the staff and clients. Also prior to any client entering the facility they are asked to empty their pockets and turn in any contraband that they might have on them. If any contraband is found, it is immediately removed and properly disposed of. Information obtained from clients revealed that four or more staffs are present during the day and at night two staff members are present. 4 of 5 clients denied seeing anyone smoke outside of the facility playground and further disclosed that if they wanted to smoke they would go AWOL for ten to fifteen minutes to do so. All clients indicated that they are aware of what staff can and can't do, where they can and cannot check for things. All clients indicated that they feel safe at the facility and feel that staff is looking out for each client's best interests. Therefore, based on the information received, the above allegation is determined to be unsubstantiated. Although the allegation may have happened or is valid, there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that the alleged violation occurred, therefore the allegation is found to be unsubstantiated. Appeal Rights were provided and discussed with the Group Home Facility Manager via teleconference. There are no deficiencies to be cited at this time. narrative: On November 19, 2020 at 11: AM, Community Care Licensing - Monterey Park Regional Office (CCL-MPRO) conducted a virtual meeting with Daughter Project Girls Home (a Short-Term Residential Program, STRTP) via Microsoft Teams meeting app. Remote meetings and tele-inspections of facilities are a part of Community Care Licensing Division's emergency response to the spread of Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19). Present at the meeting representing the Department were Licensing Program Managers (LPMs) Tira Logan-Shanks, Gustavo Garcia and Angela King; and Licensing Program Analysts (LPAs) Jean Herring and Dina Camara. Present at the meeting representing the STRTP were Brent Stratton, Board Chairman; Jennifer Jensen, CEO; Charity Jensen, Head of Programs; Dr. Jasmeet Bains, Board Member; Teodora Corbell, Administrator; and Ivette Diaz, Head of Service. Also present at the meeting were Monica Goodell, Department of Human Services (DHS) FFA & STRTP Liaison; Donna Robinson, Behavioral Health & Recovery Services (BHRS) Mental Health Supervisor; Heather Williams, BHRS Recovery Specialist II; Willie Fields, BHRS Recovery Specialist III; and Officer Jesus Gomez and Kelsey Brackett from Bakersfield Police Department. Introductions were made, and the following agenda items were discussed: Law Enforcement (LE) Contact Reports and Special Incident Reports (SIR) · Huge volume of Law Enforcement Contact Reports - Per Bakersfield Police Department (BPD) call log, the facility made 784 calls to BPD from November 1, 2019 thru October 31, 2020. This facility serves CSEC population and has a capacity of 10. Based on the review of facility rosters, facility has an average census of (Page 1 of 4) 6.5 in the past year. Taking the capacity/census of the facility into consideration, it is determined that the number of police calls made by the facility have been extremely high. · Failure to report LE contact reports and SIRs to CCL - Facility failed to report three months of LE contact reports and SIRs from April thru June 2020. This totaled to over LE contact reports and SIRs. The provider indicated that this occurred prior to the previous Head of Service (HOS) resignation from DPGH. · LE Contact Reports (624-LE) & SIRs not properly completed; missing information; duplication. Need to include incident dates, placement type, supervisor's approval and other required information related to Assembly Bill (AB) 388. Need a detailed description of engagement and de-escalation techniques used and need to be personalized for each youth. Need to ensure facility follows procedures for reintegrating client into the program following an incident or AWOL. · Samples of concerning incident reports - Law Enforcement Contact Review Unit Team discussed samples of concerning incident reports received from the facility and provided technical assistance. · Lack of Improvement - Since Law Enforcement Contact Review Unit Team unit conducted their inspection on 2/6/20, there has been no improvement with the way the facility handles AWOL, client behaviors and SIR reporting. The HOS reported that they have started conducting quality review of SIRs three weeks ago. Facility was advised to review and re-assess the facility's runaway protocols as well. · Factors that contribute to AWOL, CSEC activities and other behaviors - Per provider, the type of population they serve presents a challenge as these clients have "difficulty to stay put." Staff treats each situation differently (case-by-case basis); finds ways to occupy the youth and divert their attention (e.g. art therapy). Additional training for all staff is also being provided to better equip the staff in handling AWOLs and client behaviors. · Per Kern County FFA & STRTP Liaison, Monica Goodel's request, the provider will also submit SIRs to Ms. Goodel. (Page 2 of 4) Care and Supervision · Supervision on the second floor - Per provider, staff conducts room checks every 30 minutes during day time. The facility maintains a tracking log for each shift. Facility has a staff stationed upstairs in the laundry area from 10: PM to 6: AM. · One-on-one supervision protocols - Currently, the facility has one client (C1) that requires one-on-one supervision. Despite of the one-on-one supervision arrangement, C1 continues to leave the facility unauthorized several times a week. Due to C1's age and developmental delays, there are serious concerns about this client's health and safety when she leaves the facility unauthorized. The provider stated that C1 was provided with a gizmo watch (which was approved by the placement agency). The watch has a GPS locator and can be used for calling or texting approved individuals. The facility was advised to ensure that C1's Needs and Services Plan (NSP) contains a detailed supervision plan for the child (include one-on-one supervision and use of gizmo watch). Board Meeting minutes · Board Meeting Minutes need to include discussion of law enforcement contact reports, regular incident reports and licensing reports. · The administrator and/or a facility representative who's familiar with the youth must attend the Board Meetings as they can offer more insight on what is going on at the STRTP Needs & Services Plans (NSP) · Must cover all required areas as specified in STRP ILS Sections 87068.2; 87068.22 & 87068.3. · Must obtain and review case plan from the placement agency prior to developing a child's NSP. · Intake process (Do you interview all interested parties such as the child, the placement worker and others involved?) · Need to include inputs from CFT · Need to expand/ provide details of coping skills and triggers · Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) may need to be re-assessed and improved to ensure the facility is effectively measuring successes and failures. (page 3 of 4) Mental Health Status · The provider is working on the last piece of their MH application. KBHRS is actively providing feedback and support to the provider. New Administrator and Head of Service Credentials and Qualifications documents Need to submit to CCL by 11/30/20. Technical Support Program (TSP) referral The facility was offered a TSP referral to Technical Support Unit, which the facility accepted. This unit offers Resource Guides, which the licensee can use as a tool to understand the requirements of compliance. Resource Guides also provide best practice suggestions that the licensee may choose to implement within their facility to not only meet, but exceed, the requirements of licensure. Compliance Plan The licensee agreed to submit a plan to ensure staff follows the facility's AWOL procedures and ensure compliance with reporting requirements. The plan shall be submitted via email by 11/30/20. The virtual meeting ended at 1: PM. A signed copy of this report was provided to the licensee. (page 4 of 4)

On December 1, 2020 at 3: PM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Jean Herring made an unannounced Case Management tele-Inspection with Daughter Project Girls Home via Microsoft Teams meeting app. Remote "tele-inspections" of facilities are a part of Community Care Licensing Division's emergency response to the spread of Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19). LPA met with Teodora Corbell, STRTP Administrator. The purpose of the tele-inspection was to follow up on a death incident report received by the Department on November 30, 2020. On November 30, 2020, LPA Herring made follow up calls to the facility and spoke with Ms. Corbell and Ivette Diaz, Head of Service. The STRTP reported that on November 25, 2020 shortly after running away from the facility, C1 died after being hit by a vehicle. The STRTP reported that the youth was upset due to facility staff confiscating contraband found in her bedroom. The youth left the facility unauthorized, followed by facility staff who maintained the youth in sight, and attempted to verbally redirect the youth to return. Facility staff observed the client walk into the street where she was struck by an on-coming vehicle. The staff person immediately contacted 911 and officers from the Bakersfield Police Department, the Bakersfield Fire Department and Paramedics responded within minutes. The Bakersfield Fire Department pronounced the client deceased at the scene. The Administrator stated that the Sacramento County placing social worker was notified of the incident on November 25, 2020. On November 30, 2020, the facility submitted the following requested documents: Law Enforcement Contact Report, Death Report, progress notes for C1, intake documents, placement worker information and news links. This death incident will be further investigated by the Department's Investigation Branch. A signed copy of this report was provided to the licensee along with LIC 811 (Confidential Name/s list).

narrative: Interviews were conducted by Investigator Barragan from 12/9/20 to 2/1/21 with multiple parties such as first responders, facility staff, placement agency staff, and other clients in placement. The investigation revealed the following: On 11/25/20, client returned to the facility from an unauthorized absence. Although staff admitted that client appeared to be under the influence of unknown substance, client was described by staff as coherent and aware of client's surroundings. Client did not make any suicidal statement. Client interacted with multiple staff and other clients. Client became upset after contraband items were discovered in client's bedroom while staff was assisting client in searching for client's phone. Client walked out of the facility and refused any redirection from two staff who followed client outside the facility. Client briefly engaged in conversation with a homeless person then client walked down the sidewalk, entered the street and was struck by a vehicle. One staff ran to where the client was, and the other staff went inside the facility to call 911 and inform other staff. First responders arrived on scene and declared client deceased. Facility staff interviewed were consistent in describing client's behavior and issues with unauthorized absences and substance abuse. There were no records provided to the facility to indicate that client was suicidal after client was discharged from a 72 hour hold the client was placed on while on unauthorized absence. Staff stated that client did not appear to be a danger to self or others, so staff had no reason to restrain client from leaving. The facility's surveillance video supported the account of the incident outside the facility as described by two staff who followed the client until the client was struck. Law enforcement reviewed a neighbor's surveillance video from the other side of the street showing client standing in the center median prior to walking into the street. The video was not very clear, and it is unknown if client walked into traffic on purpose or by accident. Based on the information gathered, although the allegation may have happened or is valid, the preponderance of evidence to prove the allegation was not met, therefore, the allegation is unsubstantiated. An exit interview was conducted. A copy of this report, Confidential Names Form, and Appeal Rights were provided by email to the facility representative. LPA requested for the report to be reviewed, signed and emailed back to the LPA. There were no deficiencies cited during this inspection.

narrative: On April 6, 2021 at 10: AM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Jean Herring made an unannounced Case Management tele-Inspection with Daughter Project Girls Home via Microsoft Teams meeting app. Remote "tele-inspection" of facilities is a part of Community Care Licensing Division's emergency response to the spread of Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19). LPA met with Jennifer Jensen, CEO; Charity Jensen, Head of Programs; Ivette Diaz, Head of Service; and Erin Robinson, Facility Manager. The purpose of the tele-inspection was to follow up on a death incident report received by the Department on 11/30/2020. LPA Herring conducted an initial follow up call to the facility on 11/30/2020 and completed a Case Management Tele-inspection on 12/1/2020. Investigation Branch (IB) Investigator Maria Barragan completed an investigation and the findings were delivered to the facility by LPA Irene Yamamoto on 3/10/21 via Complaint Investigation Report (LIC 9099). Summary of Incident: The STRTP reported that on Wednesday, November 25, 2020 (Thanksgiving eve), shortly after running away from the facility, C1 died after being hit by a vehicle. The STRTP reported that the youth was upset due to facility staff confiscating contraband found in her bedroom. The youth left the facility unauthorized, followed by facility staff who maintained the youth in sight, and attempted to verbally redirect the youth to return. Facility staff observed the client walk into the street where she was struck by an on-coming vehicle. The staff person immediately contacted 911 and officers from the Bakersfield Police Department, the Bakersfield Fire Department and Paramedics responded within minutes. The Bakersfield Fire Department pronounced the client deceased at the scene. Investigation revealed that although facility staff admitted C1 was under the influence of drugs the day she was struck by a vehicle (11/25/20), they stated that she was not restrained because she was coherent, aware of her surroundings and made no suicidal statements. (See LIC 9102TA - Technical Assistance). A review of records revealed the following: (page 1) 1.) Several unreported incidents of C1's AWOLs, substance abuse and unsafe behaviors. Facility did not report the following unusual incidents to the Department: (See LIC Deficiency page.) On 11/17/20, staff observed C1 smoking marijuana during a room check at 12: PM. C1 also left the facility unauthorized twice later that day. On 11/20/20, C1 took a piece of glass from a broken window on the van and stated she's going to use it to harm herself. Staff redirected C1 and was able to retrieve the piece of glass. At 8: AM, C1 left the facility and returned at 9: AM with a box of hair dye. About an hour later, C1 left again twice for a few minutes saying she was leaving to smoke. At 6: PM, C1 left the facility unauthorized stating she's going to Disneyland. On 11/23/20, C1 returned from unauthorized absence at 9: AM with a bag of clothing, a cell phone and a credit card. Later that morning, C1 went with staff and peers to the park. As C1 was getting into the van to return to the facility, she met a stranger in the parking lot and took a cup of juice from that person. Staff told C1 she would not be allowed to take the cup in the van if there was alcohol in it. C1 became angry and ran off. She then got on a public bus but staff was able to chase the bus and ask the bus driver not to take off. Staff was able to persuade C1 to get off and return to the facility with staff. C1 appeared to be hallucinating on the way back to the facility. At about 6: PM, C1 walked out of the facility. While C1 was out, staff performed a room search and found a bag of crystal meth and eye brow razors in C1's room. C1 returned 30 minutes later. At 8: PM, C1 came downstairs very upset accusing staff of taking her belongings. At 10: PM, C1 left the facility again. On 11/24/20, C1 returned to the facility at 8: AM. C1 appeared to be under the influence of some unknown substance. C1 was still upset from the previous day. She continued to complain about staff confiscating her drugs and credit card and demanded staff to return her credit card. C1 refused to eat her afternoon snack and dinner due to being upset. At 8: PM, C1 left the facility unauthorized. C1's psychotropic medications were not administered from November 14 thru 16 and from November 18 thru 24, 2020. 2.) Facility did not notify the Department of the following unusual incidents within the required time frame: (See LIC 9102TV Advisory Notes - Technical Violation for details.) On Sunday 11/15/20, C1 left the facility unauthorized at 10: PM. On Monday, 11/16/20 at approximately 1: PM, officers from the Bakersfield Police Department (BPD) arrived at the facility and informed staff that C1 had been taken to the emergency room. Staff went to the hospital to be with C1. (page 2) During a urine test, a nurse found a drug pipe that had been hidden inside of C1's body. After this discovery, C1 became hostile and accused the staff and the nurse of giving her illegal drugs and paraphernalia. Consequently, C1 was taken to a crisis facility. The facility did not file an incident report for this incident until 11/23/20, which was after LPA Herring contacted the facility and inquired about whether there were any incidents involving C1. On Wednesday 11/18/20, C1 left the facility with her peer without permission. While leaving the facility, the clients informed the staff that they were leaving to do drugs and kill themselves. The facility filed an incident report for this incident on 11/20/20 (2 business days after the incident). 3.) There's no documentation of a completed standard appraisal for C1 on a form approved and/or furnished by the licensing agency as specified in STRTP Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) Section 87068.1 (c)(1)(C). (See LIC 9102TV Advisory Notes - Technical Violation for details.) 4.) There's no documentation of a completed initial crisis management assessment for C1 prior to placement in, or immediately after admission to the facility as required. A Safety Plan was provided to IB later during the investigation, however, it does not include all required components specified in STRTP Interim Licensing Standards Section 87068.1 (d). (See LIC 9102TV Advisory Notes - Technical Violation for details.) 5.) C1's Needs and Services Plan (NSP) does not meet the ILS requirements. It was also noted that C1's NSP was not created until 11/24/20 and signed/dated by the facility's Head of Service (HOS) on 11/25/20 (the day C1 passed away.) In addition, there's no documentation that the child, and her authorized representative(s), and the child and family team (CFT) were offered the opportunity to participate in the development of the NSP as required. (See LIC 9102TV Advisory Notes - Technical Violation for details.) 6.) All Medication Administration Records (MARs) for C1 are missing page 2 of the form. Per C1's MARs (page 1), medications were not administered from November 14 thru 16 and from November 18 thru 24, 2020. There's no documentation of reasons why medications were not administered and who was notified when medications were not administered. (See LIC 9102TV Advisory Notes - Technical Violation for details.) 7.) The facility's Program Statement does not describe core services and supports for clients with a history of substance abuse. In addition, C1's Needs and Services Plan does not contain Core Services and Supports offered to C1. (See LIC 9102TV Advisory Notes - Assistance for details.) (page 3) LPA Herring provided five (5) Advisory Notes -Technical Violation (LIC 9102TV) and two (2) Advisory Notes - Technical Assistance (LIC 9102TA). One (1) deficiency was cited from the California Code of Regulations, Title 22. Appeal Rights provided. The tele-inspection ended at 11: AM. A signed copy of this report was provided to the licensee along with LIC 809D, LIC 9102TVs, LIC9102TAs and LIC811 (Confidential Name/s form). (page 4)

narrative: On September 13, Licensing Program Analysts (LPAs) Jean Herring and Belinda Gilmer conducted an unannounced inspection at the facility at 9: AM. LPAs met with Teodora Corbell, Administrator and Erin Robinson, Acting Administrator. The purpose of the inspection was to conduct an Annual/Required inspection of the facility. Currently, the facility has a provisional Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) license which expires on 11/01/21. The STRTP's Mental Health Program Application is pending approval. The STRTP has obtained national accreditation from Joint Commission. This STRTP is licensed to serve up to ten (10) female ambulatory children ages 12-17 years of age. The facility also provide services to non-minor dependents pursuant to W&I Code 16501.1 (C)(1). There are eight (8) ambulatory minors currently in placement. This facility is a two story home with five (5) bedrooms, four (4) toilets, four (4) bathroom sinks, 3 showers, three (3) offices, kitchen, dining, art room, and visitation room. During the inspection, LPAs conducted a physical plant inspection, interviewed five(5) facility staff, and reviewed operational requirements. Physical Plant The license is posted in a prominent, publicly accessible location in the facility. Disinfectants, cleaning solutions and sharps are locked in a kitchen cabinet. Facility has non-perishable foods for at least one week. Facility provides at least three(3) meals per day. Medications are centrally stored and locked in the office. All kitchen, food preparation, and storage areas are kept clean and free of rodents and other vermin. Facility has one or more carbon monoxide detectors in the facility. Facility provides basic laundry services. A comfortable temperature for clients is maintained at all areas. The hot water temperature was tested and measured at 92 degrees F downstairs and 96 degrees F upstairs. No more than 2 children share a bedroom. All beds are equipped with good springs and a clean mattress; and supplied with pillows which are clean and in good repair. Facility provides age-appropriate clothing items and hygiene products. Operations Facility maintains a current, written plan of operation that meets licensing standards. Facility maintains a register of clients and the register is available upon request. Facility maintains and implements written complaint procedures and the procedures are posted in a publicly accessible location in the facility. The board of directors conducts quarterly meetings. Licensee does not handle cash resources for clients. During the inspection, the following deficiencies were observed: -The facility's current menu plan does not contain the servings recommended in the USDA Food Group Plan for the age group served. -LPAs observed expired bag of french fries in the freezer. -LPAs observed an open package of biscuits in the freezer. -LPAs observed the facility had less than two days of supplies of fresh perishable food on the premises. -The hot water temperature was tested and measured at 92 degrees F downstairs and 96 degrees F upstairs. -The bathroom sink in bath#4 upstairs is clogged and the counter top is peeling; the shower in bedroom#4 is out of order and shower floor needs caulking; some parts of the baseboards in bedroom#4 are missing; the bed in bedroom#4 is sagging in the middle. -The board minutes do not reflect the board's or governing body's discussion of licensing reports. An exit interview was conducted and a signed copy of this report was provided to the facility along with LIC 811 (Confidential Name/s) list). Appeal rights explained.

Licensee has not obtained written approval from the children's representatives prior to implementing their needs and services plans (NSPs). Client records do not contain case plans and there's no documentation of attempts made to obtain the case plan. Client records do not contain modifications to Needs and Services Plans (NSPs) at least every 30 days. Client records do not contain initial crisis management assessment. narrative: C1 stated that staff was not informed about the stolen cash or body suit and that it might have happened in May or June of this year. Also, that no one else witnessed this incident. It was alleged that staff do not respect resident's privacy. Staff denied the allegation and stated that they announce themselves by knocking on the door and then proceeding to unlock their room to conduct their hourly safety check. C1 stated that staff does not knock on their door before unlocking it. C6 stated that sometimes they do knock on the door and then staff enters their room. It was alleged that staff forces resident to attend medical appointments. Staff denied the allegation. Interviews conducted with S1-S5 revealed that staff does not force residents to attend their medical appointments. C1 & C6 stated that depending on how they are feeling that day they will choose to attend or decline to go to their medical appointments but that sometimes they feel like they are being forced to go. Staff encourages residents to attend their medical/therapy appointments by earning additional allowance money or by earning tickets with the incentive point system. Staff, however, reminds the residents of their child guidance, medical and therapeutic appointments but ultimately it is the residents choice to attend or refuse these appointments. It was alleged that staff did not intervene when resident was verbally abused by another resident. Staff denied the allegation. Staff revealed that when residents are verbally abused by other residents the staff tries to de-escalate the situation by separating the residents from each other and offering to take them out for a ride to calm them down before it turns to a physical altercation. C1 stated that sometimes the staff does not do anything to intervene and was unable to provide dates of similar incidents. However, C1 feels that staff is not doing enough to intervene and that they should do more. C6 stated that when residents get into verbal fights the staff might try to intervene and distract them from the other resident. It was alleged that facility is not maintained clean, sanitary and in good repair at all times. Staff denied the allegation. Interviews conducted revealed that the facility is maintained clean, sanitary and in good repair at all times. During, LPAs inspection on 06/19/21 the facility was clean, sanitary and in good repair. LPA inspected the residents rooms and observed them to be sanitary and furniture in good repair. Staff stated that when something is broken the administrator is informed so that it can be fixed or replaced. C1 & C6 could not provide dates of any time a fixture or furniture was broken or needed repair. LPA tried to interview C2-C5 on 06/19/21 but they declined to be interviewed. Therefore, due to conflicting statements and information not reported to staff by the residents and no other witnesses the allegations cannot be substantiated. The documents reviewed did not identify any specific information related to these allegations or of incidents occurring. Based on the information gathered, although the allegation may have happened or is valid, the preponderance of evidence to prove the allegation was not met, therefore, the allegation is unsubstantiated. An exit interview was conducted. A copy of this report, Confidential Names Form, and Appeal Rights were provided to the facility representative. There were no deficiencies cited during this inspection.

Staff further stated that allowances are assessed and given by the Administrator. LPA reviewed the attendance log for first client provided by the school in which she attended at the time. Document showed this client had missed approximately 46 days of school from February to May 2021 with additional days identified as possibly not attending full days. Progress notes also showed that this client did not attend various therapy sessions throughout that same period. Allowance logs showed that this client signed for and received allowances with varying deductions from the facility. Facility identified why amounts were lowered due to children not following agreed upon program. However, LPA was unable to decipher specific dates as to when deductions were made. It was also alleged that staff refused to take client to store because she did not attend school. Interviews conducted with one client stated that S1 refused to take her to the store because she did not attend school or therapy. Another client stated that staff have refused to take children to the store in the past but was unsure of which staff refused or why. Both clients that were interviewed were unable to provide dates, times, or specific details surrounding the incidents. Interviews conducted with staff (S2-S4) had similar statements in that staff try to follow companies' policies and procedures and that they are not aware of any staff not being compliant with that. Staff further stated if children do not attend school or therapy, they get blacked out meaning they do not go on outings unless it's an emergency or they need essential items. Documents reviewed did not identify staff not taking children on essential outings based on not attending therapy or school. Lastly, it was alleged that staff did not clean or replace client's backpack after being thrown in the trash. One client stated that S1 mixed up their backpack with someone else and ultimately threw the backpack in the trash. However, initial statements made by one client were indecisive in that names of staff differed as to who was involved in the incident of throwing away the backpack. Another client stated they did not recall an incident with a backpack missing or that being an issue within the facility. Staff denied not cleaning or providing a new backpack to any clients. Staff stated if a backpack or personal item was ever observed in the trash staff would clean or replace the item. Documents reviewed did not identify any specific information related to these allegations or of incidents occurring. Based on the information gathered, although the allegation may have happened or is valid, the preponderance of evidence to prove the allegation was not met, therefore the allegation is unsubstantiated. An exit interview was conducted. A copy of this report Confidential Names Form, and Appeal Rights were provided to the facility representative via electronic mail. There were no deficiencies cited during this inspection.

In the other video, LPA Mundo observed two (2) foster children fighting in the facility parking lot while one staff does not intervene. Suddenly you see another facility staff step in between the foster children breaking up the fight by creating space. It was alleged that facility serves inadequate and poor quality food. narrative: On July 10, 2024, at 10:00 a.m., Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) John Bonilla and Licensing Program Manager (LPM) Jean Herring conducted an announced Pre-licensing inspection at Valpredo Avenue, Bakersfield, CA 93313.
