On December 12, 2024 at 10:00 a.m., Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) John Bonilla conducted an unannounced Post Licensing inspection at Daughter Project Girls Home, a Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP). LPA met with Saquintha Magee, Facility Manager. The facility currently has a STRTP license and is licensed to serve ten (10) ambulatory clients age 12 to 17 years old. The facility also provides service to non-minor dependents (NMDs) pursuant to W&I CODE 16501.1(C)(1). There are currently 5 clients, none which are NMDs, at the facility. LPA requested the following: Board of Director Meeting Minutes. The facility is a one-story home with a loft space upstairs and big yard both in front and in the back. The facility has 5 bedrooms, 3.5 bathrooms (including one staff restroom), 2 offices for therapists and administrative staff, living room, dining room, kitchen, laundry room, and activity room (upstairs loft). There are no firearms or ammunition in the facility. There are no bodies of water on the facility premises. LPA conducted a walk-through of the entire facility. Physical Plant The license, facility sketch, personal rights, emergency disaster form, complaints poster, emergency phone numbers and food menu are posted in a prominent, publicly accessible location in the facility. Disinfectants and cleaning solutions are kept inaccessible and locked in a cabinet located in the kitchen and staff office. Sharps/knives are inaccessible and stored in a locked drawer in the kitchen. Facility has non-perishable food for at least one week and perishable food for at least two days. Medications are centrally stored in a locked cabinet in the office. Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors were tested and in proper working order. Fire extinguishers were fully charged. Room temperatures are maintained at around 66-71 degrees F. The hot water temperature was tested and measured at 108 degrees F. All sinks, showers and toilets are in working order. All beds are in good repair; equipped with good springs, clean mattresses and pillows. Adequate supply of beddings and linens were observed. Overall, facility is clean, safe, sanitary and in good repair. Operations Facility maintains a current, written plan of operation that meets licensing standards. Facility maintains a register of clients and the register is available upon request. Facility maintains and implements written complaint procedures and the procedures are posted in a publicly accessible location in the facility. The board of directors regularly conducts meeting to review and discuss the STRTP's operation. Cash resources are kept on the facility premises in a locked and secure location. Disaster Preparedness Plan Facility maintains a current LIC610C. Written disaster and mass casualty plan of action has been provided and is available at the facility. Emergency Intervention Plan Facility maintains a monthly log of each use of manual restraints that contains all required information. The log is available for review by the Department upon request. LPA observed documentation of Emergency Intervention Training and on-going training. Core/Therapeutic Services Facility provides core services and supports to children and non-minor dependents as appropriate or necessary that are trauma informed, culturally relevant, age and developmentally appropriate and include the following: Medi-Cal specialty mental health services; transition support services; educational and physical, behavioral, and mental health supports; activities to support children and non-minor dependents and services to achieve permanency. During today's inspection, the STRTP was provided four (4) Advisory Notes/Technical Violations (LIC9102TVs). An exit interview was conducted A signed copy of this report, LIC Confidential names list dated 12/12/24, LIC9102TVs, and appeal rights were provided to Joellen Gutierrez, Administrator.. A follow-up is required to complete inspection.

On December 12, 2024 at 10:00 a.m., Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) John Bonilla conducted an unannounced inspection at Daughter Project Girls Home, a Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) for the purpose of conducting a Case Management inspection concerning a Special Incident Report (SIR) received by the Department on November 8, 2024. LPA met with Joellen Gutierrez, Administrator. On November 8, 2024, the Department received an SIR indicating that on November 7, a facility staff (S1) (See LIC Confidential Names list dated 12/12/24) was driving three facility clients (C1, C2, and C3) from an outing when one of the clients asked staff to pull over due to feeling ill. S1 did not immediately pull over, which led to an escalated confrontation. No deficiencies were cited during this inspection. A signed copy of this report and LIC811 were provided to Joellen Gutierrez, Administrator. Exit interview conducted. Follow-up is required before completion.

Interviews conducted with four (4) children identified that staff are not allowing children go to school and that staff are not enrolling them in the schools they wish to be at. Children stated they were not given the opportunity to choose what school they wanted to attend, and that staff are not allowing them to go every day. Documents reviewed identified children signing they understood the schedules and the schools they would be attending. Additionally, documents identified that children were enrolled to attend school on one day as the school agreement signed by children. Interviews conducted with county social workers identified working with facility and children to get enrolled in the proper schools during time in which facility relocated. It was also alleged; facility staff are not ensuring that minor is provided hygiene product. Staff denied the allegation. Staff stated that children are given opportunity to get hygiene items throughout the month depending on the need. Staff stated that facility also keeps additional hygiene items in cases of emergency if children may need it. Interviews conducted with all children identified not receiving hygiene items and that staff deny children from obtaining hygiene items. LPA toured facility and observed children to have hygiene items available and additional products within the facility for emergency purposes for all children in care. Furthermore, it was alleged facility staff are not ensuring that minor is provided an age-appropriate allowance. Staff denied the allegation. Staff stated that children receive allowances and sign that they obtained it. However, staff state that money is kept on a card and that children are encouraged to save some of their money. Children stated they are not given allowances and that staff do not provide them with the appropriate amounts of money for allowance. Documents reviewed identified children signing for receiving allowances and identified within their needs and service plans it identified how much children could maintain on their persons. It was alleged, facility staff are supplying alcohol to minors in care. Staff denied the allegation. Staff stated that children have sometimes come into the facility intoxicated or try to bring alcohol into the facility. However, staff stated if children are caught with contraband, they confiscate contraband and document incident to report to proper overseeing agencies. Children were unable to identify which staff if any supplied alcohol to children, when or where. Children were unable to provide a date of occurrence or how staff were able to get alcohol within the facility. Additionally, it was alleged facility staff are not preventing minors from using substances while in care. Staff denied the allegation. Staff stated that children have been observed passing vape pens and other contraband. Staff identified when they observe children using substances, they verbally ask children to hand over the contraband or if children do not give staff the contraband staff will confiscate it when observed available for staff to take away. Staff stated they document incidents and report incidents to overseeing agencies. LPA observed staff redirecting children when staff identified children were observed passing a vape pen. Staff stated they asked for children to stop and to hand over the vape pen and children did not. Staff completed incident reports to document incident. Interviews conducted with children identified that staff would confiscate their contraband or request they give it to them but that they don't want them to take it, so they don't give it to them. Children identified hiding contraband from staff. It was alleged, facility staff are not following proper reporting requirements involving minors in care. Staff denied the allegation. Staff stated they report all incidents that happen in the facility within the time frames to meet reporting requirements. Staff stated that each shift documents what transpires on each shift and incident reports are sent out to overseeing agencies. Children were not able to identify if staff are reporting incidents. Children stated that things have transpired within the facility, but they don't feel as though staff report incidents as nothing is done about it. LPA received documents show casing various incidents transpiring within the facility. Lastly, it was alleged facility is in disrepair. Staff denied the allegation. Staff stated that facility was just relocated approximately 3 weeks ago. Staff stated that they are moving and transitioning a lot of things. Staff provided documentation that home is being exterminated regularly and that home is in the process of updating and transitioning. LPA observed home to be clean and free of obstructions. Facility had completed and full kitchen, rooms had adequate bedding and facility grounds were maintained. Interviews with children identified observing snakes in walls, rats, and bugs within the facility. Documents reviewed showed facility had recently completed a pre licensing and that facility had required items within the home to meet the needs of all children in care. Documents reviewed and interviews conducted showed that children are enrolled or in process of being enrolled in school and that children signed acknowledgment of school schedule. It was also identified that staff report incidents, confiscate contraband and do not supply or allow children to consume alcohol or controlled substances. Based on information gathered, although the allegation may have happened or is valid, the preponderance of evidence to prove the allegation was not met, therefore the allegation is unsubstantiated. An exit interview was conducted. A copy of this report Confidential Names Form, and Appeal Rights were provided to the facility representative. There were no deficiencies cited during this inspection.

narrative: On March 26, 2025 at 3:00 p.m., Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) John Bonilla conducted an unannounced inspection at Daughter Project Girls Home, a Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) for the purpose of concluding a Case Management concerning a Special Incident Report (SIR) received by the Department on November 8, 2024. LPA met with Joellen Gutierrez, Administrator. On November 8, 2024, the Department received an SIR indicating that on November 7, a facility staff (S1) (See LIC Confidential Names list dated 03/26/25) was driving three facility clients (C1, C2, and C3) from an outing when one of the clients asked staff to pull over due to client 2 needing to vomit. Per S1, she was unable to stop the vehicle due to being on the freeway, resulting in clients escalating. When clients began attempting to open the car door, S1 pulled the vehicle over to stop and saw a California Highway Patrol (CHP) officer who she asked for assistance. When S1 went to speak to CHP, she locked the clients in the car. The CHP escorted the group to a gas station. S1 locked the clients in the vehicle while she went inside the gas station to decompress. When S1 returned to the van, the youth exited, followed by S1 locking the clients out of the vehicle. S1 started the van, which caused the doors to unlock, at which time the clients re-entered the vehicle to retrieve their belongings. At this point, S1 pushed C1 out of the front passenger side of the van and made a racist remark, which was overheard by a STRTP staff on the phone. S1 was suspended on November 8, 2024, and terminated on November 13, 2024 as a result of the incident. ... Based on information obtained from incident reports, CPS investigation narrative, and interviews conducted, it was revealed that S1 did not follow the STRTP's plan of operation for de-escalating conflict and managing emergencies. In addition, S1 also violated C1's personal rights. The STRTP was issued three (3) deficiencies. Refer to LIC809D. Exit Interview was conducted. A signed copy of this report, LIC811, and LIC809Ds were provided to Joellen Gutierrez, Administrator. Appeal rights explained.

Based on review of records and e-mails, as well as confidential interviews, it was revealed, that the facility did not meet the reporting requirements for the incident that occurred on 02/22/25 . The incident was not reported to the authorized representative and CCLD until 02/26/25. The second incident, that occurred on 03/15/2025 was reported to CCLD within 24 hr via e-mail, but the final report was not submitted to the Department and authorized representative within 7 days. As a part of investigation, LPA reviewed the SIR folder and was not able to locate the report in the facility folder and requested for the Administrator to e-mail the report to the LPA. The facility had no evidence that the report was emailed to the CCLD within the 7 days from the occurrence. Based on the information collected, the preponderance of evidence has been met, therefore the complaint is SUBSTANTIATED. This violation pose potential Health, Safety, or Personal Rights risk to clients in care. The facility is being cited under ILS 87061(b)(4) for Reporting Requirements on the corresponding LIC9099D page. The copy of this report, LIC 9099D and the appeal rights were given and explained to the Administrator.

This LPA conducted the investigation of the above allegation(s), and it consisted of but was not limited to a review of records, including the client's needs and service plans, police reports, medical records, SIR's and interviews with 2 of 3 staff members (S1) on 4/4/25, (S3) on 4/18/25. No statements were received from S2 as they are no longer employed at the STRTP, and C2 has declined to provide a statement. Reference Confidential Names Form LIC 811, dated August 29, 2025. The Following Allegation(s) were reported: 1. The staff did not prevent the youth from engaging in a physical altercation. The staff refuted the allegation, asserting that on the day of the alleged incident, three staff members were present who were actively involved and took necessary actions to ensure the safety of all clients. The staff reported that they employed crisis communication techniques and verbally guided clients, reminding them to utilize their coping skills, while also attempting to escort both clients to separate areas of the facility. However, C1 and C2 were able to push past the staff, leading to a physical confrontation between them. The staff stated that they promptly positioned themselves between the clients and worked to separate them, with S1 escorting C1 outside in an effort to de-escalate the situation. Furthermore, the staff mentioned that the Kern County Sheriff's Department was contacted during the incident and subsequently arrived at the facility, where they spoke with both clients and removed them from the STRTP, placing them in the Kern County Youth Detention Center. Confidential statements from C1 and C3 supported the staff's account of the events, confirming that the staff intervened by verbally redirecting and stepping in between the two clients, escorting them to different sections of the facility. C1 and C3 expressed that they feel secure living at the STRTP and acknowledged the staff's involvement in their daily activities. Continued... Additionally, police reports acquired from the Kern County Sheriff's Department indicated that both C1 and C2 participated in a physical confrontation, with both parties regarded as aggressors towards one another. Consequently, they were expelled from the facility and transferred to the Kern County Youth Detention Center without any further incidents. Therefore, based on the information received, the above allegation(s) is determined to be unsubstantiated. Although the allegation(s) may have happened are valid, there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that the alleged violations occurred, therefore the allegations are found to be unsubstantiated. Appeal Rights were provided and discussed with the Foster Family Agency. There are no deficiencies to be cited at this time. An exit interview was conducted and a copy of the report along with the (LIC 811) was left with the STRTP Program Coordinator.

The facility is a two-story home located in a residential neighborhood and it is set up as follows: 4 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms, a living room, a dining room, kitchen, staff office, a basement, a laundry area, an activity room, a detached garage, and a backyard. Bedrooms #1 is equipped with two twin beds, two dressers, a closet and there are two window. LPA observed the drawers on one of the dressers need to be fixed and a small hole in the wall above that dresser. Bedroom #2 is equipped with two twin beds, two dressers, and a closet. This room shares a Jack and Jill restroom with bedroom #3. LPA observed the bathroom door on located in bedroom #2 to be coming off the hinges at the top and a hole in the screens on the windows. Bedroom #3 is equipped with two twin beds, two dressers and was observed to have adequate closet space. Bedroom #4 is utilized as the facility's therapy room and it is equipped with a couch and two chairs. Bathrooms were checked and found to be in working order. The hot water was tested, and the temperature was found to be between 105-120 degrees (F). The living room and dining room furniture was in good repair. The kitchen was observed to be clean and was equipped with a 5-burner gas stove, a refrigerator/freezer, dishwasher, and a microwave. The kitchen trash can was covered with a lid. The facility was observed to have a two-day supply of perishable foods and a one-week supply of non-perishable food and appear to be following the posted menu. All sharp knives are kept locked in the staffing office located off the kitchen and made inaccessible to clients in care. All prescribed medications are centrally stored in a locked cabinet in the laundry area and made only accessible to employees. Report continued on LIC 809-C. The first aid kit was checked and found to be complete. Smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors were tested were in appropriate working order. The facility has regulation fire extinguishers. LPA observed the facility to have adequate indoor and outdoor activity space. The front and backyards were inspected and found to be clean and free of debris and observable hazards. LPA observed the detached garage to be used for storage. All required forms are posted. The Administrator is present at the facility a minimum of 20 hours a week, as verified by the staff schedule. Appropriate staff/client ratios were verified during this inspection. The facility employs Facility Managers and 10 direct care staff. LPA discussed the following with the Administrator: Incident reporting, including incidents related to Law Enforcement contacts as well as incidents involving Emergency Intervention. Personnel files were not reviewed as files are maintained off-site. Client records were reviewed and found to be missing CFT documentation and timely Needs and Services Plans. LPA discussed the deficiencies found during today's inspection. LPA will return at a later date to cite deficiencies found. A copy of this report was left with the Facility Administrator.

On August 28, 2025, at 12: PM Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Timika Martin conducted an unannounced inspection at Dignity STRTP and met with Administrator, Farrah Richmond for the purpose of delivering an amended report regarding a case management deficiency that was issued on July 16, 2025. The facility was issued a citation using the incorrect regulation. The regulation used to cite applies to Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Programs (STRTP) serving more than six children and requires at least two awake and on duty direct care staff present at the facility during the hours of 10PM to 7AM. Dignity is licensed for six or fewer children and per regulation is required to have one awake and on duty direct care staff for every six children, or fraction thereof, present, at a minimum during the hours of 10PM to 7AM. Therefore, the deficiency that was cited on July 16, 2025, does not apply to your facility. Dignity was in compliance with the ILS regulations. Based on review, the deficiency is dismissed. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of the report was left with the Administrator, Farrah Richmond.

Based on the information obtained from confidential statements and documentary evidence, it was revealed that new staff had transported a resident to a dispensary. Confidential interviews determined that an incident report was not completed due to the incident being perceived to be a "teachable moment" training opportunity for the new staff member. Statements further reveal staff did not intentionally drive the minor to a smoke shop/dispensary, but rather, they went to an alternate location believing it was the approved destination of a 7-Eleven (convenience store). Once at the location, staff attempted to instruct minor to leave the location and requested the store staff to not sell anything to the minor due to their age. The investigation found that the incident occurred due to a miscommunication and a lack of understanding protocol by staff who were still in training. Confidential statements obtained further reveal denial that staff transport residents to obtain marijuana or allow residents to use marijuana/drugs in the facility. Statements obtained do not support reports of staff speaking inappropriately to either of the residents. Based on confidential interviews there is not enough evidence to support reported allegations that Staff contribute to the delinquency of minors, staff do not prevent minors from smoking in the facility, or that staff speaks inappropriately to a minor. Therefore, the allegations are deemed Unsubstantiated. There are no deficiencies per California Code of Regulations, Title 22, or Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) cited at this time. narrative: Staff 1 was not in the immediate location where the incident took place but within view point. Staff 1 was monitoring other clients with the intention to not engage. C2 sustained four to five punches from C1 during the altercation. An internal investigation was conducted by Leroy Wise (Administrator, Dimondale Adolescent) on March 9, 2021. The internal report stated on bullet 5, "staff were able to de-escalate the situation by separating the girls and escorting them to different locations in the facility". Based on information reviewed by this analyst, the successful de-escalation occurred after the altercation between C1, C2 and C3 had ended. Bullet 7 of the internal report states that Staff 1 and Staff 2 were "new to the agency" and had not completed the Professional Assault Crisis Training (Pro Act). A review of the staff training records confirm the completion of 16 hours of Pro Act training by Staff 1 and Staff 2 on March 16, 2021. The investigation finding is substantiated, meaning that the allegation is valid because the preponderance of the evidence standard has been met. Facility cited for violation of Interim Licensing Standard V3 87072(d)(11) Personal Rights. Exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this report was emailed to Leroy Wise to sign and return.
investigation_findings: 13On May 6, 2021 at 1:15 pm, Out of State Certification Analyst, Ron Leslie conducted a a follow-up complaint investigation via telephone with Leroy Wise, Administrator, to discuss complaint allegations. On 08/24/ Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Bernice Karnsrithong arrived at the facility at 11am for delivering findings for case management-incident. Health and safety risk assessment was conducted upon arriving at the facility. The Special Incident Report (SIR) stated that on 07/11/2022 clients reported to morning staff that on 07/10/2022 after returning from community pass, there was no staff onsite to receive clients. Staff were offsite on an outing. LPA Karnsrithong met with Ashley Ross, Interim Administrator. During this case management-incident, LPA Karnsrithong conducted confidential interviews and reviewed documentary evidences. Based on confidential interviews and documentation received, staff on 07/10/2022 were not present when clients came back from a community pass later that evening. Statements and documentary evidences were consistent that two (2) staff members accompanied clients to an outing in the mall, while two (2) clients were out on a community pass. Facility is cited for incompliance with Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards Article 6, 87065. Direct Care Staff/Child Ratios which states: (a) In a facility with a licensed capacity of six or fewer children, there shall be coverage by direct care staff as follows: (1) During the hours of 7 am to 10 pm, there shall be one awake and on duty direct care staff for every three children, or fraction thereof, present, at a minimum. (3) In addition to staff required in paragraph 1 or 2, when one or more children are present at the facility, at least one direct care staff shall be on call and capable of arriving at the facility site within 30 minutes. This is a Type A violation as it is an immediate risk to the personal rights of children in care. Exit interview, plan of correction, and appeals were discussed with Interim Administrator.

narrative: Information obtained revealed on November 21, 2022, during an outing to the beach, two residents allegedly stole alcohol from a retail store where two facility staff and residents stopped before going to the beach. Documentary evidence indicates residents consumed alcohol in the vehicle to and from the beach which went unnoticed by two staff members. Confidential statements revealed S1 drank alcohol with the youth at the beach. Statements also revealed that residents displayed signs of intoxication; however, Staff failed to notice a difference in behavior from intoxicated residents. Confidential statements and documentary evidence further revealed that on unspecified dates, between June 30, 2022 and February 14, 2023, S1 provided marijuana to residents in the form of a vape pen while at the facility. The investigation found that S1 would drink alcohol and smoke marijuana at the facility, sometimes with other residents. On February 13, 2023, evidence obtained reveals S1 engaging in a verbal altercation with a youth resident while at the facility in which S1 displays unprofessionalism when addressing the resident as "dumb" "stupid" "bitch" and telling the resident to "shut the fuck up." The investigation further revealed from confidential statements, photographs, and video, that staff demonstrate failure to provide adequate supervision. Video footage reviewed shows a facility staff member observed looking at youths and not attempting to stop or de-escalate a physical fight between two youth residents. Additionally, an unidentified individual is heard saying "Let them fight." Based on gathered information the preponderance of evidence standard has been met. The Department has determined substantiated findings that Facility staff contributed alcohol/marijuana to minors and that Staff failed to supervise residents which contributed to residents fighting, consuming alcohol, and marijuana. This poses an immediate health, safety, and personal rights risk to children in care. The facility is issued citations per INTERIM LICENSING STANDARDS Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program, Articles Through Version 4; 87065. PERSONNEL DUTIES and PERSONAL RIGHTS. An exit interview was conducted, appeal rights were discussed, and a copy of this report, and appeal rights were provided to the Administrator. (Continued on page LIC9099-D)

On 01/18/2022 at 10am, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA), Bernice Karnsrithong arrived at Dimondale Adolescent Care Facility #4 for the purpose of conducting an annual inspection. LPA Karnsrithong met with Administrator, Samone Kelly who provided access and tour to the facility. The facility is licensed to provide care and supervision up to six (6) clients ages twelve (12) to seventeen (17) and non minor dependents. The facility is located in a residential area. The facility conducts Covid-19 checks upon entering. A staff member checks in guests and residents upon entrance. LPA Karnsrithong reviewed two (2) staff files and interviewed (2) two staff during the inspection. LPA Karnsrithong has observed (1) one operating fire extinguisher located in the kitchen and (1) fire alarm in the living room and (2) two carbon monoxide detectors in the hallways. There are 2 (two) direct care staff for each shift. Therapist comes in from 12pm to 8pm and Activity Coordinators comes in from 1:30pm to 11:30pm. Facility Supervisor shift is from 12pm to 8pm, Mondays thru Fridays. The facility ratio is (3) three staff to (6) children. CARF Accreditation for the facility is valid until October 31, 2023. First Aid kit is available at the office and at the facility vehicle. LPA Karnsrithong interviewed (1) one client during the visit. During the inspection LPA Karnsrithong has observed the following: Office Room: There are three (3) desks and a computer, chairs and locked cabinets. The office room is located next to the front door. Clients are not permitted to use the office unless a staff is present. All facility logs are in the office room. (Medication, Facility Disinfecting Schedule, Meal Counts, Maintenance Logs, Activity Log, Disaster Drills, Shift Exchange Log, and Temperature Logs) The medication is kept locked in the staff office and only staff have access to the medications. Licensing postings are posted in the office room (i.e. Administrator Certification, Mental Health Certification, Emergency Disaster Plan).Disinfecting and cleaning supplies are stored and locked in the office room. Contraceptives are stored in the office room but is available for clients when needed. Child Family Team (CFT) meetings are typically held in the office. (Page 1 of 3) Bedrooms: There are (3) three rooms in the facility. All rooms are occupied by clients. There are (2) two twin size beds, adequate drawer space, closet and lighting. There is ample space for clients to store their personal belongings in their rooms and all bedroom furniture are in good working condition. Hallway: Bill of Rights and House Client Schedules are posted in the hallway. There is a desk and a table for clients to do schoolwork if needed. Living Room/Common Room: The living room is located directly in front of the entry way. There are (2) two sofas, an office desk, (1) one desk chair and a television. The desk is to be used by both clients and staff as needed. There is a bookshelf with books for clients to use as well. Clients chore list is also posted in the living room. Bathrooms: There are (2) two bathrooms. One bathroom is dedicated for staff and one for clients. Both bathrooms have a working shower, toilet, and sink. Both bathrooms are kept clean and in sanitary and in good working condition. Clients may use the staff bathroom if needed. Due to Covid, the staff bathroom is kept open for clients to use. Kitchen: There is a long dining table with chairs. There is a stove/oven with five (5) burners and center grill and is in good working condition at the time of the inspection. There is refrigerator which contains ample perishable food supplies for clients. There is a microwave and a toaster. There are (2) two cabinets being used as a pantry for non-perishable food items. The trash can has a tight lid on. There are utensils, plates and cookware also stored in the kitchen for clients and staff to use. Menu are posted in the refrigerator. There is (1) one working fire extinguisher in the kitchen. Kitchen is scheduled to be remodeled by this week. Therapy Room: There is a private office space located in the backyard. This room is used for therapeutic services for clients. In house Therapy services are provided from 12pm to 8pm from Mondays to Fridays. Private meetings are also held in the therapy room if needed. (Page 2 of 3) Outside Area: The backyard is fenced in and gated. There is an outdoor patio furniture with table and chairs located in the backyard. There are sports equipment that is also used by clients. There is a garden that is well maintained. The utility shut off valves are located in the side of the house. Clients have access to safe outdoor activity safe at all times. All passageways and stairs are unobstructed and free of any debris. On February 11, 2022 at 3: PM Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Regina Martin conducted a Case Management - Incident investigation at Dimondale Adolescent Care Facility #4 and met with Facility Representative. LPA further spoke with Samone Kelly, Facility Administrator. The purpose of this inspection was to deliver findings from Investigation regarding incident report #763148, dated July 7, 2021. The incident was investigated by Community Care Licensing (CCL), Investigations Bureau, Investigator Edward Hector. On July 7, 2021, CCL received incident report #763148 reporting alleged sexual abuse on Client #1 (C1) by an unidentified male on July 6, 2021 while inside of the facility at approximately AM. During the investigation, confidential interviews and statements were obtained and corresponding records reviewed. It was revealed on July 6, 2021, clients invited and allowed two unknown male individuals into the facility through an exterior door leading to client's room. According to records, C1 engaged in consensual sex then later, reported rape once the police were called to respond to the facility. While the alleged "rape" of C1 has not been confirmed at this time, the preponderance of the evidence standard has been met to support a lack of supervision leading to unknown individuals entering into client's room at the facility, C1 engaging in sexual intercourse at the facility and individuals exiting the facility all without staff's knowledge. Based on gathered information during the investigation, licensee failed to ensure enough supervision for client's safety resulting in unidentified male presence in the facility which poses an immediate Health, Safety and Personal Rights risk to residents in care. The facility is issued a citation in accordance Per California Code Regulation, Title 22, Division 6, Chapter 1, General Licensing Regulations, Responsibility for Providing Care and Supervision (Continued on page LIC809-D) Exit interview was conducted and a copy of this report and appeal rights were emailed to Facility Administrator.

narrative: Confidential statements revealed that former resident, Youth #1 (Y1) provided other youths access to illegal drugs (Percocet and marijuana) while in care at the facility (See LIC811, dated 10/13/2023). While there is not enough evidence to prove that youth were using ecstasy at the facility, statements obtained revealed Y1 would bring the drugs into the facility after a home visit with their biological parent. Youth #1 would also have the drugs delivered curbside at the facility by an unknown vehicle. Information further revealed the vehicle would pull up curbside in front of the facility, Y1 would walk outside the front door of the facility to the vehicle, take the drugs and place them on their person (in their clothing), Y1 would then walk inside the facility to their room and use the drugs. It was revealed staff's attempts to confiscate the drugs from Y1, Y1 would refuse consent and staff were unsuccessful. The investigation also revealed on other occasions Y1 would smoke marijuana in the back yard of the facility. Confidential statements revealed staffs were unable to confiscate the drugs and would routinely stand outside with the residents and watch them smoke marijuana. The staff would reportedly document the incidents. Based on the timeline of the events, record review and confidential interviews, the investigation determined substantiated findings that Y1 provided other minors access to illegal drugs (Percocet and marijuana) while in care. This poses an immediate health, safety, and personal rights risk of harm to children placed in care. The facility is issued a citation in accordance with the Interim Licensing Standards, Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program, Articles Through Version 4; 87078(b) RESPONSIBILITY FOR PROVIDING CARE AND SUPERVISION and BUILDINGS AND GROUNDS. [See page LIC9099-D for cited deficiencies]. An exit interview was conducted. A copy of this report, and appeal rights were provided to the Facility Representative. During the investigation confidential statements revealed that former resident, Youth #2 (Y2) resided at the facility from April 27. 2022 through March 7, 2023, at which time Y2 (AWOLed) left the facility without permission [See LIC811, dated, 10/13/23]. On February 17, 2023, Y2 informed their Social Worker of concerns they were having with their roommate and further informed facility staff. On February 19, 2023, Y2 was instructed by staff to write a statement of their concerns. On or around March 4, 2023, Y2 wrote a statement to staff requesting in part, a room change due to their complaints concerning their roommate (Y1). On March 7, 2023, Y2 left the facility after providing staff with the written statement and prior to staff completing the requested room change. Youth #1 (Y1) denies allegations of inappropriate sexual interactions. Confidential statements and documentary evidence determined no corroborating evidence or witnesses to the alleged; therefore, the findings alleging inappropriate interactions between youth, minor not feeling safe at the facility, minor leaving from facility without permission, staff not protecting minor from being bullied and staff not providing a safe and comfortable environment for minor in care are deemed Unsubstantiated; meaning that, although the allegations may have happened or are valid, there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that a violation occurred. Exit interview conducted. A copy of the report is left with Facility Representative.

This facility is currently licensed to care for a maximum of six (6) ambulatory only children, ages 12-17 years, as well as non-minor dependents. This is a one-story home, located in a residential neighborhood, with three (3) bedrooms and two (2) bathrooms, living room, dining room, one staff office, an office for therapeutic services, backyard, and garage. There are no security bars on the windows, there are no firearms or dangerous weapons, and there are no active facility cameras on the facility premises. There is also no pool or bodies of water on the premises. Interim Administrator, Miracle Murray-McKnight provided a tour of the entire physical plant both inside and out. The facility is set up as follows: All bedrooms furnished with sufficient lighting, drawer and closet space, comfortable mattresses, and clean linens, blankets, and pillows, all in good repair. Bedrooms 1, 2 and Equipped with 2 twin beds, 2 dressers and enough closet space to accommodate clothing for two clients clothing. Bathrooms #1 is located in the hallway and was clean and in good working condition. Bathroom #2 is located in bed room #3 and was clean and in good working condition. Staff office: Is kept locked and stores cash, first aid kit, and also equipped with a closet, which will store staff and client files. There is a locked closet in the hallway where hygiene boxes and sharps are kept. There is a file cabinet inside also where the medication is kept. Each clients medication was kept in a separate plastic container inside of a locked file cabinet. (Continued on LIC809-C) The Kitchen has a stove, oven, refrigerator and microwave all in good working condition. Threre was a menu located on the refrigerator and a dining room table with seating for the clients. The Backyard was clean and clear of hazards and also where you can find the gas shut off valves. The Front yard was clean and also where you can find the water shut off valves. The garage has two storage refrigerator/freezers that were both stocked with food for the clients. The company vehicle was also in the garage. The registration and insurance were both current and up to date. The vehicle was clean and in good working condition. Clients in care are supervised and protected at all times. Facility personnel instructed to report violations of personal rights. Personal Rights is posted inside the facility. Clients are not restricted in telephone use except by court order. Grievance procedure/ personal rights, menu, emergency disaster plan was posted. Medications are stored/ locked in the office inside a locked metal cabinet. Records for staff and clients are locked inside the office. Facility provides nutritious snacks between meals. Clients are accorded dignity in personal relationships with staff and others. Clients live in a safe, healthy, comfortable facility and are treated with respect. Clients can contact the Licensing Agency or Foster Care Ombudsman person in confidence without threats or punishment for making complaints. Clients attend school, extracurricular, cultural, and personal enrichment activities. Facility records; client cash resources, personal property, and valuables forms are in their file. Client's records contain authorization for emergency medical care signed by each child's authorized representative. Client's records contain original needs and services plan signed by each child and their authorized representative. Overall facility was clean and in good condition. There were no deficiencies cited at the time of the visit.

Licensing Program Analyst Sethany Yem conducted a case management inspection on 4/25/24 at 11:28am based on the number of relevant law enforcement contacts reported by the facility, pursuant to Health and Safety Code section 1538.7. During this inspection, 5 out of Direct Care Staff and 6 out of 6 youth files were reviewed. 2 out of Direct Care Staff and 2 out of 6 youth were interviewed. (See the Confidential Names List, LIC 811, 4/25/24). The Plan of Operation including policies and procedures were reviewed. Minutes from the board of directors' meetings related to the facility's incidents involving contact with law enforcement were reviewed. Based on the analysis of the confidential interviews and youth file review including the needs and service assessments, youth case plans, quarterly assessments, and crisis intervention plans, the licensee uses trauma-informed and evidence-based de-escalation and intervention techniques when staff is responding to the behavior of a youth residing in the facility. Interviews with youth and staff indicate the licensee prohibits calls or threats to call law enforcement as a form of discipline. LPA Yem observed documentation of completed training on policies and procedures on when and how to involve law enforcement in response to an incident. Training records show staff have been trained on Emergency Intervention as required. The licensee is contacting law enforcement in accordance to their Emergency Intervention Plan when there is an immediate risk of serious harm to a child or others. There are no deficiencies cited at this time. A copy of this report was discussed and provided to Interim Administrator Skye Hall.

Licensing Program Analyst Connie Jones-Steward visited the facility to conduct a follow-up of special incident report #1372044. Per Mr. Barnett, he picked up C1 from Los Padrinos on 07/22/25. Mr. Barnett asked Los Padrinos if the client was on medication and was told no. However, during an assessment with the Head of Service, C1 mentioned that he was on ADHD medication while he was at home but while at Los Padrinos, for a month, he was without his medication. C1 then met with the psychiatrist who issued a JV 220 on 08/01/25. However the pharmacy would not fill it because C1's father had just picked up the same medications. The father dropped off the medication that C1 had been taking at home on 08/03/25. However since it was not in a bubble pack, staff could not be sure that it was the correct medication or had not been tampered with. C1 was discharged back to Los Padrinos on 08/05/25. He never received his medication while at Dimondale #9. LPA received a copy of the JV 220(A). LPA asked for copies, the discharge papers from Los Padrinos, any CFT notes and any communication records between Dimondale 9 and the pharmacy.

Licensing Program Analyst Connie Jones-Steward met with Ms. Elisha Chapman to discuss Special Incident Report #1408028 which reported that on Sept. 20 and Sept 21, 2025, S1 and S2 failed to give C1 his morning psychotropic and anti-seizure medication because they thought they were to be given "as needed". LPA reviewed the medication book and found that medication #2, which is a psychotropic, was marked as not psychotropic in error. Ms. Chapman provided a sign in sheet showing that S1, S2 and eight others attended a 1.5 hour training on medication handling expectations on 09/22/2025. The facility was cited under Title 22 80070(f) Client Records and 87075(c) Health Related Services.
